children.translated_text:
In the treatise of instructions on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
composed by <s>Ācārya Haribhadra</s>:
The <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāravṛtti Sphuṭārthā</s> (Commentary on the Ornament of Clear Realization: The Clear Meaning)
First chapter: On <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects)

Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!
Auspicious invocation.
To the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, for the purpose of fully elucidating
the <s>kārikās</s> (verses) of its ornament, this commentary is composed—homage to her! (Abhis 0.1)
By the noble <s>Asaṅga</s>, the protector, through his association with the world's non-attachment,
having heard it from the lord <s>Ajita</s> [<s>Maitreya</s>], that great treatise was organized. (Abhis 0.2)
The kinsman devoted to the welfare of the world, <s>Vasubandhu</s>, relying on his own insight
and what is to be known internally, then composed its commentary. (Abhis 0.3)
The renowned one counted among the noble ones, <s>Vimuktisena</s>,

children.text: akṛtāmiva tāṃ draṣṭvā cakre 'nyāṃ madhyayā dhiyā // Abhis_0.4 //
children.translated_text: seeing that [commentary] as if it had not been made, composed another with middling intelligence. (Abhis 0.4)
Then <s>Vimuktisena</s>, even though he had not obtained all the treatises,
and was established on the stage of faith, composed his commentary by his own discernment. (Abhis 0.5)
Though thus expounded by the best of scholars, some deficiency is observed;
in this [present work] everything is well-accomplished—a cause of great wonder. (Abhis 0.6)
This path is very difficult to obtain, profound, and meaningful,
well-examined by the learned, and obtained through the compassion of the <s>Buddhas</s>. (Abhis 0.7)
This is in no way within my domain, yet I dare [to attempt it],
being favorably disposed to the method of merit, with the wish to benefit myself and others. (Abhis 0.8)

children.text: āryamaitreyaḥ sadācārānuvṛttimātmanaḥ prakhyāpayan svapratisaṃvijjñānena prajñāpāramitāviṣayakaḥ prasāda eva sarvaśreyaḥ prāptipradhānaheturityavadhṛtya paraṃ niratiśayānantaguṇaratnākarabhagavatyāṃ pravartayituṃ prasādotpādanāya tāvadādau yathāguṇābhidhānapuraḥsuraṃ jananīṃ namaskurvannāha -
children.translated_text: The noble <s>Maitreya</s>, proclaiming his following of proper conduct, having determined through his own experiential knowledge that faith (<s>prasāda</s>) in the subject of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the principal cause for the attainment of all welfare, [and wishing] to generate faith in the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (the Noble Lady) who is the ocean of immeasurable, unsurpassed, infinite quality-jewels—first, paying homage to the Mother with a description of her qualities, he says:
She who, through knowledge of all [things] (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), leads to peace the <s>śrāvakas</s> who desire tranquility;
she who, through knowledge of paths (<s>mārgajñatā</s>), fulfills the welfare of the world for those who act for the world's benefit;

children.text: sarvākāramidaṃ vadanti munayo viśvaṃ yayā saṃgatās
children.translated_text: she whom the sages, connected with whom, declare all this universe in all its aspects;

children.text: tasyai śrāvakabodhisattvagaṇino buddhasya mātre namaḥ // Abhis_1.1//
children.translated_text: to her, the Mother of the <s>Buddha</s> together with his retinue of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>—homage! (Abhis 1.1)

children.text: anayā kārikayā asyāḥ atiśayamāhātmyavattvam amihitam / tacchrutvā tāvacchraddhānusāriṇaḥ asyāṃ niḥsaṃśayamacireṇa śraddhāmutpādayanti / dharmānusāriṇo 'pi ekānekasvabhāvaviyuktatvādityādipramāṇena anutpannavastumārgākāraparijñānakārikārthalakṣaṇajananyāṃ bādhām adṛṣṭvā trisarvajñatāsvarūpatrayātmikā buddhādinirmātrī prajñāpāramitāvaśyameva sambhavinītyavadhṛtya tasyāṃ prasādamutpādayanti / tasyāṃ prasādena tadguṇābhilāṣiṇaḥ ubhayavidhā api pudgalāḥ tattadāśritapravacanadhāraṇādyarthaṃ sarvathā atyantamādriyante / tataḥ śrutamayādijñānotpādakrameṇa suśreyo 'dhigatāḥbhavanti / ata eva bhagavatyāṃ pradāsa eva sarvaśreyo 'dhigamahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: By this verse, her possession of surpassing greatness is indicated. Upon hearing this, those who follow faith will quickly and without doubt generate faith in her. Those who follow the <s>Dharma</s> too—since [she] is devoid of single or multiple self-nature, etc.—seeing no contradiction in the Mother characterized by the meaning of the <s>kārikās</s> that ascertain the aspect of the path regarding unproduced things, and having determined that the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, of the nature of the three <s>sarvajñatās</s> (omnisciences), the producer of <s>Buddhas</s> and others, is certainly possible, generate faith in her. Through faith in her, both types of persons, aspiring to her qualities, make every effort for the purpose of retaining the respective discourses and so forth. Then, through the sequence of generating <s>śrutamayī</s> (hearing-based) and other wisdoms, they attain the highest good. Therefore, faith in the <s>Bhagavatī</s> is the very cause of attaining all welfare.

children.text: tatra tisṛbhiḥ sarvajñatābhiraṣṭāvarthāḥ saṅgṛhītā bhavanti / tābhiśca vakṣamāṇavidhinā sarvārthāḥ sampatsyanta iti manasi nidhāya trisarvajñatābhiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ stauti / śrāvakaḥ, tatpakṣanikṣiptaḥ kiñcidvimokṣādhikaḥ ekakrama nirdiṣṭaḥ pratyekabuddhaśca nirvāṇabhilāṣiṇau, tayo anutpannasarvavastujñatayā sopadhinirupadhilakṣaṇadvividhanirvāṇaprāpikā yā, yāvatsaṃsāraṃ jagaddhitakṛtāṃ bodhisattvānāmanutpannasarvamārgajñatayā sarvalokārthasampādikā yā, anutpannasarvākārajñatayā yayā saṅgatāḥ saṃyatakāyāḥ pradhānayogīśvarā buddhāḥ sarvathā caritapratipakṣasarvadharmacakrān pravartayanti / tasyai śrāvakādiparivṛtabuddhānāmutpāyitryai mātre namaḥ / evaṃ namaskārastutipūvakeṇābhisamayālaṅkāraśāstreṇa vastupratipakṣākāreṣu kasmiṃścidekasmin (pakṣe) saṃgṛhīte, prathamapakṣe tāvattadarthapariśramavaiyarthyam / tathā hi na hi tadasti iha prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vastujātaṃ yanna lakṣaṇaśāstreṣu uktapūrvam / dvitīye vyavadānavastu (mātra) saṅgrahāt sāṃkleśikavastvasaṃgrahācca na jñāyate kasyāyaṃ pratipakṣa iti / tṛtīte nirvastukākāramātrasaṃgrahādarthādhigamaśūnyādiha kiñcidapi noktamiti vyartha eva (śāstraracanāyāsaḥ) iti nāpare śaṅkiṣyante kim iti cet? tannaḥ, yato hi yathākramaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānuttarabuddhānāṃ trisarvajñatāyāṃ samastābhisamayānāṃ saṃgrahaṇena pakṣatrayasyāpi saṃgṛhītatvāt /
children.translated_text: Therein, by means of the three <s>sarvajñatās</s>, eight topics are encompassed. And by those, all meanings will be accomplished in the manner to be explained—having placed this in mind, he praises the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by means of the three <s>sarvajñatās</s>. The <s>śrāvakas</s>, with the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> subsumed in their class—being somewhat superior in liberation, mentioned in one sequence—both desire <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Through knowledge of all unproduced things (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), she leads them to the twofold <s>nirvāṇa</s> characterized by with-remainder and without-remainder. Through knowledge of all unproduced paths (<s>mārgajñatā</s>), she fulfills the welfare of all the world for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who act for the world's benefit as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> endures. Through knowledge of all unproduced aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), the <s>Buddhas</s>—those with controlled bodies, supreme lords of yogins—connected with her, turn the <s>Dharmacakras</s> of all [types of] <s>dharmas</s> as antidotes in all ways. To her, the Mother, the genetrix of <s>Buddhas</s> together with their retinue of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others—homage! Thus, by this treatise of the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, preceded by homage and praise, when [objects], antidotes, and aspects are encompassed in any one position: In the first position, the effort regarding those topics would be fruitless—for there is nothing in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that has not been stated previously in the treatises on characteristics. In the second, since only purification-entities are encompassed and affliction-entities are not, it is not known what this is the antidote to. In the third, since only aspects without real entities are encompassed, and it is devoid of the attainment of meaning—nothing at all is stated here, so the effort of composing the treatise would be useless. Lest others raise such doubts—no, [we say], because by encompassing all <s>abhisamayas</s> (clear realizations) in the three <s>sarvajñatās</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and unsurpassed <s>Buddhas</s> respectively, all three positions are encompassed.

children.text: yathā madhyamajinajananyāṃ - "subhūte śrāvakapratyekabuddhayoḥ sarvajñatā, bodhisattvānāṃ mārgajñatā, tathāgatārhatsamyaksambuddhānāṃ sarvākārajñatā / bhagavan kimarthaṃ sarvajñatā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayoḥ? subhūte sarve hi yāvanto bāhyābhyantaradharmāḥ, tāvata eva śrāvakapratyekabuddhā jānanti, na tu mārgeṇa, nāpi sarvākāreṇa, ataḥ sarvajñatā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayoriti / bhagavan, kimarthaṃ mārgajñatā bodhisattvānām? subhūte bodhisattvaiḥ, yaṃ śrāvakasya mārgaḥ, yāḥ pratyekabuddhasya mārgaḥ, yo buddhasya mārgaḥ sarve mārgā utpādyante jñāyante ca / te 'pi paripūryante, teṣāṃ mārgāṇāṃ kriyāpi kriyate / na yāvat praṇidhānaparisamāptiḥ, sattvaparipākaḥ, buddhakṣetrapariśuddhirvā kriyate, na tāvatteṣāṃ samyagbhūtāntasākṣātkāraḥ, ataḥ mārgajñatā bodhisattvānām / bhagavan, kimarthaṃ sarvākārajñatā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya? subhūte, yena ākāreṇa, yena liṅgena, yena nimittena prakhyātā dharmāḥ, tamākāraṃ talliṅgaṃ tannimittaṃ tathāgatā avagacchanti, ataḥ tathāgatasya arhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya sarvākārajñateti / "evaṃ saṃkṣiptāyāmapi (jinajananyāṃ) - "śrāvakabhūmāvapi śikṣitukāmenāpi" ityādikamāha / vistṛtāyāmapi vistareṇābhihitam /
children.translated_text: As in the Middle Mother [the medium-length <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]: '<s>Subhūti</s>, <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all) pertains to <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) pertains to <s>bodhisattvas</s>; <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) pertains to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones. <s>Bhagavān</s>, why is <s>sarvajñatā</s> attributed to <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>? <s>Subhūti</s>, all external and internal <s>dharmas</s> that there are—those <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> know, but not through paths, nor in all aspects; therefore <s>sarvajñatā</s> pertains to <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. <s>Bhagavān</s>, why is <s>mārgajñatā</s> attributed to <s>bodhisattvas</s>? <s>Subhūti</s>, by <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all paths—what is the path of the <s>śrāvaka</s>, what is the path of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, what is the path of the <s>Buddha</s>—are produced and known. They are also fulfilled, and the work of those paths is also carried out. But as long as the fulfillment of their vows, the maturing of beings, and the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields are not accomplished, they do not directly realize the ultimate; therefore <s>mārgajñatā</s> pertains to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. <s>Bhagavān</s>, why is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> attributed to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one? <s>Subhūti</s>, by whatever aspect, mark, or sign <s>dharmas</s> are made known—that aspect, that mark, that sign the <s>Tathāgatas</s> comprehend; therefore <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> pertains to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one.' Thus in the abbreviated [Mother] too: 'Even by one wishing to train in the <s>śrāvaka</s> stage...' and so forth is stated. In the extended [Mother] too, it is stated at length.

children.text: tatra sarvajñatā hi rūpādidharmānityatādyadhiṣṭhānā ātmamohaprahāṇaphalā; mārgajñatā sarvayānaniryāṇā tattvāsākṣātkārādhiṣṭhānā asaṃgṛhītasattvasaṃgrahādiphalāḥ; sarvākārajñatā sarvadharmānutpādādhiṣṭhānā ākāśadhātuparyantāvicchinnasattvārthaphalā bhūtāntādhigamavāsanāpratisandhiprahāṇātmikā /
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>sarvajñatā</s> is based on [the knowledge of] impermanence and such [characteristics] of <s>dharmas</s> like form and the rest, and its fruit is the abandonment of self-delusion. <s>Mārgajñatā</s> is the going-forth of all vehicles, is based on the direct realization of reality, and its fruits are the gathering-in of ungathered beings and the like. <s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> is based on the non-production of all <s>dharmas</s>, its fruit is the uninterrupted welfare of beings extending to the limit of the space-realm, and its essence is the abandonment of the latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) and [karmic] connections to the realization of the ultimate.
Thus, by encompassing all things, antidotes, and aspects in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, a complete exposition of all <s>abhisamayas</s> (clear realizations) has been made—this is established.
The purpose of composing the treatise:

children.text: mandadhījanānāṃ tu vistṛtamadhmasaṃkṣiptāsu bhagavatīṣu (saṃkṣiptamadhyavistṛta) rucisampannasattvahitecchayā karuṇāmayena tattajjinajananyāṃ sakalaprajñāpāramitārthāṣṭābhisamayakramo deśita eva, bhagavata āryājitajinasya tannidarśane kiṃ prayojanamitiśaṅkānirākaraṇārthasandehotpādanena pravṛttyaṅgaṃ svīyaśāstrābhidheyaprayojanaprayojanaprayojanāntarbhūtasambandhāṃśca pradarśayannāha -
children.translated_text: For those of dull intelligence, however—with compassion, desiring the welfare of beings endowed with interest in the brief, medium, and extensive [versions of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>]—[<s>Maitreya</s>] considers: the sequence of the eight <s>abhisamayas</s> encompassing the complete meaning of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has indeed been taught by the compassionate one in each Mother (<s>Jinajananyā</s>). What then is the purpose of the noble, invincible son of the <s>Jinas</s> [<s>Maitreya</s>] showing [this]? Removing this doubt by generating the motive for engagement, and demonstrating the connection which is included within the subject matter, purpose, and ultimate purpose of his own treatise, he says:
The path of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> that was taught here by the Teacher—
may the wise examine it, untasted by others. (Abhis 1.2)
Placing the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s> in memory, the tenfold practice of <s>Dharma</s>—
that they may easily comprehend it: this is the purpose of composition. (Abhis 1.3)

children.text: iti / sarvākārajñataiva hi buddhatvamārga iti sarveṣāmabhisamayānāmupalakṣaṇatvāttasyāmeva tātparyam / triprātihāryaiḥ sakalajanānuśāsakena bhagavatā jinajananītraye yo 'bhidheyo deśitaḥ, sa abhidhānābhidheyopāyopeyapratipattirūpeṇa sambaddhaḥ, bāhyetaravītarāgādibhiḥ sarvadharmanairātmyānabhyastaiḥ śrutamayādiprajñākrameṇānālīḍha iti suvyavasthāpite vāsanāsambhūtasmṛtijñāne bodhicittadānapratipattyācāramaṣṭābhisamayātmakamaśeṣaprajñāpāramitāsūtrārthaṃ samyagādhāya sarvatragadharmadhātvadhigamalakṣaṇapramuditabhūmyādyadhigamakrameṇa sarvākāraṃ sākṣātkuryāditi prayojanaprayojanāya vineyā abhilaṣitaprajñāpāramitārthabodhicittapratipattyādilakṣaṇāni sukhena pratipatsīranniti śāstrārambhaprayojanam //
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> alone is the path to <s>Buddhahood</s>—since it characterizes all <s>abhisamayas</s>, the ultimate intent is on that alone. The subject matter taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who instructs all beings through the three miracles, in the three Mothers, is connected in the form of expression, expressed meaning, means, and goal of attainment. [The path is] untasted by outsiders, <s>vītarāgas</s>, and others who have not practiced the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. Having properly placed in the wisdom-knowledge born of latent impressions—well-established in memory—the entire meaning of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> sūtras, which has the nature of the eight <s>abhisamayas</s> consisting of <s>bodhicitta</s>, giving, practice, and conduct, one should directly realize all aspects through the sequence of realization beginning with the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage, characterized by the realization of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> that pervades all. The trainees, for the purpose of the purpose—that they may easily comprehend the <s>bodhicitta</s>, practice, and other characteristics that constitute the desired meaning of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—this is the purpose of composing the treatise.
The structural arrangement of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>:

children.text: evaṃ sambandhādīn vyāhṛtya vineyānāṃ sukhena pratipattaye supravibhaktasyāpi śāstrārthasya asaṃlulitatvena vyākhyānasaukaryamavalokya pañcadaśabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ samāsavyāsanirdeśena prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kāyikavyavasthāpanamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the connection and the rest, and observing the ease of commentary in presenting the meaning of the treatise well-divided and unconfused for the easy comprehension of trainees, he states the structural arrangement of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through fifteen <s>kārikās</s>, in both summary and detailed exposition:
The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is set forth in eight topics:
<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths), and then <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all); (Abhis 1.4)
full realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>), the culmination (<s>mūrdhaprapta</s>), the sequential [realization] (<s>anupūrvika</s>),
realization in a single instant (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>), and the <s>Dharmakāya</s>—these are the eight. (Abhis 1.5)
Generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>), instructions (<s>avavāda</s>), and the fourfold aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhāṅga</s>),
the basis of practice, and [the teaching] of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>— (Abhis 1.6)
the object of observation, the detailed exposition, the armor (<s>sannāha</s>), setting forth, and action,
the accumulations, and the going-forth—[these constitute] the <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> of the Sage. (Abhis 1.7)
The darkening and such [deeds of <s>Māra</s>], the two paths of disciple and rhinoceros [<s>pratyekabuddha</s>],
the great benefit, the path of seeing with its qualities of this life and the next, (Abhis 1.8)
function, aspiration, and the praised, extolled, and lauded,
the two supreme [practices] of dedication and rejoicing, and the supreme mental attention— (Abhis 1.9)
taking up, purity, and the utter [purity]—this is the path of cultivation;
the knowledge of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>: thus <s>mārgajñatā</s> is declared. (Abhis 1.10)

children.text: prajñayā na bhave sthānaṃ kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through wisdom, no abiding in [conditioned] existence; through compassion, no abiding in peace;
without means, there is remoteness; with means, there is proximity. (Abhis 1.11)
The opposing factors and their antidotes, the practice, and its equality;
the path of seeing of the <s>śrāvakas</s> and others: thus <s>sarvajñatā</s> is desired. (Abhis 1.12)
The aspects, with their applications; qualities and faults, with their characteristics;
the training and the aids to penetration for liberation; the trainee, the irreversible, the assembly; (Abhis 1.13)
equality of existence and peace; the unsurpassed purification of the [<s>Buddha</s>-] field—
this is the full realization of all aspects, together with skillful means. (Abhis 1.14)
Its signs, its increase, its firmness, the abiding of the mind,
and the fourfold antidote to the fourfold conceptualization; (Abhis 1.15)

children.text: pratyekaṃ darśanākhye ca bhāvanākhye ca vartmani /
children.translated_text: in each of the paths called seeing and cultivation,
the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>, together with the wrong approaches; (Abhis 1.16)
the culmination-<s>abhisamaya</s> is threefold; the sequential is tenfold;
realization in a single instant is fourfold by [its] characteristics; (Abhis 1.17)
the <s>Svābhāvika</s> (natural), the <s>Sāmbhogika</s> (enjoyment), and the <s>Nairmāṇika</s> (emanation) [bodies], and the other [<s>kāya</s>]—
the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, together with its function, is declared as fourfold. (Abhis 1.18)

children.text: iti / tatra prathamakārikādvayena aṣṭavastūnāṃ saṃgrahāt samāsanirdeśaḥ, tataḥ trayodaśakārikābhiḥ tasyaivārthaṃ saṃgṛhya vistareṇa vyākhyānaṃ bhavati / itthaṃ saṃkṣepavistarābhyāṃ bhāṣitatvena subhāṣitam / piṇḍārthakārikāṇāmeva śāstrapraṇetrā 'cittotpādaḥ parārthāya' - ityādivakṣyamāṇasakalaśāstreṇa vyākhyāsyamānatvāt tadvyākhyānenaiva vyākhyānaṃ sañcintya vīpsābhayena nātraitā vyākhyātāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, by the first two <s>kārikās</s>, the summary exposition is [given] through the encompassing of the eight topics; then by thirteen <s>kārikās</s>, having gathered the same meaning, the detailed commentary is given. Thus, being stated in both summary and detail, it is well-spoken. Since the <s>kārikās</s> of the summary meaning will themselves be commented upon by the treatise-composer through the entire treatise to follow beginning with '<s>cittotpādaḥ parārthāya</s>' (the generation of mind for the sake of others), [and since] commenting on them through that commentary is being contemplated, out of fear of redundancy these [summary <s>kārikās</s>] are not commented upon here.

<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (Knowledge of All Aspects)
1. <s>Cittotpāda</s> (Generation of the Mind)

children.text: itthaṃ sakalapiṇḍārtha nirdiśya bodhiṃ prāptukāmairbodhisattvaiḥ phalabhūtatvāt sarvākārajñatādhigantavyetyādau sarvākārajñatāsaṃgrahakārikāṃ vyākhyātukāmaḥ sālambanaṃ cittotpādasvarūpamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus indicated all the summary meanings, [the author], wishing to comment on the <s>kārikā</s> encompassing <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>—since it is to be realized as the fruit by <s>bodhisattvas</s> wishing to attain awakening, <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> should be realized first—states the nature of <s>cittotpāda</s> together with its object of observation:
<s>Cittotpāda</s> (the generation of the mind for awakening) is the desire for perfect, complete awakening for the sake of others. (Abhis 1.19 [partial])

children.text: buddho bhūtvā yathābhavyatayā parārthaṃ prati yatnaṃ kuryāmiti parārthāya samyaksambodhyadhikāmatālakṣaṇaḥ praṇidhiprasthānasvabhāvo dvividhaścittotpādaḥ / samyaksambodhikāmatā ca tatprārthanā kuśalo dharmacchandaścaitasikaḥ / viśiṣṭaviṣayapratibhāsamutpadyamānaṃ cittaṃ "cittotpādaḥ" iti kathaṃ sa (caitasikaḥ) cittotpādo bhavet? satyametat / kintu kuśaladharmacchandalakṣaṇāyāṃ prārthanāyāṃ satyāṃ bodhicittamutpadyata iti kāraṇenātra kāryaṃ nirdiṣṭamevaṃ prārthayituḥ bodhisattvasya sarve kuśalā dharmā vṛddhiṃ yāntīti jñāpanāya copacāraḥ samāśrita ityadoṣaḥ / anyaprakāreṇa praṇidhānaṃ prārthanā vā samyaksambodhikāmatā tatsahacaritacittotpādaḥ prārthanayātidiśyate / evañca praṇidhānasahagataṃ taccittamutpadyata iti jñāpanāya vā //
children.translated_text: Having become a <s>Buddha</s>, one would make effort for the benefit of others in accordance with their capacity—such is the twofold <s>cittotpāda</s> (generation of the mind [of awakening]), characterized by the desire for perfect awakening for the benefit of others, whose nature is the resolve (<s>praṇidhi</s>) and practice (<s>prasthāna</s>) [aspects]. The desire for <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening) is a wholesome mental factor (<s>caitasika</s>) of aspiration (<s>dharma-chanda</s>), which is a prayer for that [awakening]. The mind that arises as a reflection of a distinguished object is called '<s>cittotpāda</s>'—how then is it—

children.text: keyaṃ samyaksaṃbodhiḥ? kaśca parārtho yatkāmatātmako yadarthaścittotpāda iti cet? ucyate -
children.translated_text: What is this <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening)? And what is the benefit of others, the desire for which constitutes the <s>cittotpāda</s>? If this is asked, [the author] says—

children.text: samāsavyāsataḥ sā ca yathāsūtraṃ sa cocyate // Abhis_1.19 //
children.translated_text: "It [perfect awakening] is [explained] in brief and in detail, and that [benefit of others] is stated according to the <s>sūtra</s>."

children.text: tisṛṣvapi jinajananīṣu prajñāpāramitāyāṃ dānādau ca deyadāyakapratigrāhakādyanupalabdhiḥ pratipattavyeti jñāpanārthakena; yathābhavyasarvasattvān nirvāṇe, matsariṇaśca dānādau pratiṣṭhāpayitukāmenāsyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratipattavyamitipradarśanapareṇa vacanena (vākyena) sūtrārthāviruddhena samāsavyāsataḥ parārthā samyaksambodhiḥ nirdiṣṭā / itthaṃ 'cittotpādaḥ parārthāya samyaksambodhikāmatā' jñātavyā / sarvākaragranthatātparyārthanirdeśāvasare sarvaṃ kathitaṃ tathāpi bahuvaktavyamāśaṅkya na (atra pradhānataḥ) samullikhitam /
children.translated_text: In all three Mothers of the Conquerors (the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [sūtras]), with a statement intended to convey that one should practice non-apprehension of the gift, giver, recipient, and so forth in giving and the rest; and with a statement aimed at showing that one should practice in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in order to establish all beings according to their capacity in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and to establish even the miserly in giving and the rest—in brief and in detail, in a manner not contradicting the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>—

children.text: evaṃ sālambanaṃ cittotpādasvarūpamabhidhāyedānīṃ tasya dvāviṃśatiprabhedān dvābhyāmantaraślokābhyāmāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus described the nature of <s>cittotpāda</s> with its object-support, [the author] now states its twenty-two varieties in two intervening verses—
"By earth, gold, moon, fire, treasure, jewel-mine, ocean,
Diamond, mountain, medicine, friend, wish-fulfilling gem, sun, song,
King, storehouse, highway, vehicle, spring, water,
Echo, sound, river, cloud—it is of twenty-two kinds."

children.text: chanda-āśaya-adhyāśaya-prayoga-dāna-śīla-kṣānti-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñā-upāya-kauśala-praṇidhāna-bala-jñāna-abhijñā-puṇyajñāna-bodhipakṣānukūladharma-karuṇāvipaśyanā-dhāraṇīpratibhāna-dharmotsava-ekayāna-dharmakāyaiḥ sahagataḥ (cittotpādaḥ) yathākramaṃ pṛthivī-kalyāṇasuvarṇa-śuklapakṣavanacandra-jvalana-mahānidhāna-ratnākara-mahārṇava-vajraparvatarāja-bhaiṣajya-kalyāṇamitra-cintāmaṇi-āditya-dharmamadhurasaṃgīti-mahārāja-koṣṭhāgāra-mahāmārga-yāna prasravaṇodaka-ānandokti-nadīdhārā-meghaiḥ-sadṛśaḥ; sarvaśukladharmapratiṣṭhābhūtatvāt, bodhiparyāntāvikāritvāt, sakalaśukladharmavivṛddhigamanāt, trisarvajñatāvaraṇendhanadāhakatvāt, sarvasattvasaṃtarpaṇāt, guṇaratnānāmāśrayabhāvāt, sarvāniṣṭopanipātairakṣobhyatvāt, saṃpratyayadārḍhyenābhedyatvāt, ālambanavikṣepeṇāniṣkampyatvāt, kleśajñeyāvaraṇavyādhipraśamanāt, sarvāvasthāsu sattvārthāparityāgāt, yathāpraṇidhānaṃ phalasamṛddheḥ, vineyajanasya paripācanāt, vineyāvarjana karadharmadeśakatvāt, avyāhataprabhāvatvena parārthānuṣṭhānāt, bahupuṇyajñānasaṃbhārakośasthānatvāt, sarvāryayātānuyātatvāt, saṃsāranirvāṇānyatarāpātena sukhasaṃvāhanāt, śrutāśrutadharmadhāraṇādakṣayatvāt, mokṣakāmānāṃ vineyānāṃ priyaśrāvaṇāt, asaṃbhinna-ḥ parakāryakriyātvāt, tuṣitabhavanavāsādisandarśanayogyatvāt yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati / ityevaṃ 'bhūhemacandrajvalanaitira' tyādibhiḥ dvāviṃśatiścittotpādā vyākhyātāḥ /
children.translated_text: Accompanied by (1) aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), (2) intention (<s>āśaya</s>), (3) superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>), (4) application (<s>prayoga</s>), (5) giving (<s>dāna</s>), (6) morality (<s>śīla</s>), (7) patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), (8) vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), (9) meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), (10) wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), (11) skillful means (<s>upāya-kauśala</s>), (12) vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), (13) power (<s>bala</s>), (14) knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), (15) superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), (16) merit and knowledge, (17) factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), (18) compassion and insight (<s>karuṇā-vipaśyanā</s>), (19) <s>dhāraṇī</s> and eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>), (20) <s>dharma</s>-festival, (21) one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>), and (22) the <s>Dharmakāya</s>—[the <s>cittotpāda</s>] is respectively [compared to] earth, fine gold, waxing moon, fire—

children.text: tatra prathamāstrayo mṛdumadhyādhimātratayādikarmikabhūmisaṅgṛhītāḥ / tataḥ ekaḥ prathamabhūmipraveśamārgasaṅgṛhītaḥ / tadantaraṃ daśa pramuditādidaśabhūmisaṅgṛhītā darśanabhāvanāmārgagocarāḥ / tataḥ pañca viśeṣamārgasaṅgṛhītāḥ / tadantaraṃ trayaṃ cittotpādāḥ prayogamaulapṛṣṭhadvāreṇa buddhabhūmisaṅgṛhītāḥ / iti cittotpādabhedaḥ ādikarmikabhūmimārabhya yāvad buddhabhūmi saṅgṛhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these, the first three, as weak, middling, and strong, are included in the beginner's stage. Then one [the fourth] is included in the path of entry to the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). After that, ten [the fifth through fourteenth] are included in the ten <s>bhūmis</s> from <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) onward, pertaining to the paths of seeing and cultivation. Then five [the fifteenth through nineteenth] are included in the special path. After that, the three [remaining] <s>cittotpādas</s> are included in the <s>Buddha</s>-stage by means of preparation, principal, and subsequent [aspects]—
2 - The Instruction (<s>Avavāda</s>)

children.text: prasaṅgāgata (cittotpāda)-bhedamabhidhāya utpāditaprathamādibodhicittāya yathākālaṃ bodhisattvāya prārthitārthabodhicittotpādāya tadākṣiptadharmasiddhaye prāptaguṇaparirakṣaṇenābhivṛddhaye copadeśo 'vavāda ityata āha -
children.translated_text: Having described the incidentally arisen divisions [of <s>cittotpāda</s>], the instruction (<s>avavāda</s>) is the teaching for accomplishing the <s>dharmas</s> entailed by [the <s>bodhicitta</s>], and for protecting and increasing the qualities already attained, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the first and subsequent <s>bodhicittas</s> and who has at the proper time generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> for the desired purpose. Therefore [the author] says—
"In practice, in the [four] truths, in the three [jewels] beginning with the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel,
In non-attachment, in non-weariness, in the comprehensive practice,
In the five eyes, in the six qualities of superknowledge,
In the path of seeing and in what is called cultivation—the instruction is tenfold."

children.text: yathoktaprabhedabodhicittapratipattau saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyānatikrameṇa śrāvakādyasādhāraṇatayā'nupalambhayogena vartanamiti śikṣaṇaṃ pratipattyavavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The instruction on practice is: training in the practice of the <s>bodhicitta</s> of the varieties stated above, without transgressing conventional and ultimate truth, in a manner uncommon to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

children.text: duḥkhe phalabhūtarūpādiśūnyatāprajñāpāramitayostathatārūpatvādaikātmyamiti / samudaye śūnyatāhetubhūtarūpādyoravyatiriktatvena rūpādirna samudayanirodhasaṃkleśavyavadānadharmī iti / nirodhe śūnyatāyāmutpādanirodhasaṃkleśavyavadānahānivṛddhyādirahitāyānna rūpaṃ yāvannāvidyotpādo nāvidyānirodho na buddho bodhiriti / mārge dānādipāramitābhirātmano 'dhyātmaśūnyatādīnāṃ bahirdhāśūnyatādibhiḥ pūrvāntāparāntayośca parasparaṃ na yuktāyuktatvena pratipattirityupadeśaḥ satyāvavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Regarding suffering: since form and the rest—which are the result—are empty, and since <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and [emptiness] have the same nature as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), they are identical. Regarding the origin: since form and the rest, which are the cause, are inseparable from emptiness, form and the rest are not the basis of origination, cessation, defilement, or purification. Regarding cessation: since emptiness is devoid of arising, cessation, defilement, purification, abandonment, increase, and the like, there is no form, up to no arising of ignorance, no cessation of ignorance, no <s>Buddha</s>—

children.text: buddhe buddhabodhyorekatvalakṣaṇatvena buddhakaradharmalakṣaṇasarvākārajñatāyā anupalambhe rūpādyayojanenālambyālambakasamatājñānamiti / dharme trisarvajñatāsaṃgṛhītasamastavastupratipakṣākārasaṅgrahaiḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ saṅgṛhītānāṃ niḥsvabhāvateti / saṃghe buddharatnāntargatatvenārhadvarjyeṣu phalasthapratipannakabhedena saptasu mahāpuruṣeṣu pratyekabuddhena sahāṣṭāsu mṛdvindriyādibhedena viṃśatisaṃkhyāvacchinneṣyāryāvaivarttikabodhisattvaśaikṣeṣvanutpādatayā pravṛttirityupadeśo ratnatrayāvavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Regarding the <s>Buddha</s>: since <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Bodhi</s> are characterized as one, through the non-apprehension of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects)—which is the characteristic of <s>Buddha</s>-making <s>dharmas</s>—by not linking it with form and the rest, the knowledge is the equality of the apprehended and the apprehender. Regarding the <s>Dharma</s>: by the comprehensive groupings of all aspects of objects and antidotes subsumed under the three types of omniscience, all <s>dharmas</s> that are subsumed are without own-nature. Regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>: since [it is] included within the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel, excluding the <s>Arhat</s>, concerning the stages of fruition—

children.text: ārabdhavīryatayā yathoktārthānuṣṭhānaṃ prati kāyādisukhallikatvena kasyacidabhiniveśaḥ syādityasaktau kāyādīnāmasvabhāvatayā deśanāvavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since one who has begun vigor might have attachment to bodily comfort and the like regarding the practice of the stated meanings, the instruction on non-attachment is the teaching that body and the rest are without own-nature.

children.text: ciratarakālābhyāsenāpi samīhitārthāniṣpattāvuttrasanajātīyasya parikhedaḥ syādityapariśrāntau rūpāderyāvat samyaksambodheramananatayā deśanāvavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since even after prolonged practice one might become disheartened at the non-accomplishment of the desired goal, generating something like terror, the instruction on non-weariness is the teaching that form and the rest, up to <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, are without ideation.

children.text: daśadigavasthitabuddhādibhyaḥ pratyarthaṃ mārgopadeśe gṛhyamāṇe cittāvalīnatā syāditi pratipatsamparigrahe dharmāṇāṃ prakṛtyajātatvena śikṣaṇamavavādaḥ / māṃsavaipākikadivyaprajñādharmabuddhacakṣuṣāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ pratiniyatavastusarvasattvacyutyupapattisarvadharmāvikalpānāṃ sarvāryapudgalādhigamasarvākārasarvadharmābhisambodhaviṣayāṇāṃ tathatayaikatvena pratipattiriti śikṣaṇaṃ pañcacakṣuravavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since when the path-instruction is being received from <s>Buddhas</s> and others established in the ten directions for their respective purposes, there might be absorption of the mind-continuum, the instruction on comprehensive practice is the teaching that <s>dharmas</s> are unoriginated by nature. Regarding the five eyes—the flesh eye, the divine eye, the <s>prajñā</s> eye, the <s>dharma</s> eye, and the <s>Buddha</s> eye—which respectively [cognize] their designated objects, the passing away and rebirth of all beings, non-conceptualization of all <s>dharmas</s>, the attainments of all noble persons—

children.text: ṛddhidivyaśrotraparacittajñānapūrvanivāsānusmṛtyabhisaṃskārikadivyacakṣurāsravakṣayajñānābhijñānāṃ pṛthivīkampanādisarvalokadhātusthasūkṣmataraśabdaśravaṇasarāgādiparacittaparijñānasvapara-pūrvānekajātyanusmaraṇasarvarūpadarśanakleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇakāritrāṇāmādiśāntatvenāvabodha iti deśanā ṣaḍabhijñāvavādaḥ / catuḥsatyasaṅgṛhītaṣoḍaśakṣaṇasvabhāvaṃ darśanamārgaṃ dharmānvayajñānakṣāntijñānātmakaṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvabodhena māyākāra iva sarvatrānabhiniviṣṭamūrtistatprahātavyavastupratipakṣatvena yogī vibhāvayatīti deśanā darśanamārgāvavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Regarding the six superknowledges—<s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power), divine hearing, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of former lives, the conditioned divine eye, and knowledge of the destruction of the defilements—which [accomplish] respectively: earthquake and the like, hearing the subtlest sounds in all world-realms, knowing the minds of others as passionate and so forth, remembering one's own and others' many former births, seeing all forms, and eliminating the obscurations of defilements and the knowable—the teaching is that these are essentially quiescent. The teaching on the six superknowledges—

children.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtayorekarūpatvena parasparamaśakyavyatirekaprajñaptivad yathoktadarśanamārgasaṃmukhīkṛtavastvavyatirekālambanād darśanabhāvanayorapṛthagbhāva iti na lākṣaṇikaṃ bhāvanāmārgavyavasthānam, atha ca sa tatprahātavyavastupratipakṣatvena vibhāvyate pratītyasamutpādadharmatayeti deśanā bhāvanāmārgāvavāda ityevaṃ bodhicittatadākṣitpadharmasvabhāvaprajñāpāramitāyāṃ yā pratipattiranupalambhākārā, tasyā yadālambanaṃ catvāryasatyāni, ya āśrayastrīṇi śaraṇāni, yo viśeṣagamanaheturasaktiḥ, yo 'vyāvṛttigamanahetupariśrāntiḥ, yo 'nanyayānagamanahetuḥ pratipatsaṃparigrahaḥ, yo 'parapratyagāmitvahetuḥ pañca cakṣūṃṣiḥ, yaḥ sarvākārajñatāparipūrihetuḥ ṣaḍabhijñāḥ, yau niṣṭhāhetū darśanabhāvanāmārgau, tatsarvamavavādaprakaraṇe nirdiṣṭametāvataiva sarvo 'rthaḥ sampanna iti daśavidho 'vavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the conditioned and the unconditioned are of one nature and cannot be designated as separate from each other—just as the path of seeing, being face-to-face with objects inseparable from [what is seen], makes the path of seeing and cultivation inseparable—there is no characteristic establishment of the path of cultivation [as separate]. Yet it is delineated as the antidote to the objects to be abandoned by it, through its nature as dependent origination. This is the teaching on the path of cultivation—
In the section on the <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel, [the author] states two intervening verses for its easy comprehension—
"Those of soft and sharp faculties: the faith-follower and the view-attainer; the clan-to-clan;
The one-interval, the one born [in a higher realm], the going-to-<s>Akaniṣṭha</s>;
The three who leap; the supreme of the summit of existence; the destroyer of form-realm desire;
The one who attains peace in this very life; the body-witness; and the solitary realizer—[these are] twenty."

children.text: vakṣyamāṇamārgajñatāsaṅgṛhītaṣoḍaśakṣaṇadarśanamārgam āśritya śraddhādharmānusāribhedena prathamaphalapratipannako dvividhaḥ / tataḥ srota āpannaḥ / tato devamanuṣyakulaṃkulatvena sa evānyo dvividhaḥ / tato dvitīyaphalapratipannako mṛdutīkṣṇendriya evaikaḥ śraddhādṛṣṭiprāptaḥ / tataḥ sakṛdāgāmī / tataḥ sa ekavīciko 'paraḥ / tataṃ tṛtīyaphalapratipannakaḥ pūrvavacchaddhādṛṣṭiprāptaḥ / tataḥ anāgāmī antarābhave upapadya, abhisaṃskāre anabhisaṃskāre ca parinirvāyīti caturdhā / tataṃ evākaniṣṭhagaḥ plutārdhaplutasarvasthānacyutatvenordhvāvakrāntāparastrividhaḥ / tataḥ sa eva bhavāgragastu rūpavītarāgo dṛṣṭadharmaśamaḥ kāyasākṣīti aparo dvividhaḥ / tato 'rhattvaphalapratipannakaḥ / tataḥ pratyekabuddha iti viṃśatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Based on the sixteen-moment path of seeing included in the <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path) to be explained, the one who has entered the first fruit is of two kinds, as faith-follower and <s>dharma</s>-follower. Then [comes] the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>). Then that same [stream-enterer] is of two kinds as one who goes from divine to human clans and vice versa. Then the one who has entered the second fruit is one, of soft or sharp faculties, as faith-attainer or view-attainer. Then the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmī</s>). Then—
3 - The Penetration Factors (<s>Nirvedhāṅga</s>)
For the beginner who has received instruction as described, the arising of the penetration factors [is now explained]—the author states the penetration factors—
"From the standpoint of the object-support, the aspect, the cause, and the comprehension,
Of those noble ones who respectively have the conjunction of four types of conceptualization—
Compared to the <s>Śrāvakas</s> together with the solitary realizers, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Protector [has]
The distinction of the weak, middling, and strong <s>ūṣma</s> (heat) and the rest."

children.text: bodhisattvānāṃ śrutādiprakarṣaprāptamokṣabhāgīyaśraddhādilakṣaṇakuśalamūlādūrdhvaṃ catuḥsatyaprativedhānukūlāni ca caturnirvedhabhāgīyāni laukikabhāvanāmayāni ūṣmaprāpta iti kuśalamūlam, tato mūrdhaprāptaḥ, tataḥ kṣāntiprāptaḥ, tato 'gradharma iti mṛdvādikrameṇa utpādo 'thavā bodhisattvasambaddhamṛdvindriyādipudgalabhedena vakṣyamāṇamṛdumadhyādhimātrālambanaviśiṣṭavastvātmakacatuḥsatyālambanadharmadarśana-pratipakṣatvenānabhiniveśādyākāraviśeṣāt yānatrayādhigamahetutvaviśeṣādupāyakauśalakalyāṇamitralakṣaṇasamparigrahād darśanabhāvanāmārgābhyāṃ prahātavyā grāhyagrāhakacaturvikalpāḥ vakṣamāṇanayasambandhenotpannāḥ śrāvakādīnāmūṣmādibhyo viśiṣṭāḥ / teṣāmūṣmādikuśalamūlaṃ nyāye rūpaṇādilakṣaṇavastvātmakacatuḥsatyālambanamātmadarśanapratipakṣatvenānityādyākārapratipannaṃ svayānādhigamahetubhūtaṃ samparigraharahitaṃ, caturvidho vikalpo 'saṃsṛṣṭo bhavatīti vyavasthāpanāt / bodhisattvānāṃ nirvedhabhāgīyāni upāyakauśalabalena kvacit hetunā, kvacit phalena, kvacit svarūpatayā, kvacid dharmatākāreṇa yathābhavyatayā catuḥsatyavastvālambanamiti veditavyam / saṃkṣiptavyākhyāmātraṃ vaktukāmena na prapañcitam / yata idameva vyavasthāpanaṃ hyato 'nyayānamāśritya kutrāpi dūṣaṇaṃ nābhidhātavyam /
children.translated_text: Above the wholesome roots characterized by faith and the rest—the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> (conducive to liberation) [qualities] attained through the excellence of learning and the rest by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—the four <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) [factors], which are conducive to penetrating the four truths and are of the nature of worldly cultivation, are: the wholesome root called <s>ūṣma-prāpta</s> (attainment of heat), then <s>mūrdha-prāpta</s> (attainment of the summit), then <s>kṣānti-prāpta</s> (attainment of patience), then <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma)—arising in the order of weak and so forth; or alternatively, the weak and so on connected with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—

children.text: ālambanākārayoḥ kā viśeṣatā ityata ālambanākārau saptamiḥ antaraślokairāha -
children.translated_text: What is the distinction regarding object-support and aspect? Therefore [the author] states the object-support and aspect in seven intervening verses—
"The object-support is impermanence and the rest, based on the [four] truths; its aspect
Is the negation of attachment and the rest; its cause is for the attainment of the three vehicles."
"Form and the rest, increase and decrease, establishment and standing, designation and the inexpressible—"

children.text: tatra mṛduna anityādiṣoḍaśākāraṃ duḥkhādicatuḥsatyādhāramālambanam / duḥkhādisatyābhiniveśālambanādīnāṃ niṣedhaḥ tadākṛtiḥ / yānatrayādhigamaprāptaye hetubhāvaḥ sarveṣāmevoṣmādīnāṃ veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, for the weak [heat]: the object-support is the sixteen aspects such as impermanence, based on the four truths beginning with suffering. The negation of objects such as attachment to the truths of suffering and the rest is its aspect. The causal nature for the attainment of realization of the three vehicles should be understood for all of heat and the rest.

children.text: adhimuktinā tattvamanaskāreṇa ca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ rūpādīnāṃ pratipatteḥ niṣedhasya cānupalambhanaṃ na samanudarśanamiti madhyasyālambanam /
children.translated_text: Through conviction and true mental engagement, the non-perception—not seeing—of the negation of the practice of form and the rest respectively, is the object-support of the middling [heat].
Through the absence of all designations, the absence of the characteristics of occurrence that are similar and dissimilar to the continuum is the aspect.

children.text: rūpamārabhya yāvadbuddha iti sarvadharmasāṅketiko vyāvahārikadharma ityadhimātrasyālambanam / kuśalādidharmatā na kenacid vacanīyā ityākṛtiḥ / ityālambanākāravannirvikalpajñānāgneḥ pūrvarūpatvādūṣmagataṃ trividham /
children.translated_text: From form up to <s>Buddha</s>—the conventional, transactional <s>dharma</s> that is the sign-system of all <s>dharmas</s>—is the object-support of the strong [heat]. The nature of being wholesome and so forth is not to be expressed by anyone—this is the aspect. Thus, like the object-support and aspect, since [heat] is the preliminary form of the fire of non-conceptual knowledge, the heat stage is threefold.
"The establishment of form and the rest; their lack of own-nature through being of that nature;"
"The mutual own-nature-ness of those two; the non-establishment of impermanence and the rest regarding that;"
"The emptiness of those as being of that nature; the mutual naturelessness of these two;"
"The non-grasping of <s>dharmas</s>; the non-examination of their signs;"
"And the examination of <s>prajñā</s>—all through non-apprehension."

children.text: iti / atra svabhāvaśūnyatayā rūpādīnāṃ rūpādisvabhāvenāpagatasvabhāvatā, tataḥ rūpādyasthānamiti mṛduna ālambanam / paramārthena rūpādisarvadharmaśūnyatayoḥ parasparamekaṃ rūpamiti śūnyatāyāmanityatvādīnāmabhāvena rūpādau na nityānityādibhiḥ sthānamityākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through emptiness of own-nature, the own-nature of form and the rest has departed in terms of the nature of form and the rest; therefore, the non-establishment of form and the rest is the object-support of the weak [summit]. Since ultimately form and the rest and emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> are mutually one form, through the non-existence of impermanence and the rest in emptiness, there is no establishment of the permanent, impermanent, and so forth in form and the rest—this is the aspect.

children.text: dharmadhāturūpatayānityādiśūnyatānāṃ svaniḥsvabhāvatvādanityādiśūnyatānāṃ parasparamaikātmyamiti madhyasyālambanam / yaṃ svabhāvapratiṣedhenāsvīkāro rūpādīnāṃ sa ākāra iti /
children.translated_text: Since the emptiness of impermanence and the rest, being the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, is without own-nature, the identity of the emptiness of impermanence and the rest with each other is the object-support of the middling [summit]. The non-acceptance of form and the rest through the negation of own-nature is the aspect.

children.text: svabhāvābhāvatayaiva nīlādinimittādarśanaṃ rūpādīnāmiti adhimātrasyālambanam / samyagdharmapravicayatvena prajñāyāḥ sarvavastuno 'nupalambhatayā nirūpaṇamityākāraḥ / ityālambanākāravaccalakuśalamūlamūrdhatvānmūrdhagataṃ trividham /
children.translated_text: Through the very absence of own-nature, the non-seeing of signs such as blue and the rest regarding form and the rest is the object-support of the strong [summit]. Since <s>prajñā</s> is the correct analysis of <s>dharmas</s>, the examination of all objects through non-apprehension is the aspect. Thus, like the object-support and aspect, since it is the unstable wholesome root called the summit, the summit stage is threefold.
"The lack of own-nature of form and the rest; the nature of that absence;"
"Its non-origination and non-departure; purity; the signless-ness of that;"
"Non-foundation on that sign; non-conviction; non-conceptualization."

children.text: iti / atra śūnyatā rūpalakṣyalakṣaṇayorekatvenāsvabhāvo rūpādīnāmiti mṛduna ālambanam / ālambakajanaṃ prati abhāvasvabhāvatā rūpādīnāmityākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the characterized and the characteristic of form are one, the lack of own-nature of form and the rest through emptiness is the object-support of the weak [patience]. The nature of being non-existent for the apprehending person with regard to form and the rest is the aspect.

children.text: prakṛtyasvabhāvatvena rūpādīnāmanutpādānirodhāviti(madhyasya) ālambanam / sarvadharmasvarūpāvabodhena kāyādīnāṃ sarvākāraviśuddhirityākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The non-origination and non-cessation of form and the rest through being naturally without own-nature is the object-support of the middling [patience]. The complete purity of body and the rest through the realization of the true nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is the aspect.

children.text: svasāmānyalakṣaṇānupapattyā sarvadharmāṇāmanimittatvamiti adhimātrasyālambanam / prakṛtyaiva rūpādinimittānāmāśrayarahitatvenādhimokṣamanaskārānadhimokṣatattvamanaskārāparijñānamiti ākāraḥ / ityālambanākāravadapāyābhāvenādhimātradharmakṣamaṇāt kṣāntigataṃ trividham /
children.translated_text: The signless-ness of all <s>dharmas</s> through the impossibility of particular and general characteristics is the object-support of the strong [patience]. Through the lack of support for the signs of form and the rest by their very nature, the non-conviction through mental engagement of conviction and the non-comprehension of reality through mental engagement are the aspect. Thus, like the object-support and aspect, since it is called patience for strongly enduring <s>dharmas</s> without falling into bad destinies, the patience stage is threefold.
"The <s>samādhi</s> of that; its function; prediction; the cessation of ideation;"
"The mutual naturelessness of the three; the non-conceptualization of <s>samādhi</s>;"
"Thus the penetration factors, through weak, middling, and strong [degrees]."

children.text: iti / atra sarvadharmāṇāmanutpādasya vīraṃgamādīnāñca samādhirbhāvanīya iti mṛduna ālambanam / svapraṇidhānapuṇyajñānadharmadhātubalenānābhogātsarvalokadhātuṣu yathābhavyatayā samādhervyāpāraḥ pravartata ityākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>samādhi</s> to be cultivated regarding the non-origination of all <s>dharmas</s> and the <s>vīraṃgama</s> and other [concentrations] is the object-support of the weak [supreme <s>dharma</s>]. Through the power of one's own vow, merit, knowledge, and <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the function of <s>samādhi</s> proceeds effortlessly in all world-realms according to the capacity [of beings]—this is the aspect.

children.text: dharmataiṣā samyakpratipannasamādheryogino buddhairvyākaraṇaṃ kriyata iti madhyasyālambanam / sarvavikalpānupapattyā viditasamādhisvarūpasya bodhisattvasyāhaṃ samāhitaṃ ityādijñānaṃ na sambhavatītyākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that <s>Buddhas</s> give predictions to the yogin whose <s>samādhi</s> of correct practice [has matured]—this is the object-support of the middling [supreme <s>dharma</s>]. Since all conceptualization is impossible, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who knows the nature of <s>samādhi</s>, knowledge such as 'I am concentrated' does not arise—this is the aspect.

children.text: dharmatayā samādhibodhisattvaprajñāpāramitārthatrayasya parasparamekaṃ rūpamityadhimātrasyālambanam / sarvadharmāvidyamānatvena samādheravikalpanaṃ paramopāya ityākāraḥ / ityālambanākāravallaukikasarvadharmāgratvādagradharmākhyaṃ trividham /
children.translated_text: Through the nature of things, the three—<s>samādhi</s>, <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and the meaning of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—are mutually of one form: this is the object-support of the strong [supreme <s>dharma</s>]. Since all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent, the non-conceptualization of <s>samādhi</s> is the supreme method—this is the aspect. Thus, like the object-support and aspect, since it is supreme among all worldly <s>dharmas</s>, it is called the supreme <s>dharma</s> and is threefold.

children.text: ālambanamanityādi satyādhāramatiricya ālambanaviśiṣṭākārayoḥ dharmadharmyabhidhāne satyapi ālambanaviśiṣṭākārayoḥ dharmābhidhānena sarvatra ucyamāne ṛte viśiṣṭāntaraparihārāparihārau nānayoḥ kaścit prativiśeṣa iti nyāyāt / athavā kārikācchandānurodhena bhinnābhidhāne 'pi abhiniveśādiniṣedhayuktayoḥ tattvataḥ vidhānapratiṣedharahitatvād duḥkhādisatyāntargatamevālambanamākāraśca kriyete / tathaivāparatrāpi boddhavyam /
children.translated_text: Although the object-support beginning with impermanence is stated as truth-based, and the distinguished object-support and aspect express both <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s>, since wherever the distinguished object-support and aspect are expressed through the expression of <s>dharma</s>, apart from the inclusion and exclusion of particular distinctions, there is no specific difference between these two—this is according to the principle. Alternatively, even when they are stated separately due to metrical constraints in the <s>kārikās</s>, both accompanied by the negation of attachment and the rest—
For a clear understanding of the conjunction with the four types of conceptualization, [the author] states two intervening verses—
"The conceptualization of the graspable is twofold, from the standpoint of the object and its antidote;"

children.text: moharāśyādibhedena pratyekaṃ navadhā tu saḥ // Abhis_1.35 //
children.translated_text: "Each is ninefold through the divisions of the mass of delusion and the rest."

children.text: iti / sāṃkleśikavastvadhiṣṭhānatvena pratipakṣādhiṣṭhānatvena ca prakāradvaye 'vidyāvyavadānaskandhādiprabhedā navadhā /
children.translated_text: In two modes—as based on defiled objects and as based on their antidotes—the divisions of ignorance, purification-aggregates, and the rest are ninefold.
"The grasper is considered twofold, based on substance and designation;"
"Likewise through relying on the aggregates and the rest in the form of an independent self and the rest."

children.text: iti / atra pudgaladravyasatpuruṣaprajñaptisadupalambhatvena dvividho grāhakavikalpo 'pi / svatantrātmaskandhādyupalambhena pratyekaṃ navaprakāro bhavati /
children.translated_text: Here, the conceptualization of the grasper is also twofold, through the apprehension of the person as substantially existent and as conventionally designated. Through the apprehension of an independent self and the aggregates and the rest, each becomes of nine varieties.

Here is the condensed meaning: the conceptualizations of the graspable based on defiled objects are (as follows): ignorance, form and the rest, aggregates, attachment to name-and-form, clinging to the two extremes, ignorance of defilement and purification, non-establishment on the noble path, apprehension, self and the rest, [and] grasping at purity and origination and the rest.

Those based on the antidotes are: the mass [of <s>dharmas</s>], the doors of the <s>āyatanas</s>, the <s>gotra</s> (lineage), origination, emptiness, the meaning of the <s>pāramitās</s>, the path of seeing, the path of cultivation, and the path of no-more-learning—these are the conceptualizations of the graspable.

Those based on a substantially existent person are: independent self, unitary [self], causal [self], the self as seer and the rest, defilement, dispassion, seeing, cultivation, and the one who has accomplished the goal—these are the conceptualizations of the grasper.

Those based on a conventionally designated person are: aggregates, <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, dependent origination, purification, seeing, cultivation, the special [path], and the path of no-more-learning—these are the conceptualizations of the grasper.
Thus the four types of conceptualization are respectively conjoined with the four penetrative factors.

children.text: sambaddhakārikānusāram uktapūrve 'pi samparigrahe tadbalena yathoktaviśeṣo bhavatīti darśanāya tadanantaramantaraślokaḥ -
children.translated_text: Following the connected <s>kārikās</s>, for showing that even regarding the comprehensive practice already stated, its specific distinction arises through its [the penetrative factors'] power, [the author] states an intervening verse immediately after—
"Non-absorption of the mind and the rest; teaching the lack of own-nature and the rest;"
"The abandonment of their opposites—this is the comprehensive practice in every way."

The comprehensive practice (<s>samparigraha</s>) is: a spiritual friend who, through skillful means of non-absorption of the mind, non-terror, and the like, teaches the selflessness of all objects and the rest according to [beings'] dispositions, free from opposing <s>dharmas</s> such as miserliness and the rest.
4 - The Basis of Practice (<s>Pratipattyādhāra</s>)
Since the one who has the penetrative factors as described also has [other factors] such as the path of seeing and the rest, [the author] states the basis of practice—
"Of the sixteen-fold <s>dharma</s> of realization, of the antidote and abandonment,

children.text: tayoḥ paryupayogasya prajñāyāḥ kṛpayā saha // Abhis_1.38 //
children.translated_text: Of the application of those two, of <s>prajñā</s> together with compassion,
Of [the quality] uncommon to the disciple, of the sequence for the benefit of others,
Of knowledge, and of effortless activity—the basis is called the <s>gotra</s> (lineage)."

children.text: tatrādau tāvaccaturvidhalaukikanirvedhabhāgīyānāmutpādādhāraḥ / tato lokottaradarśanabhāvanāmārgayoḥ / tatastadutpattibalena cauraniṣkāsanakapāṭapidhānavat samakālaṃ samastapratipakṣotpādavipakṣanirodhayoḥ / tatastadanupalabdhyā tadutpādanirodhayuktavikalpāpagamasya / tataṃ pūrvapraṇidhānadānādyupāyakauśalyabalena saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhānayoḥ prajñākaruṇayoḥ / tatastadutpattyā śrāvakādyasādhāraṇadharmasya / tato yathāśayamavatāraṇādyabhisandhidvāreṇa yānatrayapratiṣṭhāpanalakṣaṇaparārthānukramasya / tato yāvadāsaṃsāraṃ nirnimittānābhogaparārthajñānasya cādhāraḥ / ayamevānukramaḥ / anenaiva sarva puruṣārthāḥ sampadyante /
children.translated_text: Therein, first: the basis for the arising of the fourfold worldly penetrative factors. Then of the supramundane paths of seeing and cultivation. Then, through the power of their arising—like a thief-expelling bolt simultaneously closing a door—of the arising of the entire antidote and the cessation of the opposing [factors] at the same time. Then, through their non-apprehension, of the disappearance of conceptualizations involving their arising and cessation. Then, through skillful means such as former vows and giving—

children.text: pratipattidharmāvasthāntarabhedena trayodaśavidho bodhisattvo yathoktadharmādhāro dharmadhātusvabhāva eva gotramiti nirdiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is of thirteen varieties through the different stages of the <s>dharmas</s> of practice, has been indicated as having the <s>dharmadhātu</s> itself as its nature—this is the <s>gotra</s>, the basis of the stated <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: yadi dharmadhātorevāryadharmādhigamāya hetutvāttadātmako bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtisthamanuttarabuddhadharmāṇāṃ gotram, tadā tatsāmānyavartitvād 'na bodhisattva eveti' mandabuddhi puruṣaṃ pratyāśaṃkya antaraślokamāha -
children.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose nature is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> because it is the cause for the realization of the noble <s>dharmas</s>, is the naturally abiding <s>gotra</s> of the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, then since [the <s>dharmadhātu</s>] is common to all, suspecting that a person of dull intellect might [object]: 'Then it is not only the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [who has it]'—[the author] states an intervening verse—
"Since the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is undivided, a division of <s>gotra</s> is not tenable."

children.text: yathā śrāvakayānādyadhigamakrameṇālambeta tathāryadharmādhigamāya dharmadhātorhetubhāvena vyavasthāpanād gotratvena vyapadeśa ityapi samādhiḥ dṛśyate, tathāpi saukaryāt laukikadṛṣṭāntenāpi samādhyantaramāha -
children.translated_text: Just as, through the sequential realization of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle and the rest, one would depend [on the <s>dharmadhātu</s>], so too, through its being established as the cause for the realization of noble <s>dharmas</s>, the designation as <s>gotra</s> is [justified]—this resolution is also seen. Nevertheless, for ease [of understanding], [the author] states another resolution with even a worldly illustration—
"But through the difference in the <s>dharmas</s> to be contained, its division is proclaimed."

Just as vessels—a pot and the rest—made from a single clay material and fired with a single fire, are differentiated by being containers for honey, sugar, and the rest that are to be contained in them; similarly, the diversity of the basis is indicated through the diversity of the <s>dharmas</s> to be realized that are to be contained, which are included in the three vehicles.
5 - The Object-Support (<s>Ālambana</s>)
What is the object-support of the stated basis of practice? [The author] says—
"The object-support is all <s>dharmas</s>; they in turn are wholesome and the rest,

children.text: laukikādhigamākhyāśca ye ca lokottarā matāḥ // Abhis_1.41 //
children.translated_text: And those called worldly realizations, and those considered supramundane,
<s>Dharmas</s> with and without outflows, conditioned and unconditioned,

children.text: śiṣyasādhāraṇā dharmā ye cāsādhāraṇā muneḥ // Abhis_1.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> common to disciples, and those uncommon to the Sage."

children.text: tatrādau tāvat sāmānyena (sarvadharmāḥ) kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtāḥ yathākramaṃ śrāmaṇyatāprāṇātipātādyavyākṛtakāyakarmādayaḥ / tatasteṣāmeva laukikādidvividhasyāvaśiṣṭāścattvāro bhedāḥ, yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bālapṛthagjanasambaddhāḥ pañca skandhāḥ, sarvāryajanasaṃgṛhītāni catvāri dhyānāni, ātmadarśanāpratipakṣatvena pañcopādānaskandhāḥ / taddarśanapratipakṣatvena catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni / hetupratyayādhīnāḥ kāmādidhātavaḥ / kāraṇānapekṣāḥ tathatā / sarvāryajanasantānaprabhavāni caturdhyānāni / samyaksambuddhasantānodayadharmīṇi daśabalāni ityevamadhigamānukrameṇa sarvadharmā yathāvadālambyanta ityālambanamekādaśavidham /
children.translated_text: Therein, first of all, in general, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome), <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome), and <s>avyākṛta</s> (indeterminate) — respectively such as the state of being a <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant), killing of living beings and so forth, and indeterminate bodily actions and the like. Then, of those very [dharmas], which are of two kinds beginning with worldly, the meaning is summarized in particular — by worldly [practices] such as generosity and so forth, all worldly wholesome [dharmas arise]; and of the supramundane, the meaning is summarized in every aspect through the categories of the path of seeing and the path of cultivation. And what they realize here through these aspects is itself inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, infinite, and subject to cessation.
6 - <s>Samuddeśa</s> (Declaration of Purpose)
What is the <s>samuddeśa</s> (declaration of purpose) of such an objective support and practice? To this, [the author] states the <s>samuddeśa</s> —
Supremacy among all beings, in the triad of mind, abandonment, and realization,
This declaration of the self-arisen ones should be known through three kinds of greatness. // Abhis_1.43 //

children.text: sarvathā sarvākārajñatāparijñānena bhaviṣyadbuddhabodhisattvānāṃ sarvasattva (rāśi)-akhilasattva (nikāya)-agratācittamahattvaṃ prahāṇamahattvamadhigamamahattvañcādhikṛtya pratipattau pravṛttatvānmahattvānmahattvatrayayuktatvācca trividhaḥ samuddeśo jñātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the complete knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) in every way, the threefold greatness of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who will become <s>Buddhas</s> consists of: greatness of mind as supremacy over all beings (<s>rāśi</s>) — the entire assembly of beings (<s>nikāya</s>), greatness of abandonment, and greatness of realization. And that <s>samuddeśa</s> (declaration of purpose) should be understood as the <s>abhisamaya</s> (clear realization) of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
7 - <s>Sannāhapratipattiḥ</s> (The Practice of Armor)

children.text: ityevaṃ pratipattyādhārādīn abhidhāya kiñca tatsvarūpamiti cet? sā trisarvajñatāviṣaye sāmānyena śukladharmādhiṣṭhānā, sarvākārābhisambodhādau caturvidhe 'bhisamaye pratyabhisamayaṃ ṣaṭpāramitādhiṣṭhānā ca kriyā paripattiḥ / evaṃ yathāvat prayogadarśanabhāvanāviśeṣamārgasvabhāvānāṃ pratipattilakṣaṇānāṃ sannāhaprasthānasambhāraniryāṇānāṃ madhye
children.translated_text: Having thus set forth the basis of practice and so on, if one asks what is its essential nature? It should be understood as, in general, the foundation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> with respect to the three kinds of omniscience, and as fourfold beginning with the complete awakening in all aspects. Therein, first —
[The author] states the first [practice], the <s>sannāhapratipattiḥ</s> (practice of armor), in the form of vigor —

children.text: dānādau ṣaḍvidhe teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ saṃgraheṇa yā /
children.translated_text: In each of the six kinds beginning with <s>dāna</s> (generosity), that which comprises [all six] in each one,
That is the <s>sannāhapratipattiḥ</s> (practice of armor), consisting of six sets of six, as taught. // Abhis_1.44 //

children.text: iti / dharmadānādidāne śrāvakādimanaskāraparivarjanam, sarvajanāpriyavāditvakṣāntiḥ, chandajananam, yānāntarāvyavakīrṇaikāgratānuttarasamyaksambodhipariṇāmanā yathākramaṃ deyādyanupalambhasannāhatvena kriyante / tathaiva śīlasya rakṣaṇam, kṣānteḥ sampādanam, vīryasya prārambhaḥ, dhyānasya ārādhanam, prajñāyā bhāvanā ityevaṃ dānādiṣaṭpāramitāsu pratyekaṃ dānādau saṃgṛhītāsu ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣaṭkaiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadvidyā bhavanti dānādisādharmyācca ṣaṭ sannāhapratipattayo bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus: in giving such as the gift of <s>Dharma</s> and so on, the avoidance of the mental disposition of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and others; patience with speaking kindly to all people; generation of zeal; one-pointed concentration unmixed with other vehicles ripening <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening); wisdom that comprehends the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> up to the four <s>Buddha-kāyas</s> (bodies of a Buddha) including the ten powers and so forth — this is the sixfold [set] within generosity. Thus, having donned the armor of thirty-six modes, [the bodhisattva proceeds]. And that [armor] is also fourfold — the practice of armor consisting of six sets of six, [totaling] thirty-six each — so say many self-arisen ones.
8 - <s>Prasthānapratipattiḥ</s> (The Practice of Setting Forth)
For one who has thus donned the armor, the setting forth [is next] — [the author] states the second, the <s>prasthānapratipattiḥ</s> (practice of setting forth) —
In the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and formless [attainments], in generosity and so on, through the paths, in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest,
And in the yoga of non-apprehension, and in the purities of the three spheres, // Abhis_1.45 //
In the declaration, in the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and in the method of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects),
The practice of setting forth should be known for one who ascends the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. // Abhis_1.46 //

The <s>prasthānapratipattiḥ</s> (practice of setting forth) consists, in meaning, of: the <s>dhyāna</s> and formless attainments, the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) beginning with generosity, the distinguished paths of seeing, cultivation, and no-more-learning, the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), the yoga of non-apprehension, the purity of the three spheres in all matters, the declaration, the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and the method of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects).
9 - <s>Sambhārapratipattiḥ</s> (The Practice of Accumulation)
For one who has thus set forth, the accumulation [is next] — [the author] states the third, the <s>sambhārapratipattiḥ</s> (practice of accumulation) —
Compassion, the sixfold [set] headed by generosity, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) together with <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight),

children.text: yuganaddhaśca yo mārgaṃ upāye yacca kauśalam // Abhis_1.47 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>yuganaddha</s> (conjoined) path, and skill in means, // Abhis_1.47 //

children.text: jñānaṃ puṇyaṃ mārgaśca dhāraṇī bhūmayo daśa /
children.translated_text: Knowledge, merit, and the path, <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions), the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
And the antidotes — the sequence of the practice of accumulation should be known. // Abhis_1.48 //

children.text: mahākaruṇa-dāna-śīla-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñā-śamatha-vidarśanā-yuganaddhamārga-upāyakauśala-jñāna-puṇya-darśanādimārga-vacanādidhāraṇī-bhūmi-pratipakṣāṇāmanupalambhena saṃvṛtisatyānatikrameṇa samastamahāyānārthapratipatterebhiḥ karuṇādibhiḥ samyak-pratipatsvābhāvyāt mahābodhigrahaṇāt mahākaruṇādisambhārā iti saptadaśa sambhārapratipattayaḥ / tatra jñānasambhāraḥ ādhyātmika-bāhya-tadubhaya-śūnyatā-mahat-paramārtha-saṃskṛta-asaṃskṛta-atītānanta-anavarāgra-anavakāra-prakṛti-sarvadharma-lakṣaṇa-anupalambha-abhāvasvabhāva-bhāva-abhāva-svabhāva-parabhāvaśūnyatānāṃ bhedena viṃśatidhā /
children.translated_text: The <s>sambhārapratipattiḥ</s> (practice of accumulation) consists, in meaning, of: great compassion, generosity, moral discipline, vigor, meditation, wisdom, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight), the <s>yuganaddha</s> (conjoined) path, skill in means, knowledge, merit, the path beginning with the path of seeing, <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions) such as the retention of speech, the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), and the antidotes. For this practice of accumulation is the general characteristic of the <s>āryamārga</s> (noble path).
From the perspectives of internal, external, both, and emptiness,
And from the perspectives of the directions, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, purpose, the conditioned, and the unconditioned, // 1 //
From the perspectives of the ultimate, the lowest, the highest, non-rejection, and non-modification,
And again from the perspectives of the nature of all dharmas, the characteristic, the past and so forth, // 2 //
From the perspectives of conjunction, non-existence, space-like emptiness, and inherent nature,
And from separation from inherent nature — twenty <s>śūnyatās</s> (emptinesses) are recognized. // 3 //

children.text: bhūmisambhāreṇa daśabhūbhaya iti pariṣkriyamāṇānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃdarśanāya trayoviṃśatirantaraślokā kathyante -
children.translated_text: To demonstrate the <s>dharmas</s> being purified by the accumulation of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), namely the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, twenty-three intermediate verses are spoken —
1. <s>Pramuditā bhūmiḥ</s> (The Joyful Stage)
The first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) is attained through tenfold preparation:
Intention, being beneficial to beings, equal-mindedness toward beings, // Abhis_1.49 //
Relinquishment, attendance upon spiritual friends, seeking the support of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
Constant mentality of renunciation, aspiration directed toward the <s>Buddha-kāya</s> (body of a Buddha), // Abhis_1.50 //
Teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, and truthfulness is held to be the tenth [quality];
And the preparation of these should be known through the non-apprehension of inherent nature. // Abhis_1.51 //

children.text: iti / yathāvat sarvavastuṣu akauṭilyāśayaḥ, sva-paraprayojane hitatvam, sarvasattveṣu samacittatā, sarvasvaparityāgaḥ, kalyāṇamitrārāgaṇam, yānatrayasaṅgṛhīta saddharmālambanaparyeṣṭiḥ, gṛhavāsānabhiratiḥ, anuttarabuddhakāyagatā spṛhā, saddharmaprakāśanam, satyavāditetyevamebhirdaśabhirlakṣaṇadharmaiḥ sarvathotpadyamānattvāt parikarmabhiḥ kāraṇaviśeṣaiḥ svabhāvānupalambhatayā kṛtaviśeṣalakṣaṇaparikarmabhireva prathamā pramuditā bhūmiḥ prāpyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: a sincere intention free from crookedness regarding all things, being beneficial in one's own and others' purposes, equal-mindedness toward all beings, complete relinquishment of all one's possessions, devotion to spiritual friends, aspiration for the support of the true <s>Dharma</s> in the three vehicles, the mentality of renunciation, constant aspiration directed toward the <s>Buddha-kāya</s>, teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, and truthful speech — these are the ten. Likewise, [the preparation is accomplished] through the non-apprehension of the inherent nature of those preparations.
2 - <s>Vimalā bhūmiḥ</s> (The Stainless Stage)

children.text: śīlaṃ kṛtajñatā kṣānti pramodyaṃ mahatī kṛpā /
children.translated_text: Moral discipline, gratitude, patience, joy, great compassion,
Respect, service to teachers, vigor in generosity and so forth is the eighth. // Abhis_1.52 //

children.text: iti kuśaladharma-sattvārthakriyā-saṃvaraśīlāni, parakṛtopakārasya avismaraṇam (avipraṇāśanam), parakṛtāpakārādau kṣāntiḥ, kuśaladharmasyārādhane 'vipratisāraḥ, sarvajaneṣu maitrī, upādhyāyādiṣu praṇamanam, kalyāṇamitranirdiṣṭadharmasādhanā, dānādiṣaṭpāramitāsu paryeṣṭirityevaṃ kṛtaparikarmaviśeṣeṇāṣṭaprakāradharmeṇa dvitīyā vimalā bhūmiradhigamyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: the moral disciplines of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, acting for the welfare of beings, and restraint; not forgetting (not losing) the help rendered by others; patience toward harm done by others and so forth; not losing [heart] in the accomplishment of wholesome dharmas (joy); great compassion toward all beings; respect for teachers and those who are teacher-like; attendance upon them; and unflagging (unwavering) vigor in providing <s>nirvṛti</s> (satisfaction) through generosity and so on to the virtuous.
3. <s>Prabhākarī bhūmiḥ</s> (The Luminous Stage)

children.text: atṛptatā śrute dānaṃ dharmasya ca nirāmiṣam /
children.translated_text: Insatiability in learning, giving of the <s>Dharma</s> without material [motive],
Purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), unweariness in <s>saṃsāra</s>, // Abhis_1.53 //
Shame and moral dread — this is fivefold, having the nature of forbearance.

children.text: iti / saddharmaśravaṇe tṛpterajñānam, lābhādinirapekṣacittena saddharmaprakāśanam, svabuddhakṣetrāśrayāśritasaṃśodhanam, upakṛtasattvavaiparītyādidarśanena na parikhedāpattiḥ, svaparāpekṣayā akuśaladharmākaraṇamityevaṃ pañcadhā parikarmaṇā pūrvavat kṛtānavabudhyamānasvabhāvaparikarmaṇā tṛtīyā prabhākarī bhūmiravabudhyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: not being sated in hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> [reflects] non-ignorance; illuminating the true <s>Dharma</s> with a mind free from concern for gain and the like; purifying the beings and the basis of one's own <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field); unweariness in <s>saṃsāra</s> upon seeing the ingratitude of beings one has helped and so forth; shame and moral dread — these constitute the fulfillment of the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) with five components.
4. <s>Arciṣmatī bhūmiḥ</s> (The Radiant Stage)
Forest-dwelling, few desires, contentment, observance of the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic practices), // Abhis_1.54 //
Non-abandonment of the training, disgust toward sensual pleasures,
Disenchantment through abandoning the Sarvāstivāda [view of real existence], being neither dejected nor attached. // Abhis_1.55 //

children.text: iti / araṇyāvāsaḥ, aprāptalābheṣu anabhilāṣaḥ, prāptalābheṣvanadhikābhyarthanā, bhikṣādidhautaguṇasaṃvaraṇam, gṛhītaśikṣāṇāṃ prāṇādibhyo 'pi aparityajanam, kāmaguṇeṣu doṣopalambhadarśanena nindanam, vineyānusāreṇa nirvāṇe pravaṇatvam, sarvasvaparityāgaḥ, kuśalasādhane cittāsaṃkocaḥ, sarvavastvanapekṣaṇamityevaṃ pūrvavaddaśaprakāreṇa caturthī arciṣmatī bhūmirabhirūhyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: dwelling in the forest, absence of longing for gains not obtained, not seeking more than what has been obtained, maintaining the restraint of ascetic qualities such as alms-gathering and so forth, not abandoning the trainings undertaken even at the cost of one's life, disgust toward sensual pleasures, disenchantment through abandoning the <s>Sarvāstivāda</s> (doctrine that all exists), and with an un-dejected mind, indifference to worldly intercourse accompanied by the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation).
5. <s>Sudurjayā bhūmiḥ</s> (The Hard-to-Conquer Stage)
Intimate association, attachment to families, a situation conducive to socializing,
Self-praise and disparagement of others, the ten unwholesome courses of action, // Abhis_1.56 //
Pride, rigidity, perversion, doubt, and tolerance of defilements —

children.text: vivarjayan samāpnoti daśaitān pañcamīṃ bhuvam // Abhis_1.57 //
children.translated_text: One who has cut off these twenty blemishes attains the fifth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // Abhis_1.57 //

children.text: iti / lābhādyarthaṃ gṛhipravrajitādibhiḥ saṃvāsaḥ, śrāddhakulānupadarśanam, janākīrṇanagarādi, svapraśaṃsanaparanindane, daśākuśalakarmapathāḥ, śrutādyabhimānaḥ, parāpraṇamanam, kuśalākuśalaviparītābhīniveśaḥ, mithyādṛṣṭyādikumatiḥ, sarvarāgādisarvakleśābhimukhīkaraṇaṃ cetyevaṃlakṣaṇān daśadharmān vivarjayan arthādākṣiptaviparyayadharmeṇa daśaprakāraparikarmaṇā pūrvavat pañcamī sudurjayā bhūmirākramyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: associating with householders and renunciants for the sake of gain and the like; frequenting faithful families; crowded cities and so forth; self-praise and disparagement of others; the ten unwholesome courses of action; pride born from learning and the like; rigidity due to lack of effort; the four perversions rooted in ignorance; doubts about the true <s>Dharma</s>; and tolerance of defilements in enduring what should and should not be practiced — by abandoning these twenty [blemishes], the fulfillment of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) consisting of the four training precepts and so forth [is achieved].
6. <s>Abhimukhī bhūmiḥ</s> (The Directly-Facing Stage)
Through the fulfillment of generosity, moral discipline, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom,
Avoiding the aspirations of disciples and solitary realizers, and the fear [of emptiness] in the minds [of some],
When asked, being unwithdrawn, and even in relinquishing everything, being undismayed,

children.text: kṛśo 'pi nārthināṃ kṣeptā ṣaṣṭhīṃ bhūmiṃ samaśnute // Abhis_1.59 //
children.translated_text: Even when emaciated, not turning away supplicants — one attains the sixth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // Abhis_1.59 //

children.text: dānādiṣaṭpāramitāparipūraṇena śrāvakapratyekabuddhābhilāṣasya svabhāvānupalambhotttrāsasya ca yācakajanaprārthanāsaṃkocasya svarasapravṛttasarvārthatyāgadaurmanasyasya dāridryādarthijanapratikṣepacittasya ca varjanenetyevaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ parikarmabhiḥ pūrvavat ṣaṣṭhī abhimukhī bhūmirājñāyate /
children.translated_text: Through the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) beginning with generosity, by avoiding: the aspiration for the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) [vehicles]; the terror at the non-apprehension of inherent nature; the reluctance in fulfilling the requests of supplicants; dismay at the spontaneous relinquishment of everything; and the non-giving of even one's own bodily flesh and so forth to supplicants when in an emaciated condition.
7. <s>Dūraṅgamā bhūmiḥ</s> (The Far-Going Stage)
Grasping at a self, a being, a soul, a person; eternalism and nihilism;
Clinging to signs and causes in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), // Abhis_1.60 //
Abiding in the three realms, attachment, a dejected mind,
Clinging to views regarding the Three Jewels and moral discipline, // Abhis_1.61 //
Disputing about <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and opposition to it — these twenty

children.text: kalaṅkā yasya vicchinnāḥ saptamīmetyasau bhuvam // Abhis_1.62 //
children.translated_text: Blemishes, one who has severed them attains the seventh <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // Abhis_1.62 //

children.text: iti / ātmasattvajīvapudgalocchedaśāśvatanimittahetuskandhadhātvāyatanatraidhātukādhiṣṭhāna-saktyālīnacittabuddhadharmasaṃghaśīladṛṣṭyabhiniveśaśūnyatāvivādavirodhodbhāvanāgrahotsṛṣṭayaścetyevaṃ viṃśatiprakārakalaṅkāpagamādākṣiptaviparyayadharmeṇa viṃśatiprakāreṇa parikarmadharmeṇa pūrvavat saptamī dūraṅgamā bhūmiḥ samīyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: grasping at self, being, soul, person, nihilism, eternalism, signs, causes, aggregates, elements, sense bases, the three realms, abiding, attachment, dejected mind, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṅgha</s>, moral discipline, clinging to views, dispute about emptiness, and opposition to it — these are the twenty kinds.
To indicate the nature of <s>dharmas</s> implied by the meaning, [the author] says —
Knowledge of the three gates of liberation, purity of the three spheres,
Contemplation of compassion, equality of <s>dharmas</s>, knowledge of the single method, // Abhis_1.63 //
Patience regarding the non-arising [of dharmas], ignorance, the unification of <s>dharmas</s>,
Eradication of conceptual elaboration, and avoidance of perception, views, and defilements, // Abhis_1.64 //
