Application of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and skill in <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight),

children.text: cittasya dāntatā jñānaṃ sarvatrāpratighāti ca // Abhis_1.65 //
children.translated_text: Taming of the mind, knowledge, and unobstructedness everywhere, // Abhis_1.65 //
Non-attachment as the [defining] ground, going to other buddha-fields as one wishes, equally
Seeing one's own nature everywhere — these are the twenty [qualities]. // Abhis_1.66 //

children.text: śūnyatā 'nimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhasamyagjñānam, daśakuśalakarmapatheṣu vadhavadhyaghātakānupalambhādi, sarvasattvālambanakaruṇā, vastvanupalambhaḥ, sarvadharmasamatāvabodhaḥ, mahāyānaikayānāvabodhaḥ, anutpādaparijñānam, gambhīradharmanidhyānakṣāntyavagamaḥ, sarvajñeyānāṃ mahāyānopāyamukhena prakāśanam, sarvakalpanocchedaḥ, nimittodgrahaṇavikalpābhāvasatkāyādipañcadṛṣṭisantyāgaḥ, rāgādikleśavarjanāni, śamathabhāvanā, prajñākauśalyam, cittopaśamaḥ, rūpādyapratighātajñānam, abhiniveśāsthānam, yatheṣṭasamakālabuddhakṣetragamanam, vineyānurūpaṃ sarvatra svakāyaprakāśanamiti viṃśatiprakāreṇānena parikarmadharmeṇāpi pūrvavat saptamī bhūmiḥ samīyate /
children.translated_text: Right knowledge of the three gates of liberation—<s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness), and <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness); non-apprehension of killer, killed, and killing in the ten wholesome courses of action; compassion with all beings as its object; non-apprehension of real entities; understanding of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>; understanding that the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the single vehicle; understanding of non-production; understanding consisting of patient acceptance through reflection on profound <s>dharmas</s>; illumination of all knowable things through the method of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; cutting off of all conceptual constructions; absence of conceptualizing in the grasping of signs and abandonment of the five views beginning with the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>); avoidance of the defilements of desire and the rest; cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding); skill in wisdom; calming of the mind; knowledge of the non-obstruction of form and the rest; not abiding in attachment; going to <s>Buddha</s>-fields at will simultaneously; and manifesting one's own body everywhere in conformity with those to be trained—thus by these twenty types of preparatory practices, as before, the seventh stage is attained.
8. The <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable) Stage:
Knowledge of the minds of all beings, playing with superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the auspicious [stage],
accomplishment of the <s>Buddha</s>-field, examination of the service of <s>Buddhas</s>; (Abhis 1.67)
attainment of sense-knowledge, purification of the <s>Jina</s>'s field, abiding as if in illusion,
and deliberate taking of birth in [conditioned] existence—this is the <s>karma</s> (function) stated as eightfold. (Abhis 1.68)

children.text: iti / yathāvatsarvasattvacittacaritajñānam, lokadhātau ṛddhyabhijñābhiḥ krīḍanam, ādhārabuddhakṣetrasuvarṇādibhāvapariṇāmaḥ, sarvākāradharmaparīkṣaṇena buddharāgaṇam, divyacakṣuṣo niṣpattiḥ, ādheyabuddhakṣetrasattvapariśodhanam, sarvatra māyopamatāvasthānam, sarvasattvārthadarśanāda buddhipūrvakajanmagrahaṇañcetyevamaṣṭaprakāradharmeṇa parikarmaṇā pūrvavadaṣṭamī acalā bhūmiranubhūyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: knowledge as it truly is of the mental conduct of all beings; playing in the world-systems with the superknowledges of miraculous powers; transformation of the supporting <s>Buddha</s>-field into gold and the like; examination of all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects as the service of the <s>Buddhas</s>; accomplishment of the divine eye; purification of the beings in the supported <s>Buddha</s>-field; abiding everywhere in the manner of illusion; and deliberate taking of birth through seeing the welfare of all beings—thus by these eight types of preparatory practices, as before, the eighth stage, <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable), is experienced.
9. The <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence) Stage:
Infinite aspirations (<s>praṇidhānas</s>), knowledge of the languages of gods and others,
eloquence like a river, supreme entry into the womb; (Abhis 1.69)
of family, caste, lineage, retinue, birth,
renunciation, <s>Bodhi</s>-trees, and one's own attainment in the fullness of qualities. (Abhis 1.70)

children.text: iti / anantapraṇidhānam, devādisarvasattvarutajñānam, nadyupamitākṣayapratibhānam, sarvajanapraśastagarbhāvakramaṇam, rājādisthānam, ādityādyanvayaḥ, mātrādisusambandhajñātiḥ, svavidheyaparivāraḥ, śakrādyabhinanditotpādaḥ, buddhādisañcodananiṣkramaṇam, cintāmaṇisadṛśāśvatthavṛkṣādiḥ, buddhabuddhadharmasvabhāvaguṇaparipūraṇañcetyevaṃ sampattilakṣaṇairdvādaśabhiḥ parikarmabhiḥ pūrvavatkṛtaparikarmaviśeṣairnavamī sādhumatī bhūmiḥ sākṣātkriyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: infinite <s>praṇidhānas</s> (aspirations); knowledge of the languages of all beings beginning with gods; inexhaustible eloquence likened to a river; entry into the womb praised by all people; position as kings and the like; descent in the lineage of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) and the like; well-connected kin such as the mother and so forth; a retinue of one's own followers; birth celebrated by <s>Śakra</s> and others; renunciation urged by <s>Buddhas</s> and others; a <s>Bodhi</s>-tree like the <s>Aśvattha</s> resembling a wish-fulfilling gem; and fulfillment of the qualities of the essential nature of <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>—thus by these twelve preparatory practices characterized by attainments, with their specific preparatory distinctions as before, the ninth stage, <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence), is directly realized.
10. The <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>) Stage:

children.text: hetubhūmitvena tatparikarmāṇyevaṃ nirdiśya phalabhūmitvena pṛthak tānyanabhidhāya saṅgrahaṇena daśamabhūmilakṣaṇamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus indicated the preparatory practices in terms of the causal stages, and without separately stating them for the resultant stage, he states the characteristic of the tenth stage in summary:
Having traversed the nine stages, one is established on the <s>Buddha</s> stage;

children.text: yena jñānena sā jñeyā daśamī bodhisattvabhūḥ // Abhis_1.71 //
children.translated_text: by that knowledge, the tenth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage should be known. (Abhis 1.71)

children.text: iti / śrāvakādigotra-prathamaphalapratipannaka-srota-āpanna-sakṛdāgāmi-anāgāmi-arhatāmiti ṣaṇṇāṃ nayatrayavyavasthāpanābhiprāyeṇa śeṣasaṅgṛhītāpannakatrayasya pratyekabuddhasya ca yathākramaṃ gotra-aṣṭamaka-darśana-tanu-vītarāga-kṛtavikalpa-śrāvaka-pratyekabuddhabhūmayaḥ, bodhisattvānāṃ yathoktā navavidhetyevaṃ navabhūmīratikramya daśamyāṃ punaḥ bhūmau bodhisattvo buddha eva vaktavyo na tu samyaksambuddha iti vacanāt buddhabhūmau yena praṇidhānajñānenāvatiṣṭhate sā eva daśamī bodhisattvabhūmiḥ jñeyā /
children.translated_text: Thus: With the intention of the threefold system of establishing six [types]—<s>śrāvaka</s> and other <s>gotras</s> (lineages), first-fruit attainers, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, and <s>arhats</s>—and with the remaining three attainers and the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> subsumed [therein], the stages are respectively: <s>gotra</s> (lineage), <s>aṣṭamaka</s> (eighth), <s>darśana</s> (seeing), <s>tanu</s> (diminished), <s>vītarāga</s> (dispassionate), <s>kṛtavikalpa</s> (fulfilled in discrimination), the <s>śrāvaka</s> stage, and the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> stage; for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the nine as described. Thus, having traversed the nine stages, on the tenth stage the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be called a <s>Buddha</s> but not a 'perfectly, fully awakened one' (as stated). By that aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhānajñāna</s>) by which one abides on the <s>Buddha</s> stage, that very [stage] should be known as the tenth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage.
(The Accumulation of Antidotes)
For the purpose of the accumulation of antidotes, he states an intervening verse:
The antidote should be known as eightfold, on both the path of seeing and the path of cultivation,
for the pacification of eight conceptualizations of grasped and grasper. (Abhis 1.72)

children.text: iti / sāṃkleśikavastumātrapratipakṣādhiṣṭhānagrāhyavikalpadvayasya dravyapudgalaprajñaptipuruṣādhiṣṭhānagrāhakavikalpadvayasya ca darśanamārgabhāvanāmārgayoḥ prahāṇād grāhyagrāhakāṣṭavikalpopaśāntaye satyadvayamāśritya sākṣātkaraṇīyā vipakṣabhedena mārgadvayāvasthāyāmeva aṣṭavidhāḥ pratipakṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: For the pacification of the eight conceptualizations of grasped and grasper—the two conceptualizations of the grasped that are based on the mere afflictive entities and the two conceptualizations of the grasper that are based on substance, person, and designation—through their abandonment on the path of seeing and the path of cultivation, relying on the two truths, the antidotes to be directly realized are eightfold, according to the division of opposing factors, in the two stages of the two paths.
10. The Practice of Going-Forth (<s>Niryāṇapratipatti</s>):
Having thus accumulated the accumulations, the going-forth (<s>niryāṇa</s>) is stated as the fourth practice of going-forth:
In the detailed exposition, in equality, in the welfare of beings, in the avoidance of effort,

children.text: atyantāya ca niryāṇaṃ niryāṇaṃ prāptilakṣaṇam // Abhis_1.73 //
children.translated_text: and for the ultimate—going-forth, going-forth characterized by attainment; (Abhis 1.73)
and going-forth in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, in the domain of the path—
the practice of going-forth should be known as this eightfold [practice]. (Abhis 1.74)

children.text: iti / yathokta uddeśaḥ , sarvadharmasamatā, sattvārthakaraṇam, animittasarvakriyākāritvenānābhogaḥ, śāśvatocchedarahitāvasthāviśeṣaḥ, triyānasarvārthaprāptiḥ, yathoktasarvākārajñatā tadviśiṣṭamārga ityevaṃ niryātavyavastuṣu prativiśiṣṭānyadharmābhāvena sarvānupalambhatayā ebhiraṣṭābhirniryāṇapratipattiḥ aṣṭadhā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus: the detailed exposition as stated; the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>; the accomplishment of beings' welfare; effortlessness in the sense that all activities are signless; the particular state free from eternalism and annihilationism; the attainment of all purposes of the three vehicles; <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> as stated; the path distinguished by that—thus, since there is no distinct other <s>dharma</s> in the respective objects of going-forth, through the non-apprehension of all, by these eight the practice of going-forth becomes eightfold.
End of the commentary on the first chapter of the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Second Chapter: On <s>Mārgajñatā</s> (Knowledge of Paths)
1. The Darkening and Such [Deeds of <s>Māra</s>]
Since the realization of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> is not possible without the full understanding of <s>mārgajñatā</s>, he states <s>mārgajñatā</s>:
The darkening by their own radiances, the capacity with respect to the gods,

children.text: viṣayo niyato vyāptiḥ svabhāvastasya karma ca // Abhis_2.1 //
children.translated_text: the specific object-domain, the pervasion, the essential nature, and its function; (Abhis 2.1)

children.text: mārgajñatotpattiṃ prati yogyatāpādanāya devādīnāṃ svakarmajaprabhāyāstathāgataprakṛtiprabhābhirmalinīkaraṇatā nihatamānasantāne 'dhigama utpadyata iti jñāpanāya kṛtā, ato vakroktyādhāraḥ kathitaḥ / sa cotpāditabodhicitta eveti viṣayapratiniyato bhavati / triyānavyavasthānamābhiprāyikam, na lākṣaṇikamiti nyāyādanuttarasamyaksambodhiparyavasāna eva sarvo jana ityato vītarāgetarayogināpi buddhatvaprāptaye mārgajñatā bhāvanīyeti vyāptirbhavati / sattvārthakaraṇapravṛttatvenotpāditabodhicittasya sarvathā kleśāprahāṇamiti svabhāvo bhavati / tādṛśasvabhāvasya bhūtakoṭerasākṣātkaraṇena prayopāyakauśalena cāparigṛhītasattvasya parigrahaṇādineti kāritram /
children.translated_text: For generating the capacity of gods and others toward the arising of <s>mārgajñatā</s>, the darkening of their own <s>karma</s>-born radiance by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s natural radiance [is taught]; since realization arises in the mental continuum whose pride has been crushed, [this is stated] to make known [that fact]—therefore the support is stated through indirect speech. And that [support] is the one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> itself; thus it is specifically determined as to its object-domain. Since the establishment of the three vehicles is intentional, not literal, and since by this reasoning all beings ultimately attain <s>Buddhahood</s>, <s>mārgajñatā</s> should be cultivated even by <s>vītarāga</s> yogins and others for the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s>—thus there is pervasion. The essential nature is that, being engaged in benefiting beings, the one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> does not in any way abandon the defilements. The function of one of such essential nature is: through not directly realizing the ultimate truth, and through skillful means, the gathering-in of ungathered beings and so forth.
2. The <s>Śrāvaka</s> Path:

children.text: ādhārādikamevamamidhāya mārgajñatādhikāre sarve mārgāḥ paripūrayitavyā iti śrāvakamārgamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus indicated the support and the rest, since all paths are to be fulfilled in the chapter on <s>mārgajñatā</s>, he states the <s>śrāvaka</s> path:
Through the non-apprehension of the aspects of the four noble truths,
this is the path of the <s>śrāvakas</s> to be known in the system of <s>mārgajñatā</s>. (Abhis 2.2)

children.text: iti / tatra duḥkhasatyasyānukrameṇa anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyetāni catvāri śāntākāralakṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: Therein, the four calm aspects that are the characteristics of the truth of suffering, in sequence, are: impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self.
The aspects of the truth of origination, being of the nature of cause, origination, production, and condition, are: disease, abscess, arrow, and misfortune.

children.text: nirvide virāgāya nirodhāya ca pratipanno bhavatītyatastayoḥ duḥkhasamudayayoḥ pratyekaḥ para-pralopadharmasvarūpau nirvidākārau, cala-prabhaṅgurasvarūpau virāgākārau; bhaya-upasarga-upadravasvarūpā nirodhākārāḥ / nirodhasatyasya nirodharūpa-nirātma-śānta-praṇītarūpavivikta-niryāṇarūpaśūnyānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārā nirodhasatyākārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Since one is practicing for revulsion, dispassion, and cessation—therefore, for those two [truths], suffering and origination, each has: the aspects of revulsion, whose nature is the other's deceptiveness; the aspects of dispassion, whose nature is instability and fragility; and the aspects of cessation, whose nature is danger, affliction, and calamity. The aspects of the truth of cessation are: of the nature of cessation, without self, peaceful, of excellent nature, secluded, of the nature of going-forth, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and non-formation.

children.text: mārgasatyasya mārga-nyāya-pratipatti-nairyāṇikā iti mārgasatyākārāḥ / tataścaiṣāṃ svabhāvānupalambhabhāvanayā mārgajñatādhikāre śrāvakāṇāṃ mārgo bodhisatvenaivaṃ parijñeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The aspects of the truth of the path are: path, method, practice, and going-forth. Thus, through cultivation of the non-apprehension of the essential nature of these, the path of the <s>śrāvakas</s> is to be fully understood by the <s>bodhisattva</s> in the chapter on <s>mārgajñatā</s>.
Having thus indicated the path as preceded by the realization of the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) and the full understanding of the four truths, he states the aids to penetration:
Since form and other aggregates are empty, and since there is no difference among the [types of] emptiness,
the heat stage (<s>ūṣman</s>) is through non-apprehension of those; the peak stage (<s>mūrdhagata</s>) is considered [likewise]. (Abhis 2.3)
The patience stages (<s>kṣānti</s>) are through negating the locus of permanence and such [attributes] regarding those;
through teaching the expansion starting from the ten stages; (Abhis 2.4)
the supreme <s>dharma</s> stage (<s>agradharmagata</s>) is declared on the path of the noble <s>śrāvakas</s>.
Why is that? Because the <s>Buddha</s>, having awakened, did not perceive <s>dharmas</s>. (Abhis 2.5)

children.text: rūpādiskandhānāṃ svasvarūpaśūnyatvācchūnyatānāmabhedena, rūpādīnāṃ pūrvavadanupambhena, evaṃ rūpādīnāṃ 'na nityaṃ nānityam' ityupalambhayogataḥ sthānaniṣedhena, yasmāt tathāgatena bodhimabhisambudhya dharmā na samīkṣitā iti pramāṇapuruṣādarśanakāraṇopapattyā pramuditabhūmyādau vistarāsthānadeśanayā ceti ebhirākārairyathākramaṃ satyānāmupalabdhau nirvedhabhāgīyā utpadyante /
children.translated_text: Since form and other aggregates are empty of their own nature, and through the non-differentiation of the [types of] emptiness; through the non-apprehension of form and the rest as before; through the prohibition of the locus [of attributes such as] 'neither permanent nor impermanent' regarding form and the rest, by the method of apprehension; and because the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having awakened to <s>bodhi</s>, did not perceive <s>dharmas</s>—through the reasoning of not-seeing by the authoritative person, and through teaching the expansion beginning with the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage—by these aspects, in sequence, the aids to penetration for the realization of the truths arise.
3. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> Path:

children.text: śrāvakamārgānantaraṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ mārgābhidhāne nyāyaprāpte 'pi śrāvakebhyaḥ kathaṃ prativiśiṣṭāste yena teṣāṃ mārgabheda ityāśaṅkya vaiśiṣṭyapratipādanārthaṃ tāvadāha -
children.translated_text: After the <s>śrāvaka</s> path, although it is natural to state the path of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, [one may ask:] how are they distinguished from <s>śrāvakas</s> such that there is a difference in their path? Anticipating this doubt, he first states their distinction:
The uselessness of instruction by others, [since they awaken] by their own awakening; [they are] self-arisen;
and the profundity of their knowledge—this is declared regarding the rhinoceros-like [<s>pratyekabuddhas</s>]. (Abhis 2.6)

children.text: iti / śrāvakāḥ paropadeśasāpekṣāḥ svabodhiṃ budhyante; sālāpadharmadeśanayā ca parānapi kuśale pravartayantītyāgamaḥ / pratyekabuddhāḥ punaḥ svayaṃ pūrvaśrutādyabhisaṃskāreṇa paropadeśaṃ pratyanapekṣāḥ svabodhisamadhigacchantyatasteṣāṃ buddhādyupadeśanairarthakyamityekaṃ vaiśiṣṭyam / śabdoccāraṇadharmadeśanayā śrotṛbhiḥ kriyate vaktṛjñānasāmarthyāvabodhaḥ / te (pratyekabuddhāḥ) punaḥ aśabdoccāraṇadharmadeśanayā svādhigatajñānādisāmarthyena parān daśakuśalādau pravartayantyatasteṣāṃ jñānasyānavabodhatayā dvitīyaṃ vaiśiṣṭyamiti /
children.translated_text: Thus: <s>Śrāvakas</s> depend on instruction from others and awaken to their own awakening; and through the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of conversation, they also direct others toward the wholesome—so says the tradition. <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, however, through the predisposition of former hearing and other practices, attain their own awakening without depending on instruction from others; therefore the uselessness of instruction from <s>Buddhas</s> and the like for them is the first distinction. Through <s>Dharma</s>-teaching by the utterance of words, listeners come to understand the power of the speaker's knowledge. But they [<s>pratyekabuddhas</s>], through <s>Dharma</s>-teaching without the utterance of words, by the power of their own realized knowledge and such, direct others in the ten wholesome [actions] and the like; therefore the incomprehensibility of their knowledge is the second distinction.
Anticipating the question 'How can there be <s>Dharma</s>-teaching without the utterance of words?', he says:

children.text: śuśrūṣā yasya yasyārthe yatra yatra yathā yathā /
children.translated_text: For whichever [listener], regarding whatever meaning, wherever, and in whatever manner there is desire to hear—

children.text: sa so 'rthaḥ khyātyaśabdo 'pi tasya tasya tathā tathā // Abhis_2.7 //
children.translated_text: that meaning appears to that [listener] in that manner, even without words. (Abhis 2.7)

children.text: iti / nāvitarkya nāvicārya vācaṃ bhāṣata ityālāpo vikṣepaḥ / sa ca santānakṣobhamādadhātīti yathā yathā bodhisattvena 'buddho bhūtvā ālāpamantareṇa dharmadeśanāṃ kuryām' iti praṇidhānaṃ pravartitam, tathā buddhatvasāmyāt pratyekabuddhāvasthāyāñca praṇidhānādisāmarthyena yasminnarthe yena prakāreṇa yasya śravaṇecchā, tasya vijñāne tenaiva prakāreṇa aśabdo 'pi so 'rthaḥ pratibhātītyaśabdadharmadeśanocyate / ityevaṃ vakṣyamāṇadharmasya śrotṛvijñāne sunirmāṇamutpādaścetyayaṃ bhavati dharmadeśanā śabdārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: 'He speaks words without initial application or sustained application'—this is conversation; it is the scattering [of attention]. And that produces agitation in the mental continuum. Just as the <s>bodhisattva</s> has made the aspiration 'Having become a <s>Buddha</s>, may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> without conversation,' so too, by the similarity to <s>Buddhahood</s>, in the state of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> also, through the power of aspiration and such, whatever meaning, in whatever manner, whatever listener wishes to hear—in that listener's consciousness, in that very manner, that meaning appears even without words; this is called <s>Dharma</s>-teaching without words. Thus the arising in the listener's consciousness of a well-formed [understanding] of the <s>dharma</s> to be spoken is the meaning of the term '<s>Dharma</s>-teaching.'

children.text: vaiśiṣṭyamevamabhidhāya viśiṣṭānāṃ viśiṣṭa eva mārga iti prakṛtapratyekabuddhamārgamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the distinction, since the distinguished ones have a distinguished path, he states the actual <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path:
Through the abandonment of conceptualization of the grasped object, through the non-abandonment of the grasper,
and through the support—the summary of the rhinoceros-path should be known. (Abhis 2.8)

children.text: ityuktam / pratyekabuddhasya mārgaḥ yathoktasatyabhāvanayā eva, yathāavastu pratītyasamutpādabhāvanayā ca / grāhyagrāhakārthavikalpayoryathākramaṃ prahāṇāprahāṇe pratyekabuddhayānasaṅgṛhītādhāradharmavastuno viśeṣaviśiṣṭadharmādhigamaśca bodhisattvena parijñeyo na sarvākārajñāneneti pratyekabuddhamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus stated: The path of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> is through the very cultivation of the truths as described, as well as through the cultivation of dependent origination as devoid of real entities. The respective abandonment and non-abandonment of the conceptualizations of grasped and grasper objects, and the realization of the distinct <s>dharmas</s> of the support-<s>dharma</s> entity encompassed by the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle—this should be fully understood by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, not through knowledge of all aspects. This is the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path.

children.text: nirvedhabhāgīyādhigame sati yathoktamārga utpadyata iti nirvedhabhāgīyamāha -
children.translated_text: Since the path as described arises when the aids to penetration have been realized, he states the aids to penetration:
Through non-contradiction with designation, having the form of indicating <s>dharmatā</s>,
the heat stage and the peak stage are empowered by the non-diminishment and such of form and the rest; (Abhis 2.9)
through the internal emptiness and others, through the non-grasping of form and the rest,
the patience stages; through the aspects of the non-production and such of form and the rest—the supreme <s>dharma</s> stage. (Abhis 2.10)

children.text: iti / rūpādisāṅketikadharmaprajñapteravirodhena dharmatāyāḥ pratipādanenaḥ, rūpādeḥ paramārthato na hānivṛddhyādyarthaṃ śikṣaṇena, svabhāvaśūnyatvāt rūpāderadhyātmabahirdhādiśūnyatayā aparigrahaṇena, rūpāderanutpādānirodhādyākāraiśca yathākramaṃ catuḥsatyālambane nirvedhabhāgīyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus: Through non-contradiction with the conventional designation of <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the rest, by the teaching of <s>dharmatā</s>; through the training in the meaning that there is no loss or increase and the like of form and the rest in the ultimate sense, since they are empty of own-nature; through the non-grasping of form and the rest by means of the internal, external, and other emptinesses; and through the aspects of non-production, non-cessation, and the like of form and the rest—in sequence, in observing the four truths, the aids to penetration arise.
4 - The <s>Bodhisattva</s> Path
Immediately after the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> path, [the author] states the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path—
"With fourfold moments of <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), for each and every truth,
The path of seeing with respect to <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) is said to be endowed with benefits." (Abhis 2.11)

children.text: iti / mārgajñatādhikāre bodhisattvena dharmajñānakṣāntirdharmajñānamanvayajñānakṣāntiranvayajñānaṃ ceti catvāraḥ kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ pratyekaṃ duḥkhādisatyasambandhayuktā aihikāmutrikairguṇairyuktā vimāvanīyā iti darśanamārgo mahānuśaṃsa ityucyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the chapter on <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths), the four moments of <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge)—namely, <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the knowledge of dharmas), <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas), <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge), and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge)—by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, each connected with the truths of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) and the rest, endowed with qualities pertaining to this life and the next, are to be cultivated. Thus the path of seeing is said to have great benefits.
How are the aspects to be cultivated? [The author] says—
"Due to the absence of the relation of support and supported between <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and the <s>Buddhas</s>,
Non-approbation by turns—that is the greatness and immeasurability." (Abhis 2.12)
"The absence of limitation in extent, the ascertainment of form and the rest,
For one abiding in that, [there is] no grasping or abandoning with regard to Buddhahood, and so forth." (Abhis 2.13)
"<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest, the attainment of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the encompassing of Buddhahood,
The pacification of all afflictions of all that is purified." (Abhis 2.14)
"The peace of grasping at <s>nirvāṇa</s>, protection from the <s>Buddhas</s> and the rest,
Beginning with non-killing of living beings, in the method of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience)," (Abhis 2.15)
"For one who abides [therein] oneself, the establishing of beings, the dedication,
And of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest toward <s>sambodhi</s> (complete awakening)—these are the moments of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths)." (Abhis 2.16)

children.text: paramārthataḥ tathatābuddhayorādhārādheyabhāvo na vidyata ityatastayoḥ paryāyeṇāvasthiterananujñānam / rūpādīnāṃ dharmadhātusvabhāvatayā mahattā tathaiva teṣāmapramāṇatā / pūrvavadākāśāparimāṇatayā teṣāmaparimāṇatetyevaṃ duḥkhasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: In the ultimate sense, the relation of support and supported between <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and the <s>Buddhas</s> does not exist; therefore, their non-approbation of abiding by turns. Due to the nature of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas), form and the rest have greatness, and likewise their immeasurability. As before, due to the immeasurability of space, their limitlessness—thus arise the aspects of the truth of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering).

children.text: rūpādīnāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvena śāśvatocchedādyantābhāvaḥ / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthitasya dharmadhātusvabhāvatayā rūpādīnāṃ tathāgatatvāvadhāraṇam / tathaiva tasyāṃ sthitasya sarvadharmāṇāṃ nodgrahatyāgabhāvanādikam / niḥsvabhāvādhimokṣapūrvakaṃ caturapramāṇaṃ vibhāvanīyamityevaṃ samudayasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Due to the essencelessness of form and the rest, there is the absence of extremes such as eternalism and annihilationism. For one abiding in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the ascertainment that form and the rest are of the nature of <s>Tathāgata</s>hood by virtue of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> nature. Likewise, for one abiding in that, there is no grasping, abandoning, or cultivating of all <s>dharmas</s>. The four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) are to be developed preceded by conviction in essencelessness—thus arise the aspects of the truth of <s>samudaya</s> (origination).

children.text: rūpādernijarūpā prakṛtyaiva śūnyatā / dharmadhātupariṇāmitakuśalamūlānāṃ phalaṃ tathāgatatvasya prāpaṇam / prajñāpāramitayā sarvākārapratipakṣāṇāṃ saṃgrahaḥ / tayaiva bāhyābhyantaropadravapraśamanamityevaṃ nirodhasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of form and the rest is by their very own nature. The fruit of wholesome roots transformed by the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is the attainment of <s>Tathāgata</s>hood. Through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the gathering of all antidotes of every kind. Through that very [Prajñāpāramitā], the pacification of external and internal adversities—thus arise the aspects of the truth of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation).

children.text: niḥsvabhāvatābhāvanayaiva rūpādinirvāṇābhiniveśasya śāntiḥ / prajñopāyakauśalapravṛttasya buddhebhyo rakṣāvaraṇaguptayo bhavanti / buddhatvābhilāṣiṇā svayaṃ prāṇātipātaviratyādipūrvakaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ sthitvā tatraiva pareṣāṃ sthāpanam / dānādīnāmakṣayaṃ kartumicchatā samyaksambodhau pariṇāmanamityevaṃ mārgasatyasyākārā bhavanti / ityevameva mārgajñatāyāḥ kṣaṇā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Through the very cultivation of essencelessness, the peace of fixation on <s>nirvāṇa</s> regarding form and the rest. For one who proceeds with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāyakauśala</s> (skillful means), there arise protection, safeguarding, and shielding from the <s>Buddhas</s>. For one who aspires to Buddhahood, having oneself first abstained from killing living beings and so forth, abiding in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience), one establishes others in that very [omniscience]. For one who wishes to make <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest inexhaustible, there is dedication toward <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect complete awakening)—thus arise the aspects of the truth of <s>mārga</s> (the path). In exactly this way arise the moments of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths).

children.text: kecidiha kārikārthopalakṣaṇapareṇa granthena ākārārthamanuktvā darśanamārgaṣoḍaśakṣaṇopalakṣaṇameva kevalamanukṛtamiti varṇayanti, evamuktānuktanirvedhabhāgīyādyarthakārikāsvapi draṣṭavyamiti / tairbhāvanānukramādyanirdeśāt kācidabhisamayānupūrvī na pratipāditā / 'ālambanamanityādi satyādhāraṃ tadākṛtiḥ' ityādikārikārthaśca kathaṃ vyākhyeya ityapare /
children.translated_text: Some explain that here, the text being directed toward illustrating the meaning of the verses, without explaining the meaning of the aspects, merely illustrates the sixteen moments of the path of seeing. The same should be observed in the verses on the meaning of the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (factors conducive to penetration) and so forth, both stated and unstated. Since they do not indicate the sequence of cultivation and so on, no particular order of <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization) is established by them. Others [ask] how the meaning of verses such as 'The object being impermanent and so forth, based on the truths, that is its form' should be explained.
5 - The Function of the Path of Cultivation

children.text: darśanamārgānantaraṃ bhāvanāmārgābhidhāne sati svalpavaktatvena phalanimnatvena ca vineyapravṛtteḥ tatkāritraṃ tāvat -
children.translated_text: After the path of seeing, when the path of cultivation is to be explained, since trainees proceed with little to say and with inclination toward the fruit, first its function—
"Taming in all respects, indeed the conquest of afflictions in all respects,
Invincibility against attacks, awakening, being worthy of veneration as a support." (Abhis 2.17)

children.text: ityuktam / sarvaprakāracittasvavidheyīkaraṇam, kalyāṇamitrādisarvajananamanam, rāgādyabhibhavaḥ, parakṛtāghātānanupratipatteḥ aviṣahyatvam, samyaksambodhipratipattiḥ, ādhāraviṣayapūjyatākāritrañceti ṣaḍvidhameva kāritram /
children.translated_text: Thus it is stated. Making the mind amenable to oneself in every way, respect toward all persons such as <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friends), overcoming <s>rāga</s> (desire) and the rest, invincibility due to not retaliating against assaults by others, the practice of <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect complete awakening), and the function of being worthy of veneration in the domain of support—thus the function is sixfold.
The Path of Cultivation with Outflows
6 - The Aspiration of the Path of Cultivation

children.text: kāritrānantaraṃ bhāvanāmārgaḥ / sa ca sāsravānāsravabhedena dvividhaḥ / ataḥ sāsravabhāvanāmārgādhimuktipariṇāmanānumodanāmanaskāreṣu prathamaṃ bhāvanāmārgādhimuktimanaskāramāha -
children.translated_text: After the function, [comes] the path of cultivation. That is twofold, divided into with-outflows and without-outflows. Therefore, among the mental engagements of aspiration, dedication, rejoicing of the path of cultivation with outflows, first [the author] states the mental engagement of aspiration of the path of cultivation—
"Aspiration should be known as threefold: for one's own benefit, for both one's own and others' benefit,
And for others' benefit alone—and each of these is considered threefold." (Abhis 2.18)
"Mild, middling, and intense, by the division of mild-mild and so forth,
Each again being threefold—thus it is held to be twenty-sevenfold." (Abhis 2.19)

children.text: iti / svobhayaparārthopalambhatayā yathādhimokṣaṃ dṛṣṭakuśaladharmadhiṣṭhānā bhāvanāmārgādhikārādādau asākṣātkriyārūpādhimuktiḥ trividhā satī pratyekaṃ mṛdvādibhedena trividhā / evameṣāpi pratyekaṃ mṛdumṛdvādibhedena trividhā / evaṃ navabhistribhiradhimuktiḥ saptaviṃśatiprakārā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, with apprehension of benefit for oneself, both, and others, the aspiration in the form of non-direct-realization, established in the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> seen according to one's conviction, in the chapter on the path of cultivation, being threefold at first, is threefold in each case by the division of mild and so forth. Likewise, each of these again is threefold by the division of mild-mild and so forth. Thus, aspiration through three [sets of] nine becomes twenty-seven varieties.
7 - Praise, Extolling, and Commendation of One Who Has Aspiration on the Path of Cultivation

children.text: tadbhāvakabodhisattvasyotsāhavardhanāya tadadhimokṣasya styutyādayo buddhādibhiḥ kriyanta iti stutiṃ, stobhaṃ praśaṃsāñcāha -
children.translated_text: To increase the enthusiasm of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who cultivates that, praise, extolling, and commendation of that aspiration are performed by the <s>Buddhas</s> and others. [The author] states the praise, extolling, and commendation—

children.text: stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca prajñāpāramitāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: "Praise, extolling, and commendation with regard to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
For the degrees of aspiration, are held to be in three [sets of] nine." (Abhis 2.20)

children.text: iti / yathādhimokṣadṛṣṭadharmalakṣaṇāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ prati pravṛttasyādhimokṣamanaskārasya prathamadvitrinavāvasthānāṃ pratyekaṃ navabhiḥ prakārairuttarottarābhinandanaṃ stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca iṣyate / ataste stutyādayo yathābhūtārthādhigamamātralakṣaṇā nārthavādarūpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, for the aspiration-mental-engagement that is directed toward the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> characterized by <s>dharmas</s> seen according to one's conviction, the progressive celebration in nine ways for each of the first, second, and third stages of nine is the praise, extolling, and commendation. Therefore, these praises and so forth are characterized merely by realization of things as they truly are, and are not of the nature of <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic statements).
8 - Dedication
Since aspiration thus [established] gives rise to dedication, [the author] states the second mental engagement, that of dedication—
"The distinction is dedication; its function is supreme.
It has the form of non-apprehension and is characterized by non-error." (Abhis 2.21)
"It is isolated, having as its sphere the recollection of the nature of the flood of merit of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
Endowed with skillful means, signless, and approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>." (Abhis 2.22)
"Not fallen into the three realms, and the other dedication is threefold:
Mild, middling, and intense, having as its nature the arising of great merit." (Abhis 2.23)

children.text: iti / yathokto viśeṣādhimokṣaḥ, anupalambhaḥ, aviparyāsaḥ, viviktaḥ, tathāgatakuśalamūlaudhasvabhāvasmṛtiḥ, sopāyakauśalaḥ, animittaḥ, buddhānujñātaḥ, traidhātukāprapannaḥ, mṛdumadhyādhimātraśca mahāpuṇyodaya ityevamadhyāropitamanaskārā yathākramamanuttarasamyaksambodhiḥ śīlādiskandha-pariṇāmanācitta-ātmādiyuktavastu-trikālabuddhakuśala-dānādi-nimitta-sarvamārga-kāmādidhātu-daśakuśalakarmapatha-srota-āpannādyanuttarasambodhiprasthitānāmanupalabdhānāmupalambhā iti triyānavineyasattvānāṃ mārgopadeśahetubhāvavyāpārayuktaiḥ sarvasattvārthamakṣayāya cānuttarasamyaksambodhau dvādaśa pariṇāmanāḥ kriyante /
children.translated_text: Thus, the distinguished aspiration as stated, non-apprehension, non-error, isolation, recollection of the nature of the flood of wholesome roots of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, endowment with <s>upāyakauśala</s> (skillful means), signlessness, approval by the <s>Buddhas</s>, non-falling into the three realms, and the mild, middling, and intense great arising of merit—thus, with the superimposed mental engagements in due order, [there are] twelve dedications made toward <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect complete awakening): the dedication of <s>śīla</s> (morality) and other <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), of <s>citta</s> (mind), of entities connected with self and so forth, of wholesome [roots] of <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times, of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest, of signs, of all paths, of the realms of <s>kāma</s> (desire) and the rest, of the ten wholesome courses of action, and the non-apprehension of <s>Srotāpannas</s> (stream-enterers) and the rest up to those who have set forth toward <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s>—these [dedications] are made for the sake of all beings, for inexhaustibility, toward unsurpassed perfect complete awakening, endowed with the activity of being a cause for instruction on the path for beings to be trained of the three vehicles.
9 - Rejoicing
Thus, having dedicated the objects [of merit], in order to further increase them, [the author] states the third mental engagement, that of rejoicing—
"Through skillful means and non-apprehension, the rejoicing in wholesome roots
Is ordained here as the cultivation of the mental engagement of rejoicing." (Abhis 2.24)
Thus, having apprehended the wholesome roots through conventional skillful means, with a joyful mind, they are to be rejoiced in as ultimately non-apprehensible.

children.text: tatrāyaṃ samāsārthaḥ-ākarānniṣkṛṣṭaḥ svarṇapiṇḍa ivādhimokṣamanaskāraḥ, svarṇakāreṇa tato 'laṅkārakaraṇamiva samyaksambodheraṅgakaraṇaṃ pariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, svaparapuṇyasamatāprāpti anumodanāmanaskāra iti /
children.translated_text: Here the summary meaning is as follows: the mental engagement of aspiration is like a lump of gold extracted from a mine; the mental engagement of dedication is like a goldsmith fashioning ornaments from that [gold], making it into a component of <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect complete awakening); the mental engagement of rejoicing is the attainment of equality of one's own and others' merit.
The Path of Cultivation without Outflows
10 - Actualization

children.text: sāsravānantaramanāsravo bhāvanāmārgaḥ / sa ca dvividha iti prathamamabhinirhāralakṣaṇaṃ bhāvanāmārgamāha -
children.translated_text: After [the path] with outflows, [comes] the path of cultivation without outflows. That too being twofold, first [the author] states the path of cultivation characterized by actualization—
"Its own-nature, its supremacy, the non-conditioning of everything,
The directing of <s>dharmas</s> through non-apprehension, and great purposefulness." (Abhis 2.25)

children.text: iti / rūpādyaviparītadarśanaṃ svabhāvaḥ / nānyathā buddhatvasaṃprāptiriti śreṣṭhatā / sarvadharmaviśeṣānutpādanena adhigamaprayogo 'nabhisaṃskāraḥ / tādṛśasvabhāvādiyuktamārgadharmāṇāmanupalambhatayā yogisantāne samutpādanamarpaṇā / buddhatvamahārthasādhanānmahārthatā /
children.translated_text: Thus, the unmistaken seeing of form and the rest is the own-nature. That Buddhahood is not attained otherwise is its supremacy. The practice of realization through the non-production of distinction among all <s>dharmas</s> is non-conditioning. The arising in the continuum of the <s>yogin</s> (practitioner), through non-apprehension of the path-<s>dharmas</s> endowed with such own-nature and the rest, is the directing. Due to accomplishing the great purpose of Buddhahood, it has great purposefulness.

children.text: 11 - atyantaviśuddhiḥ tadanantaraṃ yaḥ parigrahatyāgena prāpsyamānaḥ kastasyotpādānutpādaheturiti ākāṃkṣānirāsadvāreṇa dvitīyamatyantaviśuddhilakṣaṇamāha -
children.translated_text: 11 - Ultimate Purity. Next, what will be obtained through the relinquishment of grasping—what is the cause of its arising and non-arising? Through the door of dispelling such doubt, [the author] states the second [path of cultivation], characterized by ultimate purity—
"Service to the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest, and whatever skill in means [there is],
These are the causes of aspiration here; the causes of the decline of <s>Dharma</s> [are]:" (Abhis 2.26)
"The domination by <s>Māra</s>, non-conviction in the profound <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of dharmas),
Fixation on the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the rest, and association with evil companions." (Abhis 2.27)

Thus, devotion to the <s>Buddhas</s>, fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest, and skill in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding)—these are the causes of arising.
Being obstructed by <s>Māra</s>, non-conviction in the profound <s>dharmas</s>, grasping at existence, and association with evil companions—these are the causes of non-arising.
Having thus stated the causes of attainment and non-attainment, [the author] states the purity of what is under discussion in general—
"The purity of the fruit and the purity of form and the rest—of both of those,
Since they are undivided and unbroken, purity is proclaimed." (Abhis 2.28)

children.text: iti / āryapudgalasya yat śrāmaṇyatāphalaṃ tasya sarvavipakṣarahitatvena yā viśuddhiḥ saiva rūpādiviśuddhiḥ, phalarūpādiviśuddhiḥ rūpāderātmābhiniveśādivigamāt / prabhedatvena yasmāt tadviśuddhiḥ abhinnā acchinnā tasmāt svasāmānyalakṣaṇanānātvavirahād evaṃ viśuddhirabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever is the fruit of the <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (ascetic life) of the noble person, the purity of that, being free from all adversaries, is itself the purity of form and the rest. The purity of the fruit and of form and the rest [arises] from the removal of the fixation on a self regarding form and the rest. Since that purity is, by way of being undifferentiated, undivided and unbroken, being free from the multiplicity of individual and general characteristics, purity is thus proclaimed.
Having thus stated purity in general, [the author] states it in particular—
"Of afflictions, the knowable, and the three paths, of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary realizers), and the natural sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (victors),
Purity [comes] from abandonment; but for the <s>Buddha</s>, it is ultimate in every way." (Abhis 2.29)

children.text: iti / rāgādikleśaprahāṇāt, etasya jñeyāvaraṇaikadeśagrāhyavikalpasya ca prahāṇāt, yānatrayamārgāvaraṇaprahāṇād yathākramaṃ śrāvaka-pratyekabuddha-bodhisattvānāṃ śuddhirbhavati / sarvathā savāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt dharmadhātūdbhavānuttarabuddhānāṃ viśuddhiriṣyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, from the abandonment of afflictions such as <s>rāga</s> (desire), from the abandonment of this partial grasping at the knowable that is the obscuration of the knowable, and from the abandonment of the path-obscurations of the three vehicles, respectively, the purity of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> comes about. The purity of the unsurpassed <s>Buddhas</s>, who arise from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, is held to come from the abandonment of the obscurations of afflictions and the knowable together with their latencies in every way.

children.text: mārgajñatādhikāre viśuddikathanaprasaṅgādātyantikī cetarā ca buddhānāṃ śrāvakādīnāṃ ca yathākramaṃ viśuddhiḥ / saḥ kathamityāha -
children.translated_text: Since the occasion arises for discussing purity in the chapter on <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths), the ultimate and the other purities of the <s>Buddhas</s> and of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the rest, respectively, [are discussed]. How is that? [The author] says—
"The path beginning with mild-mild, purity in the nine stages,
As the antidote to defilement beginning with the most intense." (Abhis 2.30)

children.text: iti / kāradhātudhyānārūpyasamāpattaya iti navabhūmiṣvadhimātrādinavaprakāravipakṣasya pratipakṣabhāvena mṛdumṛdvādimārgo yathākramaṃ navaprakāraḥ / sarvathānyathā ca viśuddhihetutvādātyantikī cetarā ca viśuddhiriti /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the nine stages—the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), and the <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments)—the path beginning with mild-mild is ninefold in due order as the antidote to the ninefold adversary beginning with the most intense. Since it is in every way and otherwise the cause of purity, both the ultimate and the other purities [are established].
How is the ultimate [purity]? [The author] says—
"The antidotal nature with respect to the three realms, the equality of the measurable and the measure,

children.text: mārgasya ceṣyate tasya codyasya parihārataḥ // Abhis_2.31 //
children.translated_text: Of that path, is held [to be ultimate purity], by way of answering the objection." (Abhis 2.31)

children.text: iti / tatrādhimātrādhimātrādiḥ pratipakṣo mṛdumṛdvādirvipakṣa iti bhavitavyamiticodyasya vastraliptasūkṣmamalāpakaṣarṇe rajakamahāyatnodāharaṇena parihārataḥ yathānirdiṣṭabhāvanāmārgasyātyantikī / traidhātukākārajñānajñeyānupalambhād yā samatā saiva samastapratipakṣatvādātyantikī viśuddhirbuddhasya vyavasthāpyata iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, [to the objection] that the most intense antidote should correspond to the mildest adversary, by way of answering the objection through the illustration of the great effort of a washerman in removing fine stains from cloth, the ultimate [purity] of the path of cultivation as described [is established]. The equality through the non-apprehension of the aspects, knowledge, and the knowable of the three realms—that very equality, being the antidote to everything, is established as the ultimate purity of the <s>Buddha</s>.
The commentary on the second chapter of the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instructions on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text:
Sarvajñatādhikāraḥ tṛtīyaḥ
1 - prajñayā na bhave sthānam
2 - kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ
children.translated_text:
The Third Chapter: <s>Sarvajñatā</s> (Omniscience)
1 - Through Wisdom, No Abiding in Existence
2 - Through Compassion, No Abiding in Quiescence

children.text: sarvavastuparijñānaṃ vinā na mārgajñatāparijñānaṃ samyag iti sarvajñatāmāha -
children.translated_text: Without the complete knowledge of all things, the complete knowledge of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) is not correct; therefore [the author] states <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)—

children.text: nāpare na pare tīre nāntarāle tayoḥ sthitā /
children.translated_text: "Not abiding on this shore, nor on the far shore, nor in between the two,
Due to the knowledge of the equality of the three times, it is considered <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the perfection of wisdom)." (Abhis 3.1)

children.text: iti / traiyadhvikadharmāṇāmanutpādākāreṇa tulyatāvabodhāt buddhabodhisattvānāṃ yā āsannībhūtā matā prajñāpāramitā, sā khalu prajñayā punarnāpare tīre saṃsāre, na pare tīre nirvāṇe ca yathākramaṃ śāśvatocchedalakṣaṇe, na tayormadhye 'pi vyavasthiteti na saṃsāranirvāṇayoḥ vyavasthitā /
children.translated_text: Thus, because <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> understand the equality of phenomena across the three times through the aspect of non-arising, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that is considered to have become proximate to them is indeed not established in <s>saṃsāra</s> on the near shore through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), nor in <s>nirvāṇa</s> on the far shore, which are respectively characterized by eternalism and annihilationism, nor is it established in between the two — thus it is not established in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

3 - Distance through lack of skillful means
4 - Proximity through skillful means

children.text: sarvajñatādhikārād vyatirekanirdeśena śrāvakādīnāṃ tryadhvasamatājñānābhāvāt samyak prajñāpāramitā dūrībhūteti / svādhigamamātrātmikā tu prajñāpāramitā kṛpāprajñāvaikalyānnirvāṇe saṃsāre cāvasthitā vastvastūpalambhatayeti jñeyā / 'yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatā saiva te matā' iti nyāyādadhvatrayasamatājñānaṃ padārthāvabodha eva, nanu sa ca sarveṣāmeva samastīti kathaṃ śrāvakabodhisattvādīnāṃ samyak prajñāpāramitādūrībhāvaḥ, na cetareṣāṃ bhavatīti cet? āha -
children.translated_text: Since in the context of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), by way of negative indication, <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others lack the knowledge of the equality of the three times, the authentic <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is distant from them. However, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that consists merely in one's own realization is established in <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>saṃsāra</s> through apprehension of things and non-things, due to the deficiency of compassion and wisdom — this should be understood. Since by the principle that 'dependent origination is itself what is considered emptiness by you,' the knowledge of the equality of the three times is precisely the understanding of the meaning of terms. Now, if one objects that this knowledge exists equally for all, then how can <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and others be distant from the authentic <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and not others? He says —
Through lack of skillful means, she is distant, due to apprehension with characteristics;
Through skillful means, her authentic proximity is declared. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.2]

children.text: iti / māyākāranirmitavastunaḥ pratibhāse aviditatatsvarūpasya bhāvābhiniveśitā naiḥsvābhāvyāpratibhāsa iva kalyāṇamitrādyupāyakauśalavaikalyād vastu nimittayogena pratipattau tatsamatāparijñānamavijñātabhāvarūpāṇāṃ śrāvakādīnāṃ nāstītyatasteṣāṃ dūrībhāvo jinajananyā iti / bodhisattvānāṃ tu samārādhitakalyāṇamitropadeśatayā aviparītasatyadvayāśritaśrutādijñānotpattyupāyakauśalena ca utsāritabhāvābhiniveśabhrāntinimittānāṃ rūpādisarvadharmaparijñānameva tatsamatāparijñānamityatasteṣāṃ samyagāsannībhāvo 'syā māturiti anupāyena eva dūratā, upāyena tu adūratā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, just as one who does not recognize the true nature of an object created by a magician, when the appearance arises, clings to it as a real entity — as if the appearance of lack of own-nature were absent — so too, due to the deficiency in skillful means such as a spiritual friend, when engaging with things through the conjunction of characteristics, the knowledge of the equality of those things does not exist for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others whose nature of reality remains unknown. Therefore they are distant from the Mother of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors). But for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, through the instructions of well-cultivated spiritual friends, and through skillful means in the arising of knowledge from study and so forth based on the two truths without distortion, since the characteristics of the delusion of clinging to real entities have been removed, the thorough knowledge of all phenomena such as form is itself the thorough knowledge of their equality — therefore their authentic proximity to this Mother exists. Thus distance is through lack of skillful means alone, while proximity is through skillful means.
5 - The adversary (<s>vipakṣa</s>)
He states the practice of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, which through their distance from the Mother constitutes the adversary:
Regarding the emptiness of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) such as form, regarding phenomena pertaining to the three times,
And regarding generosity and the other factors of awakening, the notion of practice is the adversary. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.3]

children.text: iti / sarveṣāṃ rūpādīnāṃ traiyadhvikānāñca dharmāṇāṃ sāsravānāsravobhayasthānīyānāmanupalambhasvarūpāṇāṃ sarvatra bhāvopalambhatayā te paraparikalpitātmādiśūnyatvena dṛṣṭāḥ / anuṣṭhānasaṃjñā tu eteṣāṃ pratipakṣabhūtāni viparyāsapravṛttatvena heyatvāt vipakṣo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding all phenomena belonging to the three times such as form and the rest, which belong to the categories of the contaminated, the uncontaminated, and both, and whose nature is non-apprehension — in all cases, through apprehending them as real entities, they are seen as empty merely of a self and so forth imputed by others. But the notion of practice regarding these, because their antidotes operate in a perverted manner and are therefore to be abandoned, constitutes the adversary.
6 - The antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>)
Conversely, stating the antidote of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, he says —
Non-ego-grasping regarding generosity and the rest, engaging others in that,
The prohibition of the extreme of attachment — this subtle attachment toward the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) and others. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.4]

children.text: iti / trimaṇḍalaviśuddhyā dānādāvanātmāvabodhena svaparayorniyojanaṃ samyak pravṛttatvāt sarvasaktinicayasthānapratiṣedhena copādeyatvāt sarvathā pratipakṣaḥ / tathāgatādiṣu namaskārādiḥ puṇyasambhārahetutvena pratipakṣo 'pi san sūkṣmasaktirūpatayā na sarvathā pratipakṣa iti vipakṣo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the purity of the three spheres, engaging oneself and others in generosity and the rest through non-apprehension of self, and through the prohibition of all bases of accumulation of attachment, since it is properly engaged and to be adopted, it is in every way an antidote. However, homage and so forth toward <s>Tathāgatas</s> and others, although being an antidote as a cause for the accumulation of merit, constitutes an adversary since it has the form of subtle attachment and is therefore not entirely an antidote.
If one asks how subtle attachment is an adversary, he says —
Its profundity is by its very nature, due to the separation from the course of phenomena.

children.text: iti / yasmāt svabhāvenaiva dharmagotrāṇāṃ śūnyatvāt teṣāṃ gāmbhīryam, tasmāt tathāgatopalambho 'pi vipakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, since the lineages of phenomena are empty by their very own-nature, their profundity exists; therefore even the apprehension of a <s>Tathāgata</s> is an adversary.
If one asks how then that is to be abandoned, he says —
Knowledge of the very nature of phenomena is the abandonment of attachment. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.5]

children.text: iti / rūpādisarvadharmāṇāmekaiva prakṛtiḥ yaduta niḥsvabhāva iti jñānajñeyasamataikaparijñāne saktirvarjitā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, since the single nature of all phenomena such as form is precisely <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> (lack of own-nature), in the thorough knowledge of the equality of knowledge and the knowable, attachment is abandoned.
If one asks how phenomena are profound by nature, he says —
Through the negation of views and so forth, its difficulty of comprehension is declared.

children.text: iti / yasmāt sarvavijñānopalavdhārthanirākaraṇena tasyāḥ prakṛterdurbodhatā kathitā, atastasyā gāmbhīryam / kathaṃ punarevaṃ durbodhatetyāha -
children.translated_text: Thus, since the difficulty of comprehending that nature is stated through the elimination of objects apprehended by all forms of consciousness, therefore its profundity exists. If one asks how it is thus difficult to comprehend, he says —
Because it is not cognized through form and the rest, its inconceivability is maintained. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.6]

children.text: rūpādyāveṇikabuddhadharmādyākāraiḥ prakṛtestathatāsvābhāvyādanabhisambodhena yasmāccintātikrāntatvamiṣyate, ato 'syā durbodhateti yāvat /
children.translated_text: Since through the aspects of form and the rest up to the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities and so forth, due to the absence of own-nature of that nature which is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), because it is not fully realized, its transcendence of thought is maintained — therefore its difficulty of comprehension.
Having thus explained the adversary and the rest, he states the conclusion —

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā yathokto vai jñeyaḥ sarvajñatānate /
children.translated_text: Having done thus, as stated, in the doctrine of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience),
This complete division of the adversary and antidote should be known. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.7]

children.text: iti / sarvajñatādhikāre yathoktanayena yathākramaṃ śrāvakabodhisattvādīnāṃ vipakṣapratipakṣayorayaṃ prabhedo 'vasātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the context of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), this distinction between the adversary and antidote of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and others respectively, as stated in the above manner, should be ascertained.
7 - Practice (<s>prayoga</s>)

children.text: vipakṣādi evamabhidhāya tayorvibhāvanāyāṃ kaḥ prayoga iti cet prayogamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus explained the adversary and the rest, if one asks what is the practice for their cultivation, he states the practice —
Regarding form and the rest, regarding their impermanence and so forth, regarding their fullness and non-fullness,
The practice of conduct regarding their non-attachment is through negation. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.8]

children.text: avikāro na karttā ca prayogo duṣkarastridhā /
children.translated_text: Non-transformation, non-agency, and the threefold difficulty of practice;
The attainment of fruit as appropriate, its fruitfulness, and its approval. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.9]
And that which is not dependent on another, the sevenfold declaration and experience.

children.text: rūpādisarvadharmāḥ, teṣāmevānityatāśūnyatādayaḥ, pratipūrṇāpūrṇatā, asaṅgaḥ, anyathā 'vikāraḥ, akartṛtvam, trisarvajñatātmakānāṃ yathākramaṃ uddeśaprayogakāritrāṇāṃ duṣkaratā, yathābhavyaphalaprāptyā avandhyatā, parapratyayānirgāmitvam, pariṇāmasamāhāra-virodha-pratyaya-asaṅkrānti-nirādhāra-akārakātmaka-saptakhyātisiddhaparijñānasya nirākaraṇam, tadevamanvayamukhena bodhisattvānāṃ daśavidhaḥ prayogaḥ kathitaḥ, arthād yathoktaviparyayeṇa śrāvakādīnāṃ prayogo bhavati /
children.translated_text: All phenomena such as form; their impermanence, emptiness, and the like; their fullness and non-fullness; non-attachment; non-transformation otherwise; non-agency; the difficulty of the three types of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) in terms of enumeration, practice, and function respectively; fruitfulness through the attainment of fruit as appropriate; non-dependence on others for proceeding; and the negation of the sevenfold thorough knowledge established through declaration, whose nature comprises transformation, collection, opposition, condition, non-transference, groundlessness, and non-agency — thus in this manner through the method of positive connection, the tenfold practice of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is stated; by implication, the practice of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others is the reverse of what has been stated.
8 - Equality (<s>samatā</s>)

children.text: samatādvāreṇa prayogo bhāvanīya iti prayogānantaraṃ samatāmāha -
children.translated_text: Since practice should be cultivated through the gateway of equality, he states equality immediately after practice —

children.text: caturdhā 'mananā tasya rūpādau samatā matā // Abhis_3.10 //
children.translated_text: The fourfold non-ideation regarding form and the rest is considered equality. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.10]

Thus, the complete non-apprehension in all respects of clinging to form and the rest, of the elaboration of characteristics such as blue, and of the realization of non-ideation — since this constitutes the equality of practice, it is equality.
9 - The path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>)

children.text: prayogasamatāṃ pratividhya darśanamārgo bhāvanīya iti darśanamārgamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thoroughly understood the equality of practice, since the path of seeing is to be cultivated, he states the path of seeing —
Consisting of the moments of <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of phenomena), <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge), <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Regarding the truth of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) and the rest, this is the path of seeing in the doctrine of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.11]

children.text: iti / pratisatyaṃ dharmajñānakṣāntirdharmajñānamanvayajñānakṣāntiranvayajñānamityevaṃ ṣoḍaśakṣaṇātmakaḥ sarvajñatādhikāre darśanamārgo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, for each truth there is <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of knowledge of phenomena), <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of phenomena), <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge), and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) — in this way, the path of seeing in the context of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) consists of sixteen moments.
Now, if one asks what are the aspects of the truths, he says —
Form is neither permanent nor impermanent, its end is past, it is pure,
Unarisen and unceased and so forth, like space, free from defilement, [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.12]
Liberated from possession, inexpressible by its very nature,

children.text: pravyāhāreṇa nāsyārthaḥ pareṣu prāptaye yataḥ // Abhis_3.13 //
children.translated_text: Its meaning cannot be conveyed to others through verbal expression. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.13]
Non-apprehension produces ultimate purity; the non-arising of disease,
The cessation of lower realms; regarding the direct realization of the fruit, non-conceptuality. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.14]
Non-association with characteristics, regarding things, regarding expressions, regarding both,
And the non-arising of knowledge — these are the moments of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.15]

children.text: naiḥsvābhāvyena rūpādi nityānityaviyogānna nityaṃ nānityam, duḥkhāduḥkhavigamatvena apagataśāśvatocchedāntam, śūnyāśūnyarahitatvād viśuddham, ātmānātmasvabhāvābhāvānnotpannaṃ na niruddhaṃ na saṃkliṣṭaṃ na vyavadātamityādayo duḥkhasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Due to <s>niḥsvabhāvya</s> (absence of own-nature), form and the rest are neither permanent nor impermanent, since they are free from both permanence and impermanence; since they transcend both suffering and non-suffering, they are beyond the extremes of eternalism and annihilationism; since they are free from both emptiness and non-emptiness, they are pure; since the own-nature of both self and non-self is absent, they are unarisen, unceased, undefiled, and unpurified — these and such are the aspects of the truth of suffering.

children.text: hetvahetutucchatvādākāśasadṛśam, samudayāsamudayavisaṃyogāt sarvakleśopakleśanirupaliptam, prabhavāprabhavāsambaddhatvāt parigraheṇa nirmuktam, pratyayāpratyayavimuktatvāt svarūpato 'vacanīyamiti samudayasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Since cause, non-cause, and both are empty, it is like space; since it is free from conjunction with origination and non-origination, it is untainted by all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions; since it is unconnected with arising and non-arising, it is liberated from possession; since it is free from conditions and non-conditions, it is inexpressible in its own nature — these are the aspects of the truth of origination.

children.text: yasmānnirodhānirodhenāsambandhaḥ, tasmānnirodhasatyārtho vacanodāharaṇena santānāntare 'prāpaṇīyaḥ, śāntāśāntābhāvānnopalambhakaraṇam, praṇītāpraṇītavikalatvādatikrāntobhayāntā viśuddhiḥ, niḥsaraṇāniḥsaraṇaviviktatvāt sarvavyādhyanutpāda iti nirodhasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Since there is no connection with cessation and non-cessation, therefore the meaning of the truth of cessation cannot be conveyed to the mental continuum of another through verbal expression and illustration; since both the peaceful and the non-peaceful are absent, there is non-apprehension; since it is deficient in both the sublime and the non-sublime, there is purity transcending both extremes; since it is separated from both escape and non-escape, there is the non-arising of all disease — these are the aspects of the truth of cessation.

children.text: mārgāmārgarahitatvādapāyocchittiḥ, nyāyānyāyāsaṃśleaṣāt phalasākṣātkaraṇaṃ pratyupāyo 'vikalpatvam, pratipattyapratipattivinirmuktatvena sarvadharmāṇāṃ nimittairasaṃsargaḥ, nairyāṇikānairyāṇikavikalpatvenobhaye vācyavācakabhāvalakṣaṇe jñeye śabde jñānasyānutpattiriti mārgasatyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Since it is free from both path and non-path, there is the cessation of lower rebirths; since it is unconnected with both correctness and incorrectness, the direct realization of the fruit is the method of non-conceptuality; since it is liberated from both practice and non-practice, there is the non-association of all phenomena with characteristics; since it is free from the conceptual distinction of both leading-out and non-leading-out, the non-arising of knowledge pertains to both the knowable objects characterized by the expressed and the expressor, and to verbal expression — these are the aspects of the truth of the path.

children.text:
evamete ākārāḥ sarvajñatākṣaṇā iti bodhisattvānāṃ darśamārgaḥ, tadviparyayeṇa śrāvakadīnāmanityādibhirākāraiḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ darśanamārgo vibhāvanīyaḥ /
śrāvakamārgo bodhisattvena parijñātavyo na sākṣātkaraṇīya iti bhāvanāmārgo na nirdiṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Thus these aspects are the moments of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), and this is the path of seeing of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Conversely, the path of seeing in <s>sarvajñatā</s> for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others should be understood through aspects such as impermanence and so forth.
Since the <s>Śrāvaka</s> path is to be thoroughly known by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> but not directly realized, the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) is not set forth here.
Having thus set forth in detail, summarizing the three types of omniscience as encompassing the complete meaning, he says —

children.text: iti seyaṃ punaḥ seyaṃ khalu punastridhā /
children.translated_text: Thus this is again this, and indeed again this is threefold.
The completion of the three chapters is illuminated. [<s>Abhis</s>. 3.16]

children.text: iti / yathoktanītyā iyaṃ sarvākārajñatā, iyaṃ mārgajñatā, iyaṃ sarvajñatā cetyevaṃ parivartatrayeṇa prakāratrayaṃ parisamāptam /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner stated, this is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), this is <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths), and this is <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) — in this way, the three modes are completed through the three chapters.
Thus concludes the commentary on the third chapter of the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Chapter Four: The Realization of All Aspects (<s>Sarvākārābhisambodha</s>)
1 - Aspects (<s>ākāra</s>)

children.text: parijñātatrisarvajñatāvaśitvārthaṃ punaḥ sarvākāramārgavastujñānasaṅgraheṇa trisarvajñatāṃ bhāvayatīti sarvākārābhisambodha ityāha -
children.translated_text: For the purpose of mastery over the three types of omniscience that have been thoroughly known, one again cultivates the three types of omniscience through the collection of knowledge of all aspects, paths, and objects — this is called <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s> (realization of all aspects). He says —
The defining characteristic is that the modes of object-knowledge are aspects.

children.text: sarvajñatānāṃ traividhyāt trividhā eva te matāḥ // Abhis_4.1 //
children.translated_text: Since the types of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) are threefold, those aspects are also considered to be of three kinds. [<s>Abhis</s>. 4.1]

children.text: nityādigrāhavipakṣasya pratipakṣadharmatāsvabhāvānāmanityādyālambanajñānaprakārāṇāmākāratvena vyavasthānaṃ lakṣaṇam / te cākārāstrisarvajñatābhedāt triprakārā eva matāḥ /
children.translated_text: The defining characteristic is the establishment as aspects of the modes of knowledge that take as their objects impermanence and so forth, which are the antidotal properties countering the grasping of permanence and the like. And those aspects are considered to be of three kinds due to the division of the three types of omniscience.
Having indicated the aspects in general, he now states them in particular —
Beginning with the aspect of non-existence, up to the form of immovability,

children.text: catvāraḥ pratisatyaṃ te mārge pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ // Abhis_4.2 //
children.translated_text: Four for each truth, and fifteen for the path are remembered. [<s>Abhis</s>. 4.2]

children.text: iti / tatra trisarvajñatāmadhikṛtya asad-anutpāda-viveka-anavamardanīya-apada-ākāśa-apravyāhāra-anāma-agamana-asaṃhārya-akṣaya-anutpattaya iti dvādaśa ākārā hi yathākramaṃ duḥkhādisatyatrayasya anityādilakṣaṇā bhavanti / kleśāvaraṇapratipakṣatvenaikaḥ anāsravamārgaḥ, sarvajñatayā pratyekabuddhāḥ saṅgṛhītā iti teṣāṃ jñeyāvaraṇapratipakṣatvena dvau sāsravānāsravabhāvanāmārgau ceti mārgāḥ triprakārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding the three types of omniscience, the twelve aspects — non-existence, non-arising, separation, indomitability, non-abode, space, non-expression, namelessness, non-going, immovability, inexhaustibility, and non-arising — are respectively the characteristics of impermanence and so forth for the three truths of suffering and the rest. As the antidote to the obscuration of afflictions, there is one uncontaminated path; since <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are included under <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), as antidotes to the obscuration of the knowable for them, there are two paths — the contaminated and uncontaminated paths of cultivation — thus the paths are of three kinds.

children.text: tatra prathame akārakājānakāsaṃkrāntyavinayākārā iti catvāro yathākramaṃ mārgādilakṣaṇāḥ (kleśāvaraṇapratipakṣe) bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Among these, in the first, the four aspects of non-agency, non-cognition, non-transference, and non-training are respectively the characteristics of the path and so forth, serving as antidotes to the obscuration of afflictions.

children.text: dvitīye svapna-pratiśrutkā-pratibhāsa-māyākārā iti pañca yathākramaṃ niḥsvabhāva-anutpanna-aniruddha-ādiśānta-prakṛtiparinirvṛtilakṣaṇāḥ sāmānyato jñeyāvaraṇapratipakṣabhūtāḥ santi /
children.translated_text: In the second, the five aspects of dream, echo, reflection, illusion, and so forth are respectively characterized as lack of own-nature, unarisen, unceased, primordially peaceful, and naturally <s>parinirvṛta</s> (completely passed beyond suffering), serving in general as antidotes to the obscuration of the knowable.

children.text: tṛtīye asaṃkleśa-avyavadāna-anupalepa-aprapañca-amanana-acalākārāṃ ṣaṭ yathākramaṃ saṃkleśa-vyavadāna-kleśavāsanā-rūpādiprapañca-svādhigama-parihāṇi-vikalpānāṃ pratiniyatajñeyāvaraṇānāṃ pratipakṣabhūtā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: In the third, the six aspects of non-defilement, non-purification, non-staining, non-elaboration, non-ideation, and immovability are respectively antidotes to the specifically determined obscurations of the knowable, namely the conceptual distinctions of defilement, purification, latent tendencies of afflictions, elaboration of form and the rest, one's own realization, and decline.

children.text: ityevaṃ mārgasatyasya pañcadaśa ākārāḥ / samudāyena saptaviṃśatiriti sarvajñatākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus there are fifteen aspects of the truth of the path. In total, there are twenty-seven aspects of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).
Next, he states the aspects of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) —

children.text: hetau mārge ca duḥkhe ca nirodho ca yathākramam /
children.translated_text: Regarding the cause, the path, suffering, and cessation, respectively,

children.text: aṣṭau te sapta pañceti ṣoḍaśeti ca kīrtitāḥ // Abhis_4.3 //
children.translated_text: Eight, seven, five, and sixteen are declared. [<s>Abhis</s>. 4.3]

children.text: tatra saṃkleśetarapakṣāśrayeṇa samudayamārgasatye kāraṇam, duḥkhanirodhasatye ca phalamityarthadvāreṇa nirdiṣṭe samudayamārgaduḥkhanirodhasatyeṣu yathāsaṃkhyamaṣṭādyākārā boddhavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Therein, by way of the two sides of the defiled and the non-defiled, the truth of origination and the truth of the path are stated as cause, and the truth of suffering and the truth of cessation as fruit — thus, having been set forth through the gateway of meaning, the aspects beginning with eight and so forth should be understood in the truths of origination, path, suffering, and cessation respectively.

children.text: tatra virāga-asamutthāna-śānta-arāga-adveṣa-amoha-niḥkleśa-niḥsattvākārā eva yathākramaṃ yo hetuḥ chando rāgo nandī ca, yaḥ samudayaḥ rāgo dveṣo mohaśca, yaḥ prabhavaḥ parikalpaḥ, yaśca pratyayaḥ sattvābhiniveśa iti eteṣāṃ pratipakṣabhūtatvena trayastraya eka eka ityaṣṭāvākārāḥ samudayasatye bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Therein, the aspects of dispassion, non-arising, peace, non-attachment, non-aversion, non-delusion, freedom from defilements, and absence of [grasping at] beings are respectively the antidotes of: whatever is the cause—desire, passion, and delight; whatever is the origin—passion, aversion, and delusion; whatever is the source—conceptual construction; and whatever is the condition—attachment to beings. Being the antidotes of these, three [aspects]—

children.text: apramāṇa-antadvayānanugama-asambhinna-aparāmṛṣṭa-avikalpa-aprameya-asaṅgākārā-yathākramaṃ yaḥ sarvasattvāvakāśado mārgaḥ yathā va sarvasattvāvakāśadaḥ, yo nyāyo yathā ca nyāyaḥ, yā pratipattiryathā ca pratipattiḥ, yacca niryāṇamiti tatsvabhāvā dvau dvau dvāveka iti saptākārā mārgasatye bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The aspects of immeasurability, non-pursuit of the two extremes, non-confusion, non-grasping, non-conceptualization, immeasurability, and non-attachment are respectively [the antidotes of]: whatever path gives opportunity to all beings and however it gives opportunity, whatever is the method and however the method is, whatever is the practice and however the practice is, and whatever is the way out—having those as their nature, two [sets of aspects]—

children.text: anitya-duḥkha-śūnya-anātmākārāḥ pañcamālakṣaṇākārasvabhāvā ityevaṃ pañcākārā duḥkhasatye bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The aspects of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, having as their nature the five unlabeled aspects, are thus five aspects pertaining to the truth of suffering.

children.text: adhyātmabahirdhobhayavastūnāṃ nirodhenādhyātmabahirdhobhayaśūnyatākārāstrayaḥ nirodhākārasvabhāvāḥ, śūnyatāyāṃ bhājanaloke paramārthe saṃskṛte 'saṃskṛte śāśvatocchedānte 'navarāgrasaṃsāre adhigatadharmānavakāre abhiniveśasya prajñaptyātmakasya nirodhena yathākramaṃ śūnyatā-mahat-paramārtha-saṃskṛta-asaṃskṛta-atyanta-anavarāgra-anavakāraśūnyatākārā aṣṭau śāntākārasvabhāvāḥ, praṇītākāraḥ paraparikalpitakārakanirodhena prakṛtiśūnyatākāraḥ, viṣayabhrāntyātmikānāṃ prajñaptilakṣaṇakālabhrāntīnāṃ ca nirodhena sarvadharmasvalakṣaṇānupalambhaśūnyatākārāstrayo niḥsaraṇākārasvabhāvāḥ, svabhāvanirodhena abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatākāra ekaḥ niḥsaraṇākārātmaka ityevaṃ ṣoḍaśākārā nirodhasatye bhavanti / samudāyena ṣaṭtriṃśaditi mārgajñatākārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the cessation of internal, external, and both-internal-and-external objects, the three aspects of internal, external, and both-internal-and-external emptiness, having the nature of cessation-aspects—[pertaining to] emptiness regarding the vessel world, the ultimate, the conditioned, the unconditioned, [avoiding] the extremes of eternalism and annihilation, the beginningless and endless <s>saṃsāra</s>, the non-deterioration of realized <s>dharmas</s>, and the cessation of the designation-natured attachment—
Next, regarding the aspects of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), [the author] says—
"Beginning with the applications of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and ending with the aspects of Buddhahood,

children.text: śiṣyāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ buddhānāṃ ca yathākramam // Abhis_4.4 //
children.translated_text: Of disciples, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s> respectively—"
"Thirty-seven, thirty-four, thirty-nine—these are the accepted [numbers];
According to the threefold division of omniscience, in conformity with the truth of the path."

children.text: smṛtyupasthānamārabhya buddhākāraparyantānāṃ hi trisarvajñatāsaṅgṛhītamārgadvāreṇa sarvākārajñatayā sarveṣāmāryapudgalānāṃ saṅgrahaṇena ca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ saptatriṃśat, bodhisattvānāṃ catustriṃśat, buddhānāṃ triṃśannava ceti matāḥ / tatra sarvajñatāyāmādau catuḥsatyāvatārāya svasāmānyalakṣaṇaparīkṣitakāyavedanācittadharmasmṛtyupasthānākārāścatvāro vastuparīkṣāmārgaḥ / tato 'vatīrṇasya vīryamiti utpannānutpannasya akuśalasya kuśalasya ca yathākramaṃ samyakprahāṇānutpādanārthaṃ vardhana (bhūyobhāva)-utpādanārthaṃ ca hetubhūtavīryātmakāḥ samyakprahāṇākārāścatvāro vyāvasāyikamārgaḥ / vīryavataścittakarmaṇyatāpādanamiti chandavīryacittamīmāṃsāsamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgatarddhipādākārāścatvāraḥ samādhiparikarmamārgaḥ / kṛtacittaparikarmaṇo 'nantaramūṣmamūrdhaprayogaḥ iti ūṣmamūrdhasvabhāvāḥ śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñendriyākārāḥ pañca samyagabhisamayaprāyogikamārgaḥ / adhigatoṣmādeḥ kṣāntyagradharmaprayoga iti kṣāntyagradharmasvabhāvāḥ śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñābalākārāḥ pañca abhisamayasaṃśleṣamārgaḥ / viditoṣmādicatuṣkasya satyadarśanamārgotpāda iti smṛtidharmapravicayavīryaprītiprasrabdhisamādhyupekṣākārāḥ sapta bodhyaṅgānyabhisamayamārgaḥ / parijñātasatyadarśanasya bhāvanāmārgotpāda iti samyagdṛṣṭisaṃkalpavākkarmāntājīvavyāyāmasmṛtisamādhyāryāṣṭāṅgamārgākārā viśuddhanairyāṇikamārga iti śiṣyāṇāṃ sarvajñatāmārgādhiṣṭhānāḥ saptatriṃśadākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: From the applications of mindfulness up to the aspects of Buddhahood, through the path included in the three types of omniscience, and by the inclusion of all noble persons through <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, respectively: thirty-seven for <s>Śrāvakas</s>, thirty-four for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and thirty-nine for <s>Buddhas</s>—these are the accepted [numbers]. Therein—

children.text: mārgajñatāyāṃ dṛṣṭikṛtapratipakṣaḥ, tannimittavikalpapratipakṣaḥ, traidhātukapraṇidhānapratipakṣaḥ iti tatsvabhāvā yathākramaṃ śūnyānātmākārasvabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ vimokṣamukham, nirodhamārgasatyākārasvabhāvaṃ dvitīyam, anityaduḥkhasamudayasatyākārasvabhāvaṃ tṛtīyamityevaṃ trivimokṣamukhākārāstrayaḥ pratipakṣamārgaḥ /
