children.translated_text: In <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path): the antidote to [wrong] views, the antidote to conceptualization based on those signs, and the antidote to aspirations directed toward the three realms—having these as their nature respectively: the first door of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>) whose nature is the aspects of emptiness and non-self; the second, whose nature is the aspects of cessation and the truth of the path; the third, whose nature is the aspects of impermanence, suffering, and the truth of origination—

children.text: avibhāvitavibhāvitarūpasaṃjñatvād yathākramamadhyātmaṃ rūpyarūpīti bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatītyetau nirmāṇāvaraṇapratipakṣeṇa dvau vimokṣau / śubhāśubharūpanirmāṇe ca yathākramamābhogaḥ prātikūlyañca saṃkleśaḥ tatpratipakṣeṇa śubhaṃ vimokṣamukhaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasampadya viharatītyeko vimokṣa iti vimokṣākārāḥ trayo niryāṇamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the [distinction between] non-developed and developed perception of form, respectively [contemplating] 'having form internally, one sees forms externally' and 'formless internally, one sees forms externally'—these two liberations are antidotes to the obstruction of emanation. Regarding the emanation of beautiful and ugly forms, respectively: effort and adversity are the defilement; as antidote to that, the liberation door of the beautiful, [witnessed] with the body—

children.text: mokṣānukūlavihāramārgasvabhāvāścaturārūpyasamāpattyākārāḥ śāntavihārasvabhāvaḥ saṃjñāveditanirodhākāra eka iti pañcākārā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāramārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: The four formless attainment-aspects, whose nature is the path of abiding conducive to liberation, are the path of peaceful abiding; the single aspect of the cessation of perception and feeling is [one more]—thus five aspects constitute the path of abiding in happiness in this very life.

children.text: caturdhyānārūpyanirodhasamāpatyākārā nava lokottaramārgaḥ / catuḥsatyasaṅgṛhītāḥ kleśavisaṃyogalakṣaṇānantaryamārgākārāścatvāraḥ prahāṇamārgaḥ / dānādipāramitākārā daśa buddhatvamārgaḥ / tadevaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mārgajñatāmārgādhiṣṭhānāścatustriṃśadākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The nine aspects of the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the formless [attainments], and the cessation attainment are the supramundane path. The four aspects of the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), characterized by separation from defilements, included in the four truths, are the path of abandonment. The ten aspects of the <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with giving are the path to Buddhahood. Thus for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the aspects based on the path of <s>mārgajñatā</s> are thirty-four.

children.text: sarvākārajñatākārastu niratiśayatvādeka eva kevalamasādhāraṇamārgaḥ / tatra sthānāsthāna-karmavipākaḥ-nānādhimukti-anekalokadhātu-indriyaparāpara-sarvatragāminī-pratipat-saṃkleśavyavadāna-pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-cyutyupapatti-āsravakṣayajñānabalākārā daśa / buddho 'hamityātmapratijñāne rāgādīnāmantarāyatvākhyāne sarvajñatādimārgasya niryāṇatvaprakāśane kṣīṇāsravatvenātmano 'bhyupagame ca paryanuyokturabhāvena vaiśāradyākārāścatvāraḥ / paryāye dharmalakṣaṇe janapadabhāṣāyāṃ dharmaprabhede ca yathākramaṃ dharmārthaniruktipratibhānapratisaṃvidākārāścatvāraḥ / nāsti skhalitaḥ ravitaṃ muṣitasmṛtirasamāhitaṃ cittaṃ nānātvasaṃjñā apratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā cetyevamākārāḥ ṣaṭ / nāstichandato vīryataḥ smṛtitaḥ samādheḥ prajñāyāḥ vimukteśca parihāṇirityevamākārāḥ ṣaṭ / kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇāṃ jñānapūrvaṅgamānuparivartanākārāstrayaḥ / atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣu asaṅgāpratihatajñānākārāstraya iti aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmākārāḥ / sarvabuddhabhāṣitatathatā-satvadharmavaśavartanasvayambhū-sarvākārābhisambodhibuddhatvākārāḥ trayaśca / ityekonacatvāriṃśadākārāḥ sarvākārajñatāmārgādhiṣṭhānā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The aspect of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) is just one, being unsurpassed—it is solely the uncommon path. Therein, the ten aspects of the powers (<s>bala</s>) are: knowledge of what is possible and impossible, knowledge of the ripening of <s>karma</s>, [knowledge of] various dispositions, various world-realms, the superior and inferior faculties, the path leading everywhere, the practice of defilement and purification, recollection of former lives, passing away and rebirth, and the destruction of the outflows—

children.text: tatrānāsravāḥ sāsravāśca sarvajñatākārā yathākramaṃ śrāvakabodhisattvabhedena / mārgajñatākārāḥ sāsravā eva, bodhisattvānāmatyantakleśāprahāṇāt / anāsravā eva sarvākārajñatākārāḥ sarvathā savāsanasarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇena samyaksambuddhasya sarvadharmavaśavartitvād, ityekatra gaṇyamānaṃ trisaptatyuttaraśatamityākārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>sarvajñatā</s> aspects that are undefiled and defiled respectively correspond to the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Bodhisattva</s> divisions. The <s>mārgajñatā</s> aspects are only defiled [i.e., with outflows], because <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have not utterly abandoned the defilements. The <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> aspects are only undefiled, because the Perfectly Awakened One has abandoned all defilements and cognitive obscurations together with their latencies—

children.text: viśiṣṭaprayogairākārā bhāvayitavyāḥ, te ca prayoktāraṃ vinā kathayitumaśakyā iti śravaṇādibhājanaṃ prayoktāramāha -
children.translated_text: The aspects are to be cultivated through distinguished practices, and those cannot be explained without one who applies them; therefore, [the author] states the practitioner who is the vessel for hearing and the rest—
"Those who have performed service to the <s>Buddhas</s>, who have obtained wholesome roots in their [presence],
Who are guided by good spiritual friends—they are the vessels for hearing this [teaching]."
"Through the practice of attending upon the <s>Buddha</s>, questioning, giving, morality, and the rest,
The status of being a vessel for taking up, retaining, and the rest is considered [proper] for noble ones."

children.text: atītapratyutpannabuddheṣu sāmānyenoptaśodhitaśubhamūlakāḥ, kāyādyupasthānārādhanāt kṛtatathāgataparyupāsanāḥ, kṛtaśaṃkāsthānaparipraśnāḥ, kṛtadānādidaśapāramitāpratipattyanuṣṭhānāḥ, kalyāṇamitrairadhiṣṭhitāśca yathākramamākāralakṣaṇāyā māturasyā granthaśravaṇadhāraṇāmuṣitārthayathānayamanaskārāṇāṃ bhājanaṃ buddhādibhiḥ matamiti /
children.translated_text: Those who have generally planted and purified wholesome roots in the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past and present, who have performed attendance on the <s>Tathāgata</s> through service of body and the rest, who have asked questions about points of doubt, who have practiced the ten <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with giving, and who are supported by spiritual friends—these are respectively [qualified as] vessels for hearing, and so forth, of this treatise on the Mother [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] characterized by aspects—
2 - The Practices (<s>Prayogas</s>)
Having indicated the practitioner, [the author] states the practice—
"From non-establishment in form and the rest; from the prohibition of engagement in them;
From the profundity of their <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); from their unfathomability;
From their immeasurability; from the difficulty and length of time for awakening;
In being predicted and non-retrogressing; in the way out, with and without interval;
In approaching awakening, quickly; in the benefit of others, without increase or decrease;
In the non-seeing of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> and the rest; in the non-seeing of form as inconceivable and the rest;
Non-conceptualizing regarding form and the rest, their signs, and their nature;

children.text: phalaratnapradātā ca śuddhakaḥ sāvadhiśca saḥ // Abhis_4.11 //
children.translated_text: Being a bestower of the jewel of the fruit; a purifier; and one with a limit."

children.text: rūpādiṣu niḥsvabhāvatayā 'navasthānam, ayoga eva teṣu prayogo bhavati, tāveva rūpāditathatāsvarūpatvena gambhīraḥ, duravagāhaḥ, apramāṇaścetyevamabhisambodhānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ rūpādiṣvanavasthānaayogagambhīraduravagāhaapramāṇānīti pañca prayogāḥ / prajñāpāramitāyā uttrāsaanuttrāsasamyagudgrahaṇaāntarāyikadharmavarjanasatatadharmabhāvanā abhinavānāsravadharmādhāratvadharmakāyaphalābhinirvartanadharmacakrapravartanavṛddhi parihāṇyadarśanakāmadhātvanupalambharūpādyacintyākārāmananarūpatannimittatatsva bhāvāvikalpaprathamaphaladarśanarūpaviśuddhisaṃvatsarābhiyogānutsargādipratipattimatāṃ yathākramaṃ mahatkṛcchracirābhisambodhavyākaraṇalābhaavinivartanīyaniryāṇanirantaraāsannābhisambodhakṣiprābhisambodhaparārthaavṛddhyaparihāṇidharmādharmādyanupalambharūpādyacintyākāranirodharūpādibhāvāvikalpaphalaratnadānaviśuddhiavadhiprayogāḥ pañcadaśadhā iti viṃśatiprayogā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Non-establishment in form and the rest through their lack of own-nature; engagement in them is itself non-engagement as practice; those very form-and-the-rest, being the nature of <s>tathatā</s>, are profound, unfathomable, and immeasurable—thus the [first five] practices, respectively being non-establishment, non-engagement, profundity, unfathomability, and immeasurability regarding form and the rest, for the [five] awakenings in their respective order, are five practices. The practice—
3 - The Qualities (<s>Guṇas</s>)

children.text: prayogānantaraṃ guṇadarśanapūrvakaṃ sutarāmabhyasyante prayogā iti tadguṇān āha -
children.translated_text: After the practices, since the practices are cultivated even more earnestly after seeing the qualities, [the author] states those qualities—
"The quality is of fourteen kinds, beginning with the destruction of <s>Māra</s>'s power."

children.text: māraśaktivyāghātabuddhasamanvāhārajñātatvabuddhapratyakṣīkaraṇasamyaksambodhyāsannībhāvamahārthatādideśanirūpaṇasarvānāsravadharmaparipūriguṇakathāpuruṣatāabhedyatāasādhāraṇakuśalamūlotpattipratijñāyāthārthyasampādanaudāraphalaparigrahaṇasattvārthapratipattiniyatilābhā - iti guṇā yathāsaṃkhyaṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānaānubhāvajñānadarśanaṃ - āsannībhāvamahānuśaṃsakṛtyakaraṇapratipakṣadharmaparipūraṇasarvākārajñatākathākathanasānāthyakaraṇamahodāraprītisampādanatatpratijñāvacanānumodanagambhīradharmābhilāṣasattvārthakaraṇaavikalaprajñāpāramitāprāpakā ityetadaviparītaprayogānumodanāt - sattvārthakaraṇa - avikalaprajñāpāramitāprāpakā ityetadaviparītaprayogānumodanāt caturdaśa guṇā utpadyante prāpyante ca /
children.translated_text: The destruction of <s>Māra</s>'s power, the consolation by <s>Buddhas</s>, knowledge of the realized truth, making <s>Buddhas</s> directly perceptible, approaching <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, teaching concerning the great purpose and the rest, the completion of all undefiled <s>dharmas</s>, the discourse on qualities, manhood, indestructibility, the arising of uncommon wholesome roots, the fulfillment of one's vow, the reception of the noble fruit, and the accomplishment of the welfare of beings—
4 - The Faults (<s>Doṣas</s>)

children.text: tadanantaraṃ ke punaḥ prayogāntarāyakarā doṣāḥ, yeṣāṃ parivarjanena prayogā bhāvayitavyā ityantarāyakarān doṣānāha -
children.translated_text: Next, what are the faults that obstruct the practices, by avoiding which the practices are to be cultivated? [The author] states the obstructive faults—
"The faults should be understood as six, together with four sets of ten."

children.text: mahākṛcchraprāptiḥ, atyāśupratibhānatā, kāyadauṣṭhulyam, cittadauṣṭhulyam, ayogavihitasvādhyāyādikam, vaimukhyanimittagrāhitā, hetvabhiniveśabhraṃśaḥ, praṇītāsvādabhraṃśaḥ, sarvathā uttamayānasaṃgrahabhraṃśaḥ, sarvadoddeśabhraṃśa iti prathamaṃ daśakam / hetuphalasambandhabhraṃśaḥ, niruttarabhraṃśaḥ, bahuvidhaviṣayavikalpapratibhānotpādaḥ, akṣaralikhanābhiniveśaḥ, abhāvābhiniveśaḥ, akṣarābhiniveśaḥ, anakṣarābhiniveśaḥ, janapadādimanaskāraḥ, lābhasatkāraślokāsvādanam, amārgopāyakauśalamārgaṇamiti dvitīyaṃ daśakam /
children.translated_text: encountering great difficulty, excessively quick understanding, physical rigidity (<s>kāyadauṣṭhulya</s>), mental rigidity (<s>cittadauṣṭhulya</s>), improperly performed self-study and the like, grasping at signs due to aversion, lapse from adherence to the cause, lapse from the taste of what is excellent, total lapse from the embrace of the supreme vehicle, and lapse from instruction in every situation — this is the first group of ten. Lapse from the connection of cause and effect, lapse from what has no superior, the arising of understanding of manifold conceptualizations of objects, clinging to writing syllables, clinging to non-existence, clinging to syllables, clinging to non-syllables, mental preoccupation with countries and the like, relishing gain, honor, and fame, and searching for the path of unskillful means on a non-path — this is the second group of ten.

children.text: yathāsaṃkhyaṃ śrotāvaktroḥ pūrvāparayoḥ kasyacidabhisambandhena chandakilāsavaidhuryam, chandaviṣayabhedavaidhuryam, alpecchatānalpecchatāvaidhuryam, dhūtaguṇayogāyogau, kalyāṇākalyāṇadharmatvam, tyāgamātsaryam, dānāgrahaṇam, uddhaṭitajñavipañcitajñatvam, sūtrādidharmābhijñānabhijñatvam, ṣaṭpāramitāsamanvāgamāsamanvāgamāviti tṛtīyaṃ daśakam /
children.translated_text: In due order, through some connection between the earlier and later of the listener and speaker [respectively]: divergence through disposition, indolence, or confusion; divergence regarding the differentiation of objects of interest; divergence regarding desiring little and not desiring little; engagement and non-engagement in the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities); having wholesome or unwholesome qualities; generosity and avarice; giving and non-acceptance of gifts; being an intuitive knower or an analytical knower; knowing and not knowing the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>sūtras</s> and the like; possession and non-possession of the six <s>pāramitās</s> — this is the third group of ten.

children.text: tathaiva upāyānupāyakauśale, dhāraṇīpratilambhāpratilambhau, likhitukāmatā'likhitukāmate, vigatāvigatakāmacchandatve ceti catvāri; apāyagativaimukhyam, sugatigamanasaumanasyamiti dve; yathāsaṃkhyaṃ śrotāvaktroḥ pūrvāparayoḥ kasyacidabhisambandhena ekākiparṣadabhiratiḥ, anubandhakāmānavakāśadānatvam, āmiṣakiñcitkābhilāṣatadadātukāmatā, sadasajjīvitāntarāyadiggamanamiti catvāri ca caturthaṃ daśakam /
children.translated_text: Likewise: skill and lack of skill in means, obtaining and not obtaining <s>dhāraṇī</s>, desiring and not desiring to write, and being with and without desire for sensual pleasures — [these are] four. Aversion to the realms of miserable existence, and joy at going to the happy realms — [these are] two. In due order, through some connection between the earlier and later of the listener and speaker: delight in solitude or in an assembly, giving and not giving opportunity to those who wish to follow, longing for some material thing and desiring to give that, and going in a direction where there is safety or danger to life — [these are] four. This is the fourth group of ten.

children.text: tathaiva durbhikṣadiggamanāgamanam, caurādyākulitadiggamanāgamanam, kulāvalokanadaurmanasyamiti trīṇi; mārabhedaprayogaḥ, prativarṇikopasaṃhāraḥ, ayathāviṣaya-spṛhotpādanamiti aparāṇi trīṇi / ityevaṃ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśaddoṣā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Likewise: going to and coming from a direction of famine, going to and coming from a direction disturbed by thieves and the like, and despondency from visiting families — [these are] three. The stratagem of <s>Māra</s>'s division, the misleading attraction of a counterfeit [teacher], and the arousing of longing for inappropriate objects — [these are] another three. Thus there are forty-six faults.
5 — Characteristics (<s>Lakṣaṇas</s>)

children.text: doṣānantaraṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ guṇadoṣādānatyāgena prayogā bhāvanīyā lakṣaṇajñāna pūrvakamiti teṣāṃ lakṣaṇamāha -
children.translated_text: After the faults, the practices are to be cultivated through the adoption and abandonment of virtues and faults in due order, preceded by knowledge of their characteristics. Thus he states the characteristics of those —

children.text: lakṣyate yena tajjñeyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: That by which something is characterized should be known as the characteristic; and it is threefold:

children.text: jñānaṃ viśeṣa kāritraṃ svabhāvo yaśca lakṣyate // Abhis_4.13 //
children.translated_text: knowledge, specific function (<s>kāritra</s>), and the own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) that is characterized. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.13//

children.text: prayogāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ karaṇasādhanaparigraheṇa jñānaviśeṣakāritrasvarūpam, karmasādhanaparigraheṇa ca svabhāvātmakamiti lakṣaṇaṃ caturvidhaṃ boddhavyam /
children.translated_text: The characteristic of the practices, taking the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) as the means, is the specific function of knowledge as its nature; and taking the object (<s>karman</s>) as the means, it is of the nature of own-nature — thus the characteristic should be understood as fourfold.

children.text: tatra tāvat jñānalakṣaṇaṃ trisarvajñatābhedena bhidyamānaṃ sarvajñatādvāreṇāha -
children.translated_text: Therein, first, the knowledge-characteristic, being divided by the three types of omniscience, is stated through the door of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) —
In the cessation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and in the world whose nature is non-disintegration,
in the mental activities of beings, in their contraction, in their going outward, //<s>Abhis</s> 4.14//
in the aspect of inexhaustibility, in the expanded [minds] with attachment and so forth,
in [minds that are] vast, immeasurable, and in consciousness that is without indication, //<s>Abhis</s> 4.15//
in the knowledge of invisible mind — that designated as the winking and the like [of mind];
furthermore, by the aspect of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the knowledge of those [minds] is beyond [the ordinary]. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.16//
In the <s>tathatā</s>, the awakening of the sage, the exposition concerning that —
this is the collection of the knowledge-characteristic under the topic of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). //<s>Abhis</s> 4.17//

children.text: tathāgatanirvṛttilokālujyatāsattvacittacaritacittasaṃkṣepacittavikṣepacittākṣayākārasarāgādicittaādiśabdasaṅgṛhītavigatarāgacittavipulacittamahadgatacittaapramāṇacittaanidarśanacittaḥadṛśacittacittonmiñjitādiunmiñjitāditathatākāratathāgatatathatāvabodhatatparasamākhyānaprajñapanañcetyebhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ jñānākāraprakāraiḥ yathānayaṃ sarvajñatāprayogāḥ samyag lakṣyanta iti jñānalakṣaṇaṃ sarvajñatayā saṅgṛhītam /
children.translated_text: By these sixteen types of knowledge-aspects — the cessation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the non-disintegration of the world, the mental activities of beings, the contraction of mind, the distraction of mind, the aspect of inexhaustibility of mind, the mind with attachment and so forth (the word 'and so forth' includes the mind free from attachment), the vast mind, the exalted mind, the immeasurable mind, the mind without indication, the invisible mind, the winking and the like of mind, the aspect of <s>tathatā</s>, the awakening of the <s>Tathāgata</s> to <s>tathatā</s>, and the exposition and designation concerning that — by these, the practices of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) are properly characterized. Thus the knowledge-characteristic is collected under omniscience.
Next, under the topic of path-knowledge (<s>mārgajñatā</s>), he states —
In emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), in the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), and in what is devoid of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>),
in non-arising and non-cessation and the like, in the non-disturbance of the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>), //<s>Abhis</s> 4.18//
in the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskāra</s>), in non-conceptualization, in differentiation and characteristiclessness —
the knowledge-characteristic is accepted under the topic of path-knowledge (<s>mārgajñatā</s>). //<s>Abhis</s> 4.19//

children.text: śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānutpādānirodhātmakāni / ādiśabdena asaṃkleśāvyavadānābhāvasvabhāvāniśritākāśalakṣaṇāni etāni ṣaṭ saṅgṛhītāni / dharmatā 'vikopanāsaṃskārāvikalpaprabhedālakṣaṇāni cetyebhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ jñānākāraprakāraiḥ yathāvat mārgajñatāprayogā lakṣyanta iti jñānalakṣaṇaṃ mārgajñatāsaṅgṛhītam /
children.translated_text: Emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-arising, non-cessation — by nature these [are five]; by the word 'and the like,' non-defilement, non-purification, non-existence, own-nature, non-dependence, and space-like characteristiclessness — these six are included. The non-disturbance of the nature of reality, the unconditioned, non-conceptualization, differentiation, and characteristiclessness — by these sixteen types of knowledge-aspects, the practices of path-knowledge (<s>mārgajñatā</s>) are properly characterized. Thus the knowledge-characteristic is collected under path-knowledge.
Next, through the door of knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), he states —
Relying on one's own <s>dharmas</s>, in the practice of the abode, in honoring it,
in holding it in esteem, in reverence, in worship of that, and in being unpretentious — //<s>Abhis</s> 4.20//
knowledge that operates everywhere, that shows what has not been seen,
that indicates, announces, and makes visible the aspect of the emptiness of the world — //<s>Abhis</s> 4.21//
that perceives inconceivable peace, and that extinguishes the designation of the world —
this is declared as the knowledge-characteristic under the method of knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). //<s>Abhis</s> 4.22//

children.text: iti / tathāgatasvadharmopaniśrayavihāra-satkāra-gurukāra-mānanā-pūjanā-akṛta-katva-sarvatraga-adṛṣṭārthadarśaka-lokaśūnyatākāra-lokaśūnyatāsūcakaḥ-lokaśūnyatājñāpaka-lokaśūnyatādarśaka-acintyatādeśanā-śāntatādeśanā-lokanirodha-saṃjñānirodhākhyaiḥ ebhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirjñānākāraprakāraiḥ yathāvat sarvākārajñatāprayogā lakṣyanta iti jñānalakṣaṇaṃ sarvākārajñatāsaṃgṛhītaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: By these sixteen types of knowledge-aspects — reliance on the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s own <s>dharmas</s>, abode, honoring, esteeming, reverencing, worshipping, being unpretentious, pervading everywhere, showing what is unseen, the aspect of emptiness of the world, indicating the emptiness of the world, announcing the emptiness of the world, showing the emptiness of the world, teaching inconceivability, teaching peace, the cessation of the world, and the cessation of designation — by these, the practices of knowledge of all aspects are properly characterized. Thus the knowledge-characteristic is collected under knowledge of all aspects. Thus altogether there are ninety-one characteristics gathered under a single [heading].

children.text: navabhirantaraślokairevaṃ jñānalakṣaṇamabhidhāya jñānākāreṇa paricchinnānāṃ viśeṣo jñeya iti jñānalakṣaṇānantaram antaraślokena viśeṣalakṣaṇamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the knowledge-characteristic in nine intermediate verses, since the distinction of those delimited by knowledge-aspects should be known, after the knowledge-characteristic, [the author] states the distinction-characteristic in an intermediate verse —
Through the distinction of inconceivability and the like, by those distinguished by the domain of [the four] truths,
the distinction-characteristic is stated through six and ten moments. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.23//

By the sixteen moments of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge, conformity-knowledge, patience, and knowledge-moments — distinguished by distinctions of inconceivability, incomparability, and the like — having the domain of the truths of suffering and the like, the practices of path-knowledge and the like are characterized. Thus [there is] the distinction-characteristic.
What then is the distinction of inconceivability and the like? He states [this] in three intermediate verses —
Inconceivability, incomparability, the transcendence of what is to be measured and of number,
inclusion of all Noble Ones, being knowable by the wise, and knowledge of the uncommon; //<s>Abhis</s> 4.24//
swift knowledge, and neither deficiency nor excess; attainment and accomplishment;
a shared object of support, completeness, and full embrace; //<s>Abhis</s> 4.25//
and non-relishing — this distinction, sixteenfold in nature, should be known;
it is the distinction-path by which it is distinguished from other paths. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.26//

children.text: iti / samyaksambuddhādeḥ susaṃgṛhītaprajñābalena acintyatā, atulyatā, prameyasamatikramaḥ, saṃkhyeyasamatikramaḥ, sarvāryapudgalasaṃgrahaḥ, vijñapuruṣavedanīyatā, śrāvakādyagocaravastuparijñānam, svamatāpekṣakṣiprābhijñatājñānam, saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyāśritasarvadharmānyūnāpūrṇatā, trimaṇḍalaviśuddhadānādiṣaṭpāramitāpratipattiḥ, samyakprayogenānekakalpeṣu āsāditapuṇyajñānasamudāgamau, avikalpena sarvadharmālambanam, dharmadhātusvabhāvabodhisattvādhāraḥ, praṇidhānādiṣaṭpāramitāparisamāptihetusambhāraḥ, kalyāṇamitropāyena saṃparigrahaḥ, abhiniveśānāsvāda iti ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ yathākramaṃ duḥkhādisatyakṣaṇānāṃ viśeṣaḥ, yena śrāvakādimārgebhyo bodhisattvādīnāṃ mārgajñatādidvaye viśeṣamārgo viśiṣyate / atasteṣāṃ yathoktaviśeṣavikalo 'bhiniveśādyutpādanalakṣaṇatvena sugamatvānnoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the power of the well-collected wisdom of a Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddha</s> and the like: inconceivability, incomparability, transcendence of what is measurable, transcendence of what is numerable, inclusion of all Noble Persons, being experienceable by the wise, comprehension of objects inaccessible to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like, knowledge of swift supernormal knowledge in accordance with one's own doctrine, neither deficiency nor excess of all <s>dharmas</s> based on conventional and ultimate truth, practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with generosity purified in three spheres, the accomplishments of merit and knowledge attained over many aeons through correct practice, non-conceptual apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, being a support for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose nature is the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the cause-accumulation for the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), full embrace by the means of a virtuous spiritual friend, and non-relishing through non-clinging — this sixteenfold [distinction] is, in due order, the distinction of the moments of the truths of suffering and the like, by which the distinction-path of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the like is distinguished from the paths of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like in the two [knowledges] of path-knowledge and the like. Therefore, that which lacks the stated distinction, such as generating clinging and the like, is not stated since it is easily understood as the opposite characteristic.
What is the function of those delimited by the distinction-characteristic? He states the function-characteristic (<s>kāritralakṣaṇa</s>) in two intermediate verses —

children.text: hitaṃ sukhaṃ ca trāṇaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: Benefit, happiness, protection, refuge, resting-place for people,

children.text: parāyaṇa ca dvīpaṃ ca pariṇāyakasaṃjñakam // Abhis_4.27 //
children.translated_text: final resort, island, and that designated as guide — //<s>Abhis</s> 4.27//
effortless (<s>anābhoga</s>), the direct realization of the fruits of the three vehicles —
this last, the destination-function, is the function-characteristic. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.28//

children.text: iti / anāgatahita-aihikasukhaḥ-duḥkharahitāvipākadharmatopasthāpanārthena hitāditrayaṃ sarvajñatākāritram / ātyantikahita-duḥkhahetunivartana-saṃsāranirvāṇa-samatādhigama-svaparārthādhigamādhārabhāva-parārthapratipati-anābhogapravṛttasattvārtha-yānatrayaniryāṇaphalāsākṣātkārā iti yathākālamupasaṃhārārthena śaraṇādīni sapta mārgajñatākāritrāṇi / sarvākārajñatayā sarvadharmadaiśikatvena sarvākārajñatāyā ekameva gatikāritram / kāritrākārairevaṃ yathāvad sarvajñatātrayasya prayogā lakṣyanta iti kāritralakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of establishing the <s>dharmatā</s> of the ripening free from suffering: benefit pertaining to the future, happiness pertaining to this life, and freedom from suffering — these three are the function of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). Ultimate benefit, the removal of the causes of suffering, the attainment of the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being a basis for the attainment of one's own and others' welfare, practice for the benefit of others, effortless (<s>anābhoga</s>) engagement in the welfare of beings, and the direct realization of the fruits of going forth in the three vehicles — these seven, having the sense of progressive summation, are the functions of path-knowledge. The single destination-function of knowledge of all aspects — guiding all <s>dharmas</s> through knowledge of all aspects. Thus, through the function-aspects, the practices of the three omnisciences are properly characterized — this is the function-characteristic.

children.text: kāritralakṣaṇenāvacchinnānāṃ kaḥ svabhāva iti antaraślokatrayeṇa svabhāvalakṣaṇamāha -
children.translated_text: What is the own-nature of those delimited by the function-characteristic? He states the own-nature-characteristic in three intermediate verses —
The separation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), their signs, and their causes,
of the opponents and their antidotes — difficult deeds, exclusive devotion, instruction with non-apprehension; //<s>Abhis</s> 4.29//
the prohibition of clinging, and that designated as the object of support;
counter-teaching, non-obstruction, being without foundation, without destination, and without birth; //<s>Abhis</s> 4.30//
and non-apprehension of <s>tathatā</s> — the own-nature is sixteenfold;

children.text: lakṣīva lakṣyate ceti caturthaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ matam // Abhis_4.31 //
children.translated_text: it is characterized as if by a mark (<s>lakṣī</s>) — this is considered the fourth characteristic. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.31//

children.text: iti / rāgādikleśa-talliṅgakāyadauṣṭhulya-tannimittāyoniśomanasikārādirāgārāgādivipakṣapratipakṣāṇāṃ śūnyatvena sarvajñatāvivekasvabhāvacatuṣṭayam / paramārthāsatsattvaparinirvāṇaduṣkarakāraka-anyayānāpātalakṣaṇaikāntika-cirasādhyottamoddeśa-bhāvyabhāvakadharmānupalambha-samastabhāvābhiniveśaniṣedhā ityete pañca mārgajñatāsvabhāvāḥ / sarvajñatāmārgajñatāsaṅgṛhītavastuviśeṣālambanam, lokapratipattigrahaṇādiviparītanirdeśāt vipratyayaḥ, rūpādyavighātijñānam, jñānajñeyānupalambhena apratiṣṭham, tathatayā agatiḥ, rūpādiniḥsvabhāvatvena ajātikaḥ, bhāvābhāvādisvabhāvatrayānupalambha iti ete sarvākārajñatāyāḥ sapta svabhāvāḥ / ityevaṃ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ svabhāvairyathāvat trisarvajñatāprayogā lakṣīva lakṣyante iti caturthaṃ svabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ matam / ityevaṃ sāmānyena ekatra kṛtāni ekanavatiḥ lakṣaṇāni bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The four own-natures of omniscience consist in the separation, through emptiness, of the <s>kleśas</s> such as attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, their signs [namely] physical rigidity, their causes [namely] improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>) and the like, and the opponents and antidotes such as attachment, non-attachment, and the like. The five own-natures of path-knowledge are: performing what is difficult to do [namely] the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of beings who are ultimately non-existent; exclusive devotion to the characteristic not [shared by] other vehicles; instruction that is long to be accomplished and supreme, with non-apprehension of both the object of cultivation and the cultivator; the prohibition of clinging to all existents. The seven own-natures of knowledge of all aspects are: the object of support that is the specific objects collected under omniscience and path-knowledge; counter-teaching [i.e.] instruction contrary to the worldly view of practice and so forth; knowledge that does not obstruct form and the like; being without foundation through non-apprehension of both knowledge and the knowable; without destination through <s>tathatā</s>; without birth through the lack of own-nature of form and the like; and non-apprehension of the triple own-nature of existence, non-existence, and the like. Thus, by these sixteen own-natures, the practices of the three omnisciences are properly characterized as if by a mark — this fourth own-nature-characteristic is accepted. Thus, altogether, ninety-one characteristics are made under a single [heading].
6 — The Roots of Virtue Conducive to Liberation (<s>Mokṣabhāgīya</s>)
Since the comprehension of the aforementioned practices belongs only to one who possesses roots of virtue conducive to liberation, [the author] states the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> —
Skill in the accomplishment of generosity and the like with a signless (<s>animitta</s>) [orientation] —
this is accepted as conducive to liberation in this awakening to all aspects. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.32//

children.text: iti / animittālambanajñānākāreṇa dānādipāramitā ārabhya sarvākārajñatāparyantaṃ svasantāne samudāgame kauśalamevāsmin sarvākārābhisambodhe mokṣabhāgīyamiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Skill in the accomplishment within one's own continuum — with the aspect of knowledge having a signless object of support — from the <s>pāramitā</s> of generosity and the like up to knowledge of all aspects, is accepted as conducive to liberation in this awakening to all aspects.
Furthermore, what is that skill? To show that, he states two intermediate verses —
Faith with <s>Buddhas</s> and the like as its object; vigor with generosity and the like as its domain;
mindfulness as the attainment of [pure] disposition; <s>samādhi</s> as non-conceptualization; //<s>Abhis</s> 4.33//
and wisdom as knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects — [thus] fivefold;
with sharp [faculties], awakening is easy to attain; with dull [faculties], it is considered difficult to attain. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.34//

children.text: iti / anindriyasvabhāvāḥ śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiviśiṣṭaprajñāḥ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ buddha-dāna-āśayasampatti-avikalpa-sarvadharmasarvākāraparijñādiṣu pañcavidhaviṣayeṣu kauśalam / evamapi na sarvairanuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ prāpyā / dharmateyaṃ yato 'dhimātraiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ samyaksambodhiḥ subodhā, mṛdubhistaireva durbodhetyarthādidamākṣiptam / madhyaiḥ pratyekabuddhabodhirmṛdubhiḥ śrāvakabodhiścādhigamyata iti //
children.translated_text: The non-faculty natures of faith, vigor, mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s>, and distinguished wisdom constitute skill in five types of domains, respectively: <s>Buddhas</s>; generosity [and the like]; attainment of [pure] disposition; non-conceptualization; and comprehension of all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects. Even so, not all attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. This is the nature of things, since with intense [faculties] of faith and the like, perfect awakening is easy to attain, and with dull ones, it is difficult — this is implicitly suggested. With moderate [faculties], <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-awakening is attained; with dull [faculties], <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening is attained.
7 — The Roots of Virtue Conducive to Penetration (<s>Nirvedhabhāgīya</s>)
For one in whom the roots conducive to liberation have arisen and who is diligent, the roots conducive to penetration arise — thus he states —
Here, all beings are declared to be the object of support of the <s>ūṣma</s> (heat) [stage];
the aspect [of heat], beginning with equanimity of mind, is stated tenfold with respect to them. //<s>Abhis</s> 4.35//
For one who has himself turned away from evil, and who abides in generosity and the like —
the enjoining of others to those [virtues], and conformity with praise [of those virtues]; //<s>Abhis</s> 4.36//
The summit (<s>mūrdhagata</s>), which is the support of self and others, truth-knowledge, and likewise patience (<s>kṣamā</s>) —
Likewise, the supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>agradharmā</s>) should be known through the ripening and other [activities] for beings. (Abhis 4.37)

children.text: iti / asyāṃ sarvākārābhisambodhau samamaitrahitāpratighāviheṭhanācittākāraiḥ pañcabhirmātāpitṛcittabhrātṛbhaginīcittaputraduhitṛcittamitrāmātyacittajñātisālohitacittākāraiḥ ānyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ sattvālambane ūṣmagatimiṣyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: In this full realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisamaya</s>), the heat stage (<s>ūṣmagati</s>) with regard to beings as object is intended through five aspects—the mental aspects of equanimity, friendliness, beneficence, non-hostility, non-harming, and non-agitation—and through another five aspects—the mental aspects of [regarding beings as] mother, father, mind-siblings, sons and daughters, friends and counselors, and kinsmen and blood-relatives.

children.text: saṃkṣepato 'kuśalakuśalayoryathāsaṃkhyaṃ hānopādānābhyāṃ svayaṃ nivṛttasya pravṛttasya ca, taddvārā anyeṣāṃ pāpānnivartanaṃ kuśale ca pravartanamiti dvāvākārau / tathaiva anyeṣāṃ svayampravṛttau varṇavādo 'nukūlatā ceti dharmaprabhedadvaividhyena hi anantākārā iti sattvālambane mūrdhagato bhavati /
children.translated_text: In brief, with respect to the unwholesome and wholesome respectively, through abandonment and adoption, for oneself who has ceased and engaged, and through that, turning others away from evil and engaging them in virtue—these are two aspects. Likewise, in the self-engagement of others, praising and being favorable—through the twofold division of <s>dharma</s> categories, [the aspects] are indeed innumerable. Thus one is at the peak stage (<s>mūrdhagata</s>) with regard to beings as object.

children.text: yathā mūrdhagate svaparādhiṣṭhānabhedena ālambanākārāḥ, tathā niyojanavarṇavādānukūlatādyākāraiḥ svaparādhiṣṭhānaduḥkhādisatyeṣvālambanameva kṣāntirbhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as at the peak stage there are object-aspects through the distinction of one's own and others' empowerment, so too through the aspects of directing, praising, being favorable, and so forth, the patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) consists precisely in taking as object the truths of suffering and the rest with respect to one's own and others' empowerment.

children.text: pūrvavat svaparādhiṣṭhānapācanamocanādyākāraiḥ sattvālambanameva agradharmā bhavantītyevaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: As before, through the aspects of one's own and others' empowerment in ripening, liberating, and the rest, the supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>agradharmā</s>) consist precisely in taking beings as object. Thus the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) arise.

children.text: sarvākāramārgavastuvibhāvanābhedena yathākramaṃ sarvākārajñatāditrividhe 'bhisamaye laukikanirvedhabhāgīyādhigamapūrvako lokottaradarśanabhāvanāmārgādhigamaḥ / sarvākārābhisambodhādau tu trividhe 'bhisamaye bhāvanottarottarāvasthāviśeṣeṇa sarvākāraviśeṣamārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ jñānamanāsravaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrakrameṇotpadyata iti sakṛdutpattinirāsāya nirvedhabhāgīyādivyapadeśo 'bhihita iti veditavyam /
children.translated_text: Through the distinction of cultivating the objects of the path in all aspects, in the threefold realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) beginning with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> and the rest in sequence, the attainment of the supramundane paths of seeing and cultivation is preceded by the attainment of the worldly aids to penetration. But in the full realization of all aspects and the rest, in the threefold realization, through the special distinction of progressively higher stages of cultivation, undefiled knowledge encompassed by the path of all-aspect distinction arises in the sequence of mild, middling, and intense. To refute [the notion of] single arising, the designation 'aids to penetration' and so forth has been stated—this should be understood.
8 - The Non-retrogressing Assembly (<s>Avaivartika-gaṇa</s>)

Since the aids to penetration as described arise for the assembly of non-retrogressing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [the author] states the characteristics of the non-retrogressing <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly—
"Taking up the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhāṅga</s>), on the paths of seeing and cultivation,

children.text: ye bodhisattvā vartante so 'trāvaivartiko gaṇaḥ // Abhis_4.38 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who abide—they are here the non-retrogressing assembly." (Abhis 4.38)

children.text: iti / ye vīrāḥ caturṣu nirvedhabhāgīyeṣu vakṣyamāṇadarśanamārgabhāvanāmārgayoḥ tattadadhigamanayena sthitāḥ, te eva avaivartikaśaikṣyabodhisattvasaṃghā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Those heroes who abide in the four aids to penetration by the method of realizing the respective [objects] on the paths of seeing and cultivation to be described—they themselves are the assemblies of non-retrogressing trainee <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

children.text: kiñca teṣāmāveṇikalakṣaṇamiti cet tāvadekena antaraślokena nirvedhabhāgīyasthitānāṃ lakṣaṇamāha -
children.translated_text: Furthermore, if one asks what their distinctive characteristics are—first, [the author] states in one intervening verse the characteristics of those established in the aids to penetration—
"Through signs such as turning away from form and the rest, twenty in number,
this is the characteristic of the non-retrogressing one established in the aids to penetration." (Abhis 4.39)

Thus: Through twenty types of aspects such as turning away from form and the rest, freedom from doubt, and so on, the non-retrogressing characteristic of those established in the aids to penetration should be known.

children.text: kāni ca nivṛttyāderlakṣaṇāni iti cet ṣaḍbhiḥ antaraślokaiḥ pratipādayitumāha -
children.translated_text: If one asks what the characteristics beginning with 'turning away' are—[the author] undertakes to explain them in six intervening verses—
"Turning away from form and the rest, the destruction of doubt and [inauspicious] moments,
oneself being established in virtue, directing others to that same [virtue]; (Abhis 4.40)
supporting others in giving and the rest, non-longing even for profound meaning,
friendliness, non-association of body and the rest, and with the fivefold obstruction; (Abhis 4.41)
abandonment of all latent tendencies, mindfulness and clear comprehension, purity
of robes and the rest, and in the body the non-arising of worms; (Abhis 4.42)
non-crookedness of mind, adoption of the ascetic practices (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>), freedom from miserliness and the rest,
proceeding in accordance with <s>dharmatā</s>, aspiring for hell for the sake of the world; (Abhis 4.43)
not being led astray by others, recognizing <s>Māra</s> who teaches a different path

children.text: māra ityeva bodhaśca caryā buddhānumoditā // Abhis_4.44 //
children.translated_text: as '<s>Māra</s>' itself, and conduct approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>; (Abhis 4.44)
established in the heat, peak, patience, and supreme <s>dharma</s> stages,
through these twenty signs, one does not retrogress from awakening." (Abhis 4.45)

children.text: iti / asvabhāvatvād rūpādidharmebhyo nivṛttiḥ, avetya prasādalābhena vicikitsākṣayaḥ, praṇidhānasamṛddhyā mithyādṛṣṭi-naraka-preta-tiryagupapatti-buddhavacanā-śravaṇa-pratyantajanapadotpāda-indriyavaikalyajaḍamūkabhāva-dīrghāyuṣkadevopapattītyaṣṭā-kṣaṇakṣayaḥ, kāruṇikatayā svaparakuśaladharmaniyojanam, parātmaparivarttakatvena parasattvaviṣayapariṇāmitadānādiḥ, samyagdharmāvabodhena gambhīradharmārthākāṃkṣaṇam, parahitapratipannatvena maitrakāyavāṅmanaskarma, prayogasampattyā kāmacchando vyāpādaḥ styānamiddhamauddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ vicikitsā ceti pañcanīvaraṇairasaṃvāsaḥ, vibhāvitapratipakṣatvena avidyādisarvānuśayavidhvaṃsaḥ, nityasamāhitatvena smṛtisamprajñānayogaḥ, caukṣasamudācāratvena śuciparibhogyacīvarādīti ekādaśa ākārāḥ / sarvalokābhyupagatakuśalamūlatvena kāye aśītikṛmikulasahasrāsambhavaḥ, kuśalamūlaviśuddhyā cittākauṭilyam, lābhasatkārādinirapekṣatvena pāṃśukūlikatvādidhūtaguṇasamādānam, dānādiviśeṣapratipatipattyā tadvipakṣamātsaryabhraṣṭaśīlāderabhāvaḥ, sarvadharmasaṃgrahād dharmatā 'viruddhaprajñāpāramitāyogagamanam, svātmīkṛtasattvadhātutvena parārthanarakābhilāṣa iti ṣaḍākārāḥ / adhigatasampratyayadharmatvena aparapraṇayanam, viditabuddhatvopāyakauśalatvena pratirūpamārgopadekamārasya māratvāvabodhaśceti dvāvākārau / trimaṇḍalaviśuddhyā sarvāsu caryāsu buddhānumoditatvamiti eva ākāraḥ / yathākramaṃ ūṣmamūrdhakṣāntyagradharmeṣvavasthito bodhisattvo 'nuttarabodherna nivartata iti ebhirviṃśatiliṅgairvijñeyam /
children.translated_text: Thus: Turning away from <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the rest due to their lack of own-nature; destruction of doubt through gaining irreversible faith; destruction of the eight inauspicious moments—birth in [a realm of] wrong views, hells, hungry ghosts, animals, not hearing the <s>Buddha</s>'s word, birth in a border region, deficiency of faculties, dullness and muteness, and birth as a long-lived god—through the fulfillment of aspirations; directing oneself and others to wholesome <s>dharmas</s> through compassion; giving and the rest dedicated to other beings through the exchange of self and other; non-longing for the meaning of profound <s>dharmas</s> through correct understanding of the <s>Dharma</s>; friendly actions of body, speech, and mind through being engaged in the benefit of others; non-association with the five hindrances—sensual desire, ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, restlessness-and-remorse, and doubt—through perfection of practice; destruction of all latent tendencies beginning with ignorance through having cultivated the antidotes; the practice of mindfulness and clear comprehension through being always concentrated; purity of robes and the rest to be enjoyed through refined conduct—these are eleven aspects. Non-arising of eighty thousand families of worms in the body through wholesome roots accepted by the entire world; non-crookedness of mind through purification of wholesome roots; adoption of the ascetic qualities such as wearing discarded rags through being indifferent to gain, honor, and the rest; the absence of miserliness, broken morality, and the rest through the distinguished practice of giving and the rest; proceeding in accordance with <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> practice that is not contrary to <s>dharmatā</s> through comprehending all <s>dharmas</s>; aspiring for hell for the sake of others through having made the realm of beings one's own—these are six aspects. Not being led by others through having realized the <s>dharmas</s> of verified confidence; recognizing as <s>Māra</s> the <s>Māra</s> who teaches a counterfeit path through knowing the skillful means of Buddhahood—these are two aspects. Through the purity of the three spheres, being approved by the <s>Buddhas</s> in all conduct—this is one aspect. In sequence, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the heat, peak, patience, and supreme <s>dharma</s> stages does not retrogress from unsurpassed awakening—this should be known through these twenty signs.
After the non-retrogression characteristics of the aids to penetration, [the author] states in one intervening verse the non-retrogression characteristics of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>)—

children.text: kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ ṣaṭ ca pañca pañca ca dṛkpathe /
children.translated_text: "Six moments of patience and knowledge, and five and five on the path of seeing—
this should be known as the non-retrogression characteristic of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>." (Abhis 4.46)

children.text: iti / duḥkhādisatyadvārā dharmānvayajñānakṣāntyādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ darśanamārgasthabodhisattvasyāvaivartikalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus: The sixteen moments beginning with <s>dharma</s>-knowledge-patience (<s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>) and the rest, through the door of the truths of suffering and the rest, are the non-retrogression characteristic of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the path of seeing.
If one asks what the characteristics of these moment-aspects are—[the author] states the aspects in five intervening verses—
"Turning away from the perception of form and the rest, firmness of mind regarding the lesser
vehicles, turning away [from them], and the exhaustion of the factors of <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest; (Abhis 4.47)
lightness of body and mind, and the approach to sense-enjoyment,
perpetual <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and the purification of livelihood; (Abhis 4.48)
regarding the aggregates and the rest, regarding obstacles, regarding the accumulations beginning with the faculties,

children.text: samare matsarādau ca neti yogānuyogayoḥ // Abhis_4.49 //
children.translated_text: regarding the battle against miserliness and the rest—'no' in the practices and engagements; (Abhis 4.49)
prohibition of [ordinary] abiding, non-apprehension of even an atom of <s>dharma</s>,
certainty regarding one's own stage, and establishment in the three stages; (Abhis 4.50)
sacrificing one's life for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>—these are the sixteen moments,
the signs of non-retrogression of the wise one established on the path of seeing." (Abhis 4.51)

children.text: iti / svalakṣaṇaśūnyatayā rūpādidharmāvabodhavyāvartanam, buddhāderadhiṣṭhānena anuttarabodhicittadṛḍhatā, mahāyānaviśeṣadharmapratipattyā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānacittavinivartanam, dharmapravicayasāmarthyād dhyānārūpyasamāpattyādyudayāṅgaparikṣaya iti catvāra eva duḥkhasyākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Understanding <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the rest as empty of own-characteristic is the turning away from the perception of form and the rest; firmness of the mind of unsurpassed <s>bodhicitta</s> through the empowerment of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the rest; turning away from the mind of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles through the practice of the distinctive <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; exhaustion of the arising-factors of <s>dhyāna</s>, formless attainments, and the rest through the power of discernment of <s>dharmas</s>—these four are the aspects of the truth of suffering.

children.text: apagatākuśalatvena kāyacetolāghavam, sattvadamanopāyakauśalasāmarthyena anabhiniveśakāmopabhogaḥ, viṣayādīnavadarśanena sadā brahmacāritvam, satpuruṣadharmatayā samyagupakaraṇājīvaviśuddhatvamiti catvāra eva samudayākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Lightness of body and mind through the absence of unwholesomeness; enjoyment of sense pleasures without attachment through the power of skill in means for taming beings; perpetual <s>brahmacarya</s> through seeing the faults of sense objects and the rest; purity of right livelihood through the nature of a noble person—these four are the aspects of the truth of origination.

children.text: śūnyatāvasthitatvena skandhadhātvāyatanayogānuyogayorakaraṇamityevaṃ yogānuyogavihārapratiṣedhaḥ, nirastavipakṣatvena adhigamāntarāyadharmāṇāṃ pūrvavadyogānuyogavihārapratiṣedhaḥ, parijñātavikalpadoṣatvena bodhisambhāradānādīnāṃ pūrvavat kathāyogānuyogavihārapratiṣedhaḥ, grāhyagrāhakayorheyatvenendriyāśrayanagarādiyuddheṣu pūrvavadyogānuyogavihārapratiṣedha iti catvāro nirodhākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Not engaging in the practice and engagement regarding the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases through abiding in emptiness—thus the prohibition of practice-and-engagement abiding; prohibition of practice-and-engagement abiding regarding the <s>dharmas</s> that obstruct attainment through having eliminated the adversaries, as before; prohibition of speech-practice-and-engagement abiding regarding the giving and the rest of the <s>bodhi</s>-accumulation through having understood the faults of conceptualization; prohibition of practice-and-engagement abiding regarding battles with faculties, supports, cities, and the rest through the rejectability of grasped and grasper—these four are the aspects of the truth of cessation.

children.text: dānādiviśeṣāvabodhena mātsaryadauḥśīlyādiyogānuyogavihārapratiṣedhaḥ, sarvadharmatrivimokṣamukhasvabhāvatvena aṇumātrajñeyadharmānupalambhaḥ, abhisampratyayalābhena trisarvajñatātmakasvabhūmitrayayathāvanniścitāvasthānam, ekāntaniṣṭhatvena sarvākārajñatādidharmārthaṃ jīvitatyāga iti catvāro mārgākārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Prohibition of practice-and-engagement abiding regarding miserliness, immorality, and the rest through understanding the distinctions of giving and the rest; non-apprehension of even an atom of knowable <s>dharma</s> through the nature of all <s>dharmas</s> as the three doors of liberation; certain establishment in one's own stage of the three types of <s>sarvajñatā</s> through gaining verified confidence; sacrificing one's life for the sake of <s>dharmas</s> of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> and the rest through being of single purpose—these four are the aspects of the truth of the path.

children.text: evaṃ kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākāraiḥ samyagadhigatāḥ santo 'nabhiniviṣṭagrāhyagrāhakākāraśuddhalaukikapṛṣṭhacittasaṃgṛhītaṃ svānurūpakāryaṃ rūpādisaṃjñāvyāvartanādikaṃ parapratipattiviṣayaṃ janayantītyato darśanamārgasthāvaivartikabodhisattvalakṣaṇāni bhavanti / adhigamānurūpa eva sarvatra yogināṃ vyavahāraḥ anyatra sattvavinayaprayojanavaśāditi jñāpanāyopacāreṇoktam, anyathā yogisantānapratyātmavedyakṣaṇāḥ kathaṃ parapratipattaye lakṣaṇānīti?
children.translated_text: Thus the sixteen moments of patience and knowledge, having been correctly realized through the sixteen aspects, being pure of the aspects of grasped and grasper that are not grasped at, being encompassed by the worldly subsequent mind (<s>pṛṣṭhacitta</s>), produce their respective appropriate effects such as turning away from the perception of form and the rest, which are objects of others' understanding. Therefore they are the non-retrogression characteristics of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the path of seeing. The conduct of <s>yogins</s> everywhere is in accordance with their realization—except when governed by the purpose of disciplining beings, it is stated figuratively to indicate this. Otherwise, how could moments that are personally experienced by the <s>yogin</s>'s mind-stream be signs for others' understanding?

children.text: tadanantaraṃ satyapi bhāvanāmārgasthāvaivartikalakṣaṇe 'nāgṛhītaviśeṣaṇā viśeṣye buddhirutpadyate ' iti nyāyāt tāvadbhāvanāmārgaṃ viśeṣayannāha -
children.translated_text: After that, although there exist non-retrogression characteristics of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) as well, since 'understanding arises regarding the qualified object when the qualifier has not been apprehended,' [the author] first qualifies the path of cultivation, saying—
"The path of cultivation is profound; profundity is emptiness and the rest;
freedom from the extremes of superimposition and deprecation—that is profundity." (Abhis 4.52)

children.text: iti / śūnyatādike na rūpādikam, na tato 'nyacchūnyatādikamiti yathākramaṃ yā samāropāpavādāntamuktatā, sā śūnyatādergāmbhīryaṃ śūnyatādikamiti gāmbhīryayogād gambhīro 'bhyāsapatha iti /
children.translated_text: Thus: In emptiness and the rest, form and the rest do not [exist], nor is emptiness and the rest something other than those—through the respective freedom from the extremes of superimposition and deprecation, that is the profundity of emptiness and the rest. Being emptiness and the rest, through the connection with profundity, the path of cultivation is profound.
Having indicated the qualifier, [the author] now states the qualified substance—
"Reflection, examination, and meditative absorption—repeated cultivation is the path;

children.text: nirvedhāṅgeṣu dṛṅmārge bhāvanāmārga eva ca // Abhis_4.53 //
children.translated_text: in the aids to penetration, on the path of seeing, and on the path of cultivation itself." (Abhis 4.53)

children.text: iti / śrutacintābhāvanāmayaprajñayā samādhau vā prayogamaulapṛṣṭhabhāvinyā prajñayā yathākramaṃ triṣu nirvedhāṅgādiṣu nirdiṣṭānāmarthānāṃ punaḥ punaścintātulananidhyānāni bhāvanāmārge prābandhikāni bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Through the wisdom born of hearing, thinking, and meditation, or through the wisdom of the preparatory, principal, and subsequent stages in <s>samādhi</s>—respectively, in the three [stages] beginning with the aids to penetration, the repeated reflection, examination, and meditative absorption on the meanings taught [there] are continuous on the path of cultivation.
If one asks how many types it has, [the author] says—
"Being continuous, it is taught as ninefold in type,
through the further division of mild, middling, and intense into mild and the rest." (Abhis 4.54)

children.text: iti / vikalpakleśā bodhisattvā iti kṛtvā yathaudārikañca tamaḥ sūkṣmeṇālokena hanyate sukṣmañcādhimātreṇeti mṛdumadhyādhimātravikalpānāṃ pratyekaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedāt teṣāṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrapratipakṣāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedāt tathā paramārthataḥ śūnyatālakṣaṇākāradvārā vikalpapratipakṣayorbhedād yathāsaṃkhyaṃ kāmadhātvādinavabhūmiṣu navaprakāraḥ prabandhena vartamānaḥ bhāvanāmārgo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus: Since <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have conceptualization and defilements, just as gross darkness is destroyed by subtle light and subtle [darkness] by intense [light], through the division of mild, middling, and intense conceptualizations each into mild, middling, and intense, and [correspondingly] through the division of their mild, middling, and intense antidotes each into mild, middling, and intense—and likewise, ultimately through the distinction of conceptualization and antidote via the aspect of the characteristic of emptiness—the path of cultivation, existing continuously in the nine stages beginning with the desire realm, is of nine types, in respective correspondence.

children.text: tattajjinajananīnāmekaikaṃ prakāramadhikṛtya asaṃkhyeyāprameyāpramāṇapuṇyaprasavavacanād bahudhā bhedāt kathaṃ navaprakāra iti cedāha -
children.translated_text: If one asks how it can be ninefold when, taking each single type of the respective <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [sūtras], the statements of innumerable, immeasurable, and incalculable merit indicate many divisions—[the author] says—
"The designations 'innumerable' and the rest are not tenable in the ultimate sense;
they are the outflow of compassion, accepted by the Sage in the conventional sense." (Abhis 4.55)

children.text: iti / asaṃkhyeyāprameyāpramāṇanirdeśā vāgabhilāpasvabhāvā vyāvṛttyapekṣopajanitanānātvarūpeṇa ekasminnarthe pratyuktāstasmāt paramārthena yathoktalakṣaṇasya bhāvanāmārgasya bhedaṃ kartuṃ na kṣamāḥ / saṃvṛtyā tvanālambanamahākaruṇāsvabhāvadharmadhātuniṣyandabhūtāste deśanādharmasvabhāvā yathoktanirdeśā bālajanānāṃ mahāphalodayaprakāśakatvenābhimatāstathāgatasyeti bahutvaṃ na prasajyate /
children.translated_text: Thus: The designations 'innumerable,' 'immeasurable,' and 'incalculable,' being of the nature of verbal expression, with the plurality generated by the form of differentiation dependent on exclusion, are applied to a single object. Therefore, in the ultimate sense, they are not capable of creating divisions in the path of cultivation as characterized above. But conventionally, being teachings whose nature is <s>dharma</s> that are the outflow of the great compassion whose nature is objectless <s>dharmadhātu</s>—those designations as described are accepted by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as capable of illuminating the arising of great fruit for childish people. Thus multiplicity does not follow.

children.text: śūnyatālakṣaṇatayā atiśayādhānābhāvād kiñcidapi mandabuddhipuruṣaṃ prati na kriyata eveti āśaṅkyāha -
children.translated_text: Suspecting that since emptiness is the characteristic, there being no basis for the production of excellence, nothing at all is done even for a person of dull intellect, [the author] says—
"Loss and gain are not tenable for an entity that is beyond verbal expression;

children.text: bhāvanākhyena kiṃ hīnaṃ vartmanā kimudāgatam // Abhis_4.56 //
children.translated_text: what is diminished by the path called 'cultivation,' and what has arisen?" (Abhis 4.56)

children.text: dharmatāsvarūpasya abhimatamārgavastuno niḥsvabhāvatayā tattvānyatvobhayānubhayatvairavācyasya bhāvanātiśayādhānābhāvāt vipakṣapratipakṣayoryathākramamapagamodayau na yujyete /
children.translated_text: Since the object of the favored path, being the nature of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality), is without own-nature and inexpressible as identical, different, both, or neither, and since there is no imposition of a special degree of cultivation, the respective disappearance and arising of the opposing factor and the antidote are not tenable.

children.text: yadyevaṃ bhāvanāsaṃjñakena mārgeṇa kiṃ vipakṣasvarūpaṃ parityaktam, kiñca vyavadāna svarūpaṃ prāptam, na kiñcidapi kriyate, ataḥ anupanyasanīya eveti cet? maivam / tathā coktam -
children.translated_text: If so, by a path designated as 'cultivation,' what opposing nature is abandoned, and what purified nature is attained? Nothing at all is accomplished, so it should not even be brought up—if this is objected? Not so. As it is stated—
"Just as awakening is, so too is the accomplisher of the desired aim;"

children.text: tathatālakṣaṇā bodhiḥ so 'pi tallakṣaṇo mataḥ // Abhis_4.57 //
children.translated_text: "Awakening has the characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and he too is considered to have that characteristic."

children.text: iti / yathā niratiśayādhānā tathatāsvarūpā bodhiḥ niṣprapañcajñānātmakadharmakāyādibuddhasvabhāvā ādhipatyamātreṇa vineyajanānāṃ puṇyajñānānurūpatayā viśiṣṭārthapratibhāsicittajananadvāreṇābhimatārthasya sādhikā, tadvadayamapyāgantukamalāpagamād bhāvanayā sākṣātkṛto mārgaḥ tathatālakṣaṇo 'pi saṃvṛtyābhimatārthakriyākārī / paramārthatastu hānivṛddhyabhāva evāṅgīkriyata iti aprayoga eva prayogatvāt na doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as awakening, whose nature is <s>tathatā</s> with no higher imposition, whose essence is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> and other <s>Buddha</s>-natures consisting of non-elaborated knowledge, accomplishes the desired aim merely through its dominance, by generating in the minds of those to be guided a reflection of the distinguished aim in accordance with their merit and knowledge—similarly—

children.text: evaṃ sati saṃvṛtyā arthakriyāsāmarthyaṃ na ghaṭata ityāśaṅkayannāha -
children.translated_text: Given this, anticipating the objection that conventionally the capacity for efficacious action would not be possible, [the author] says—

children.text: pūrveṇa bodhirno yuktā manasā paścimena vā /
children.translated_text: "Awakening is not established by a prior mind, nor by a subsequent one."

children.text: iti / ekaikasmiṃścitte pūrvāparībhūte buddhabodhiniṣpādakasarvākārajñatādisamastārthāpratibhāsanānnaivaikena (pūrveṇa paścimena vā) bodhiryujyate / 'ekavijñānasantatayaḥ sattvāḥ' iti vacanādasambhavitvena yugapadutpannasamīhitārthaniṣpādakadharmapratibhāsena anekacittenāpi na (yujyate) / anuttarabuddhabodhiniṣpādakasmṛtyupasthānādyaṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmaparyantādhigantṛsvarūpa-pūrvāparībhūtānekacittena vā na(yujyate) ; niranvayodayavināśena parasparasambandhāt /
children.translated_text: Since in each individual mind, whether prior or subsequent, there is no reflection of the totality of aims including <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) that would accomplish <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, awakening is not established by any single [moment of mind]—whether prior or subsequent. Since the statement 'beings have single streams of consciousness' makes it impossible for simultaneously arisen—

children.text: kiṃ tarhi viśiṣṭārthapratibhāsicittajananadvāreṇa arthakriyākārīti? na, tadasamyaktvāt / ityāha -
children.translated_text: Is it then through generating a mind that reflects the distinguished aim that efficacious action is performed? No, because that is incorrect. Therefore [the author] says—
"By the analogy of the lamp, the profound nature of <s>dharmatā</s> is eightfold."

children.text: prathame jvālāvartyormīlanakṣaṇe dvitīyakṣaṇamantareṇa svakāraṇaparamparākramāyātasamānakālasaṃhatotpattyaviśiṣṭatvāt kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇadāhyadāhakābhāvaḥ / tathaiva dvitīyakṣaṇe 'pi viśiṣṭajvālāvartyorūtpattikṣaṇe prathamakṣaṇamantareṇa nityasattvādiprasaṅgatayā saṃvṛtyutpādābhāvāt kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇadāhyadāhakābhāvaḥ / yadyevaṃ tathāpi yadā idampratyayatātmakapratītyasamutpādadharmatayā avicāraikaramyatvena hetuphalasambandhabalād saṃhataviśiṣṭotpannaṃ prathamakṣaṇaṃ samapekṣya tadāhitasāmarthyātiśaya eva viśiṣṭo dvitīyakṣaṇaḥ syāt, tadā nirhetukavināśe 'pi kāraṇakāryayoḥ yathākramaṃ tulyakālaniranvayavināśodayād dāhyadāhakabhāvaḥ / tasmāt prathamakṣaṇe dvitīyārciranapekṣya vartī na dahyate, dvitīyakṣaṇenāpi prathamārciranapekṣya vartī na dahyata iti dīpadṛṣṭāntanyāyena pūrvāparībhūtakṣaṇayorekaviṣayopayogajñāpanapareṇa pūrvakṣaṇavat bodhiniṣpādakakatipayapadārthapratibhāsi prathamavijñānaṃ pratītya tatpratibhāsābhyadhika viśiṣṭārthapratibhāsipaścimavijñānodayād bodhiprāptiryujyate /
children.translated_text: At the first moment when flame and wick meet, without the intervening second moment, since there is no distinction from the simultaneous arising of the series that comes through the successive order of their own causes, there is no [real] combustible and combustor having the characteristics of effect and cause. Likewise, at the second moment too, at the moment of arising of the distinguished flame and wick, the first—

children.text: yathoktenaiva ca dṛṣṭāntena aṣṭaprakārā gambhīradharmatā pratisartavyā iti bhāvanāmārgasthabodhisattvānāmavaivartikalakṣaṇakathanāya yasmin viṣaye aṣṭavidhagāmbhīryaṃ tatkathayannāha -
children.translated_text: And by the very analogy stated, the eightfold profound nature of <s>dharmatā</s> is to be understood. Thus, in order to state the characteristic of non-retrogression for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the path of cultivation, explaining the subject in which the eightfold profundity [applies], [the author] says—

children.text: utpāde ca nirodhe ca tathatāyāṃ gabhīratā /
children.translated_text: "Profundity in origination and cessation, in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),"
"In the knowable, in knowledge, in practice, and in non-dual skillful means."

children.text: iti / na pūrvāparakṣaṇābhyāṃ na ca niḥsvabhāvatayā bhāvanāgamyaviśiṣṭārthotpādanamiti pratītyasamutpādaḥ / sarvabhāvodaya eva niḥsvabhāva iti saṃvṛtyā nirudhyata iti nirodhaḥ / sarvāvasthāsu tathatābhyāse 'pi tasyā asākṣātkaraṇamiti tathatā / tathatāsvabhāvasarvadharmasya dānādyanekavidhānuṣṭhānamiti jñeyaḥ / tathatārūpeṇādarśanameva darśanamiti jñānam / dharmatayā sarvatrācaraṇameva caraṇamiti caryā / advayasvabhāve sarvasiddhirityadvayaḥ / sarvasambhārapariniṣpattau tatphalabuddhatvasyāprāptirityupāyakauśalam / acintyavimokṣamukhalābhāt parasparaviruddhārthānuṣṭhānena gāmbhīryaṃ bhavati / evaṃ avaivartikaśaikṣaḥ salakṣaṇo 'bhihitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dependent origination means that the arising of the distinguished aim accessible through cultivation is not through prior or subsequent moments, nor through lack of own-nature. That the very arising of all entities is without own-nature and conventionally ceases—this is cessation. Even in the cultivation of <s>tathatā</s> in all states, its non-direct-realization—
9 - The Equality of Existence and Peace (<s>Bhavaśāntyoḥ Samatā</s>)

Since one who has attained the <s>dharma</s> of the learner's accumulation strives for the attainment of Buddhahood, in order to explain the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> that is the cause of attaining Buddhahood, [the author] says—
"Because <s>dharmas</s> are like a dream, there is no conceptualization of existence and peace;"
"The refutations of objections such as the non-existence of <s>karma</s> are as stated."

children.text: iti / vipakṣapratipakṣasāṃsārikavaiyadānikadharmāṇāṃ pratibhāsamātrasvabhāvasvapnasadṛśatvena avagamāt saṃsāranirvāṇayornānātvena avikalpa iti samatā / nanu svapnasadṛśatve sati daśākuśaladānādīnāmabhāvaḥ svapnāvasthāyāmiva jāgraddaśāyāmapi syāditicodyānāṃ parihārā bāhyārthavādanaye kṣaṇikatayā nirhetukavināśe
children.translated_text: Since <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the opposing factor, the antidote, <s>saṃsāra</s>, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> are understood to be like a dream, having the nature of mere appearance, there is no conceptualization of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> as different—this is equality. Now, if [all is] dream-like, then the non-existence of the ten unwholesome actions, giving, and the rest—in a dream state—
"The variety of the world is born from <s>karma</s>"—

children.text: iti siddhāntāt paramārthato na kaścinna kenaciddhato nāpi kayacid dravyaṃ kenacid gṛhītamityādyupagame pakṣapravṛttasantānaviruddhapadārthotpādanāt māraṇādyadhyavasāyadvāreṇa ayoniśomanaskārādimato 'kuśalādivat prāṇātipātādayo vyavasthāpyante, tathaiva svapnasadṛśe vastuni tadanurūpārthe bhāvādyabhiniveśena akhaṇḍitasakalaviparyāsabandhanānāmityevaṃ tatpatihārāḥ tatpakṣāścānyatra abhihitā ityavagantavyāḥ / kiñcamiddhenopahataṃ cittaṃ svapne tenāsamaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: From this established principle: even when one accepts that ultimately nothing is killed by anyone, nor is any substance grasped by anyone, still, since objects contradicting the continuum that has commenced a thesis [can] arise, through the determination involved in killing and the like, for one who has improper mental engagement and the rest, there is the taking of life and the like, just as with unwholesomeness—

children.text: iti dṛṣṭāntāsiddhiḥ / ityeva svapne 'pyupacittakuśalākuśalasya prabuddhāvasthāyāmaho kṛtaḥ sukṛta ityanumodane pṛṣṭhāvasthācittābhiniveśaparipuṣṭyā paripoṣaḥ / ataśca dṛṣṭāntāsiddheḥ saṃsāranirvāṇasamatā eva /
children.translated_text: Thus the counter-example is unestablished. In this way, even in a dream, the wholesome and unwholesome accumulated [in the dream], upon awakening, [generates the thought] 'What a good deed was done!'—through the subsequent-state mind's reinforcement by attachment in the form of rejoicing, [merit] increases. Therefore, from the unestablished counter-example, there is indeed the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
10 - The Unsurpassed Purification of the [Buddha-]Field (<s>Anuttarā Kṣetraśuddhi</s>)

children.text: ubhayasamatāvibhāvanayā svabuddhakṣetre buddho bhaviṣyatīti tadanantaraṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhirityāha -
children.translated_text: Through the cultivation of the equality of both [existence and peace], one will become a <s>Buddha</s> in one's own <s>Buddha</s>-field; therefore, the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field [is discussed] next—
"Whatever impurity there is of the world of beings, by offering its purification,"
"And likewise of the vessel world—this is the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field."

children.text: sattvabhājanalokabhedena dvividhabuddhakṣetrayoryathākramaṃ jighatsāpipāsāsthāṇukaṇṭakādikā yā 'śuddhiḥ, tasyāḥ pratipakṣeṇa divyopabhogakanakabhūbhyādiśuddhijananadvāreṇa viśuddhirbuddhakṣetraviśuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The impurity of the twofold <s>Buddha</s>-field, divided into the world of beings and the vessel world—hunger, thirst, thorns, brambles, and the like respectively—through the antidote to that, by generating purification through divine enjoyments, a golden ground, and the like, the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field [is accomplished].
11 - Skillful Means (<s>Upāyakauśala</s>)
Having accomplished the purification of one's own <s>Buddha</s>-field, one should perform the <s>Buddha</s>-activity according to capacity through skillful means; therefore, skillful means is stated—
"Its domain, its practice, the transcendence of hostile [forces],"
"Non-abiding, [acting] according to the mark, the uncommon characteristic,"
"Non-attachment, non-apprehension, free from signs and aspirations,"
"Its indication, and the immeasurable—skillful means is tenfold."

children.text:
iti / āntarāyikadharmasamatikramaṇena devādimārātikramaḥ, vibhāvitasarvadharmasamatvena apratiṣṭhitavihāraḥ, praṇidhānasamṛddhyā yathāvedhaṃ parārthakaraṇam, svabhyastasarvaduṣkaratvena asādhāraṇaḥ, śukladharmaviśuddhyā sarvadharmasyāgrahaṇam, śunyatāvimokṣamukhatvena anupalambhaḥ, animittavimokṣamukhatvena animittaḥ, apraṇihitavimokṣamukhatvena apraṇidhānam, praśnapūrvakāvaivartikadharmakathanena avaivartikaliṅgam, sarvaviṣayajñānatvena apramāṇamiti prajñāpāramitāyā daśavidhaviṣayāṇāṃ sākṣātkriyāyāṃ kālākālajñānaprayoga eva upāyakauśalaṃ bhavatīti /
iti abhisamayālaṅkāre nāma prajñāpāramitopadeśaśāstre caturthādhikāravṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: By transcending obstructive <s>dharmas</s>, the transcendence of <s>Māras</s> including the gods and the rest; through cultivating the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-abiding abiding; through the fulfillment of vows, accomplishing the benefit of others according to the mark; through practicing all difficulties, the uncommon [characteristic]; through the purity of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—
Fifth Chapter: The <s>Mūrdhābhisamaya</s> (Peak Realization)
1 - The Indication (<s>Liṅga</s>) (Heat—the Peak Practice)

children.text: prāptasarvākārabhisambodhasya prakarṣaparyanto 'dhigamo bhavatīti tatsukhāvabodhāya liṅgādyabhidhānapuraḥsaraṃ mūrdhābhisamayamāha -
children.translated_text: Since the realization that has attained all aspects reaches its culmination, for easy comprehension thereof, preceded by the statement of the indication and the rest, [the author] states the peak realization—

children.text: mūrdhaprāptasya yogasya liṅgaṃ dvādaśadhā matam // Abhis_5.1 //
children.translated_text: "The indication of the <s>yoga</s> that has attained the peak is considered to be twelvefold."
"Even in a dream, seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like appearances, and the rest—"

children.text: iti / svapnāvasthāyāmapyatyabhyāsāt svapnasadṛśasarvadharmekṣaṇam, śrāvakādibhūmispṛhācittānutpādanam, tathāgatādidarśanam, buddharddhivikurvitopalabdhiḥ, dharmadeśanādicittotpādaḥ, nairayikasattvādīkṣaṇapuraḥsarasvabuddhakṣetrāpāyaprahāṇānusmaraṇam, nagarādidāhapraśamanasatyādhiṣṭhānasamṛddhiḥ, yakṣādyamanuṣyāpagamasatyavākyaniṣpattiḥ, svayamabhijñāparākramakalyāṇamitrasevanam, sarvaprakāraprajñāpāramitāśikṣaṇam, sarvadharmānabhiniveśaḥ, buddhabodhyāsannībhavanamiti dvādaśa prakārāṇi prāptābhisamayāvasthāyā viśeṣaliṅgāni /
children.translated_text: Even in the dream state, through intensive practice, the seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like; the non-arising of a mind aspiring to the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and other stages; seeing <s>Tathāgatas</s> and the rest; perceiving the miraculous transformations of the <s>Buddha</s>'s powers; the arising of the mind to teach the <s>Dharma</s> and the rest; seeing one's own <s>Buddha</s>[-field] preceded by seeing beings in the hells and the rest—
2 - Growth (<s>Vivṛddhi</s>) (Summit—the Peak Practice)
Of one thus characterized by the indication, how many types of growth are there? [The author] states the growth—
"Making a manifold comparison with [the merit of] beings born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and the rest, [and their] worship of <s>Buddhas</s>, [their] wholesome [deeds], and the rest,"

children.text: upamāṃ bahudhā kṛtvā vivṛddhiḥ ṣoḍaśātmikā // Abhis_5.2 //
children.translated_text: "The growth is of sixteen kinds."

children.text: iti / jambūdvīpakāditrisāhasralokadhātavīyasattveyattātathāgatapūjādhikatvam, viśiṣṭaprajñāpāramitāmanaskāraḥ, anutpattidharmakṣāntilābhaḥ, bodhyabodhakadharmānupalambhaḥ, daśakuśalādyārūpyasamāpattiyogād viśeṣotkarṣaḥ, sarvadevanikāyopasaṃkramaḥ, sarvamārābhibhavaḥ, śāstṛsadṛśajanasamānāvasthā iti aṣṭaprakārāṇi puṇyāni / punaḥ sarvathopāyakauśalapariśuddhaśikṣā, buddhagotrībhavanam, buddhatvaphalaprāptinimittam, pāramitāvipakṣacittānutpādaḥ, rūpādiyogādhigamacittānutpādaḥ, sarvapāramitāsaṃgrahajñānam, sarvasampatpratilambhaḥ, samyaksambodhyāsannībhāva ityanyāni aṣṭaprakārāṇi puṇyāni / puṣpādibhiḥ buddhapūjāyāḥ śubhādikāṃ bahudhā upamāṃ kṛtvā uttarottaraviśeṣotkarṣeṇa ṣoḍaśāvasthātmikā vivṛddhirbhavati /
children.translated_text: The surpassing in <s>Tathāgata</s>-worship [compared to] the number of beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and the rest up to the tri-thousand great-thousand world system; distinguished mental engagement on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the attainment of the patient acceptance of the non-origination of <s>dharmas</s>; non-apprehension of the <s>dharmas</s> that constitute and do not constitute awakening; special excellence through the practice of the ten wholesome [actions] up to the formless attainments—
3 - Firmness (<s>Nirūḍhi</s>) (Patience—the Peak Practice)
To state the firmness, characterized by culminating in the giving up of one's own body, for one who has grown through such growth—[the author] says—
"The unsurpassed completion of the <s>dharmas</s> of the three types of omniscience,"
"Without abandoning the welfare of beings—this is called firmness."

children.text: iti / samyagupāyakauśalabalenaivaṃ nirvikalpādhigamāvasthāyāṃ mahākaruṇādisammukhīkaraṇabhāvena aparityaktasattvārthalakṣaṇā yathoktasarvākārajñatāditrisarvajñatādharmāṇāṃ cittotpādādīnāmuparyuktānāmanuttarā paripūrirnirūḍhiriti /
children.translated_text: Through the power of correct skillful means, in the state of non-conceptual realization, with the characteristic of not abandoning the welfare of beings because of making present great compassion and the rest, the unsurpassed completion of the above-mentioned <s>dharmas</s> of the three types of omniscience beginning with the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>—this is firmness—
4 - The Stability of Mind (<s>Cittasaṃsthiti</s>) (The Supreme <s>Dharma</s>—the Peak Practice)
To state the stability of mind, characterized by becoming firm, for one who has thus grown through firmness—[the author] says—
"Making a comparison with [the merit of] four continents, the first-thousand, the second-thousand, and the third-thousand [world systems],"
"The <s>samādhi</s> is proclaimed through the abundance of merit."

children.text: iti / sambhavatpramāṇasya palapramāṇena parimāṇaṃ pramātuṃ śakyata iti nyāyāt caturdvīpāditrisāhasralokadhātūnāṃ sarveṣāṃ pāramitādīnāṃ samādhipuṇyajñānasvarūpāṇāṃ pṛthak pṛthak upamāṃ kṛtvā tebhyo viśiṣṭā pramāṇātikrāntapuṇyabahutvena samādhilakṣaṇā cittasaṃsthitiḥ kathiteti /
children.translated_text: By the principle that the quantity of what can exist can be measured by measuring units, making a comparison of all the <s>pāramitās</s> and the rest—which are in nature <s>samādhi</s>, merit, and knowledge—for all [beings in] the four continents up to the tri-thousand great-thousand world system, one by one, [this <s>samādhi</s>] surpasses them and exceeds all measure—
These indications and the rest should be understood respectively as the nature of the four penetrative factors beginning with heat.
5 - <s>Darśanamārga</s> (The Path of Seeing) (<s>Mūrdhaprayoga</s> / The Peak Application)

children.text: nirvedhabhāgīyānantaraṃ darśamārgaḥ / tatra caturvidho vipakṣaḥ sapratipakṣaḥ / vipakṣaṃ tāvad grāhyavikalpadvayamāha -
children.translated_text: Immediately after the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) comes the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). Therein, the fourfold adversary together with its antidote [is presented]. First, he states the two conceptualizations of the grasped object (<s>grāhyavikalpa</s>)—

children.text: pravṛtau ca nivṛtau ca pratyekaṃ tau navātmakau /
children.translated_text: In engagement and in withdrawal, each of the two is ninefold;
The conceptualizations of the grasped object are to be known as having the nature of distorted objects. (Abhis 5.5)

children.text: iti / anupalambhopalambhasvabhāvo pravṛttinivṛttipakṣau yathākramaṃ śrāvakabodhisattvādīnāṃ dharmasyādānasantyāgākāreṇa grāhyāviti kleśavad vipakṣau grāhyavikalpau vastunyapratibaddhavṛttitvena vitathapratibhāsitvādayathāsvarūpau viṣayaprabhedena pratyekaṃ navaprakārau jñeyāviti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Having the nature of non-apprehension and apprehension, the two sides of engagement and withdrawal—respectively for <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and others—are grasped in the form of acceptance and rejection of <s>dharmas</s>. Being adversaries like the afflictions, these conceptualizations of the grasped object have distorted appearance, operating without being bound to actual things, and thus have the nature of distorted objects.
