Each is of nine kinds by differentiation of objects, and is to be known thus.
Having thus indicated the two sides of the conceptualization of the grasped object, he states the two conceptualizations of the grasper (<s>grāhakavikalpa</s>)—
The conceptualizations of the grasper are held to be [based on] substantial existence and designational existence of persons;
By the distinction of ordinary beings and noble ones, each of the two is ninefold. (Abhis 5.6)

children.text: grāhau cenna tathā sto 'rthau kasya tau grāhakau matau /
children.translated_text: If the grasped objects are not so, then of whom are those two held to be graspers?
Thus the characteristic of emptiness of those two is [established] through the absence of a grasper-nature. (Abhis 5.7)

children.text: iti / pṛthagjanāryapudgalayoryathākramaṃ dravyaprajñaptisatpuruṣādhiṣṭhānau grāhakavikalpau vibandhakatvād vipakṣau viṣayabhedena pratyekaṃ navaprakārāviti / yadā viṣayabhāvāpannagrāhyāvarthau na tathā grāhyarūpeṇa bhavatastadā na kasyacit tau grāhakāviti, grāhakarūpeṇānayorviviktaṃ rūpamiti vitathapratibhāsitvādayathāviṣayasvarūpau jñeyāviti /
children.translated_text: Thus: For ordinary beings and noble persons respectively, the conceptualizations of the grasper based on substantially existent and designationally existent persons are adversaries because they are obstructive, and are each of nine kinds by differentiation of objects. When the objects that have become grasped are not so—are not in the form of something graspable—then those two are not graspers of anything. Since their form as graspers is isolated from them, they have distorted appearance and thus have the nature of distorted objects, and are to be known [as such].

children.text: kathaṃ pravṛtyadhiṣṭhānaḥ prathamo grāhyavikalpo navadhāḥ? ityāha -
children.translated_text: How is the first conceptualization of the grasped object, based on engagement, ninefold? He states—
This [conceptualization] pertains to own-nature, to spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), to practice, to attainment,
to the object and non-delusion of knowledge, to the antidote and the adversary, (Abhis 5.8)
to one's own realization, to the agent, to the activity of that [agent], and to the fruit of action—
the conceptualization based on the side of engagement is held to be ninefold. (Abhis 5.9)

children.text: iti / viviktena viviktānavabodhasvabhāve, acalādibhūmipraveśena niyatabuddhagotre, māyopamapratipattyā darśanādimārgasamudāgame, pratibhāsamātreṇa abhrāntajñānālambane, guṇadoṣapūrvakopādeyaheyatvena pratipakṣavipakṣe, sarvamalarahitatvena svādhigame, hīnāpraṇītatvena śrāvakādibhūmidūrīkaraṇe, yathāśayānurūpanirmāṇena sattvārthavyāpāre, samyagupāyakauśalabalena sarvajananirvāṇapratiṣṭhāpanakriyāphale ca nirdoṣatayā upādeyatvena pravṛttiḥ kāryā, ityevaṃ pravṛttipakṣādhiṣṭhānaḥ prathamo grāhyavikalpo navaprakāro darśanamārgaprayogāvasthāyāṃ praheyo mata iti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Regarding the own-nature of non-realization of the isolated by the isolated; regarding the definite <s>Buddha</s>-lineage through entry into stages such as the <s>Acalā</s>; regarding the attainment of the path of seeing and other paths through illusion-like practice; regarding the object of non-deluded knowledge through mere appearance; regarding the antidote and adversary through their being acceptable and rejectable preceded by qualities and faults; regarding one's own realization through freedom from all defilements; regarding the distancing from the stages of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others through their being inferior and unexcelled; regarding the activity for the welfare of beings through emanation in accord with their dispositions; and regarding the fruit of action in establishing all beings in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> through the power of skillful means—engagement is to be undertaken as faultless and acceptable. Thus the first conceptualization of the grasped object, based on the side of engagement, is held to be of nine kinds, to be abandoned at the stage of the application of the path of seeing.

children.text: kathaṃ nivṛttipakṣadhiṣṭhāno dvitīyo grāhyavikalpo navadheti? āha -
children.translated_text: How is the second conceptualization of the grasped object, based on the side of withdrawal, ninefold? He states—
In falling into existence or peace, in the deficiency of realization,
in the absence of [proper] reception, and in the impairment of the one on the path, (Abhis 5.10)
in dependence on others, in the cessation of the stated purpose,
in partiality, and in the variety of the confusion of ground and departure, (Abhis 5.11)
and in following behind—this conceptualization is ninefold,
based on the side of withdrawal, arising in the minds of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others. (Abhis 5.12)

children.text: iti / saṃsāranirvāṇānyataraprapātitvena nyunatādhigame, kalyāṇamitropāyakauśalavikalatvena saṃparigrahābhāve, samastajñeyāvaraṇāpratipakṣatvena pratipadvaikalye, tathāgatādyupadeśasāpekṣatvena parapratyayagāmitve, sarvasattvāgratācittamahattvādyapravṛttatvena uddeśanivṛtau, kleśāvaraṇapratipakṣatvena prādeśikamārgavyāpāre, sopalambhatvena prathamaphalādyadhigamanānātve, sarvāvidyānuśayāprahīṇatvena sthānagamanājñāne, mahāyānasarvasaṃgrāhakatvena sarvākārajñatāsarvanirvāṇapaścādanugamane ca sadoṣatayā grāhyatvena vinivṛttiḥ kāryā / ityevaṃ dvitīyo grāhyavikalpo nivṛttipakṣādhiṣṭhānaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhasantānopādeyatvasamudbhavo navadhā bodhisattvānāṃ darśanamārge cittacaittapravṛttyavasthāyāṃ praheyo mata iti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Regarding the deficient realization through falling into either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>; regarding the absence of proper reception through being devoid of the skillful means of a spiritual friend; regarding the impairment of the path through not being an antidote to all cognitive obscurations (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>); regarding dependence on others through reliance on the instruction of <s>Tathāgatas</s> and others; regarding the cessation of the stated purpose through not generating the mind of supreme aspiration for all beings and so forth; regarding the partial scope of the path through being an antidote only to the afflictive obscurations (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>); regarding the variety in attaining the first fruit and so on through having apprehension; regarding the ignorance of ground and destination through not having abandoned the latencies of all ignorance; and regarding following behind all [other paths] through the <s>Mahāyāna</s> encompassing everything, including omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) and all <s>nirvāṇas</s>—withdrawal is to be undertaken as faulty and as [something] grasped. Thus the second conceptualization of the grasped object, based on the side of withdrawal, arising from the acceptance of the continua of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, is held to be ninefold, to be abandoned by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the path of seeing at the stage of the arising of mind and mental factors.

children.text: kathaṃ dravyasatpṛthagjanapuruṣādhiṣṭhānaḥ prathamo grāhakavikalpo navadhā? ityāha -
children.translated_text: How is the first conceptualization of the grasper, based on a substantially existent ordinary person, ninefold? He states—
The first grasper is to be known in terms of grasping and liberation,
in mental activity, in the conjoining of the elements, and of the three, (Abhis 5.13)
in abiding, in fixation, in the designation of the entity of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: saktau ca pratipakṣe ca yathecchaṃ ca gatikṣatau // Abhis_5.14 //
children.translated_text: in attachment, in the antidote, and in the obstruction of progress as one wishes. (Abhis 5.14)

children.text: iti / saṃvṛtyā māyāvad grahaṇamokṣaṇe, tattvato 'manaskāreṇa manaskaraṇe, dharmatayā traidhātukopaśleṣaṇe, śūnyatā 'navasthānena avasthāne, vastvanabhiniveśena sarvābhiniveśe, dravyasadbhāvena sarvadharmaprajñaptau, tattvajñānāsaktyā anabhiniveśapūrvakasaktau, samatābhāvanāpratipakṣatayā pratipakṣe, samyagavijñātaprajñāpāramitatvena yathecchagamanavyāghāte ca pāramārthikabhāvābhiniveśena prathamo grāhakavikalpo navaprakāro darśanamārgaprayogāvasthāyāṃ praheyo mata iti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Conventionally, grasping and liberation as if by a magician; in reality, mental engagement through non-attention; by the nature of reality, conjoining within the three realms; by the emptiness of non-abiding, remaining in a position; by the non-fixation on things, all fixation; by substantial existence, the designation of all <s>dharmas</s>; by non-attachment to the knowledge of reality, attachment preceded by non-fixation; by the absence of the antidote of the cultivation of equanimity, the antidote; and by not having properly understood <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the obstruction of progress as one wishes—through fixation on the ultimately real, the first conceptualization of the grasper is held to be of nine kinds, to be abandoned at the stage of the application of the path of seeing.

children.text: kathaṃ prajñaptisatpuruṣādhiṣṭhāno dvitīyo grāhakavikalpo navadhā? ityāha -
children.translated_text: How is the second conceptualization of the grasper, based on a designationally existent person, ninefold? He states—
In the non-departure from what is indicated, in the determination of path and non-path,
in cessation together with origination, in conjunction and disjunction from things, (Abhis 5.15)
in the abiding of the lineage (<s>gotra</s>), in its destruction, in the absence of aspiration and cause,
and in the apprehension of opponents—[this is] another conceptualization of the grasper. (Abhis 5.16)

children.text: iti / śrāvakādiniryāṇatvena yathoktoddeśāniryāṇe, svābhīṣṭamārgābhāvena itaramārgāmārgāvadhāraṇe, saṃvṛtikāryakāraṇabhāvena utpādanirodhe, nirantaretarapratibhāsatvena samastavastusaṃyogaviyoge, vyomāvasthitaśakunisadṛśatvena rūpādisthāne, bodhicittotpādādidvāreṇa śrāvakādigotravināśe, tathatāprativiśiṣṭadharmatābhāvena abhilāṣābhāve, paramārthasatyāśrayeṇa hetvabhāve, abhyastamātsaryadharmatayā pratyarthikamārādivastūpalambhe ca prajñaptibhāvābhiniveśena dvitīyo grāhakavikalpo navaprakāro darśanamārgacittacaittapravṛttyavasthāyāṃ praheyo mata iti /
children.translated_text: Thus: In the non-departure from what is indicated as the path of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others; in the determination that the other path is not a true path due to the absence of one's preferred path; in the origination and cessation through conventional cause and effect; in the conjunction and disjunction of all things through constant mutual appearance; in abiding in the realm of form and the rest like a bird resting in the sky; in the destruction of the lineage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others through the door of the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> and the rest; in the absence of aspiration due to the absence of a distinct <s>dharmatā</s> from <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); in the absence of a cause based on ultimate truth; and in the apprehension of things such as opponents (<s>Māra</s>) and the rest through the nature of having cultivated miserliness—through fixation on the designationally existent, the second conceptualization of the grasper is held to be of nine kinds, to be abandoned at the stage of the arising of mind and mental factors on the path of seeing.

children.text: darśanamārge vipakṣaṃ sapratipakṣamevaṃ nirdiśya yanmahābodhiniṣpattaye darśanamārgo yena kāraṇena sahita iṣyate, tatkāraṇapradarśanāyāntaraślokamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus indicated the adversary together with its antidote on the path of seeing, in order to demonstrate the reason why the path of seeing is considered to be accompanied by a cause for the accomplishment of great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>), he states an intervening verse—
Showing to others the visions in awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), and the offering of the cause of that,
and the immediate cause for attaining that, characterized by an abundance of merit— (Abhis 5.17)

children.text: iti / vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇabodhau darśanādimārgasandarśanena anyeṣāṃ pratiṣṭhāpanaṃ prathamam (kāraṇam) /
children.translated_text: Thus: The first [reason] is establishing others through showing the path of seeing and other paths in the awakening whose characteristics will be described;
The second [reason] is the proper transmission of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to others through the door of the meaning of the treatise and the rest, which is itself the sign of awakening;
The third [reason] is the proximate cause for attaining awakening, characterized by merit from one's own extensive cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the rest.

children.text: kā punariyaṃ mahābodhiryadarthaṃ yathoktakāraṇasahāyo darśanamārgo 'bhipreta ityantaraślokena mahābodhimāha -
children.translated_text: What then is this great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) for whose sake the path of seeing is intended to be accompanied by the stated causes? He states great awakening in an intervening verse—
Awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is said to be the knowledge of the destruction and non-arising of the defilements;
since there is no destruction and no arising, those objects of knowledge are sequential respectively. (Abhis 5.18)
Thus: The defilements of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations (<s>kleśa</s> and <s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>), being imagined as having arisen and not having arisen—
"Since apart from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (reality-realm) no <s>dharma</s> is found,"

children.text: iti dharmadhātusvabhāvānāmākāśasyeva nirodhotpādābhāvād ekānesvabhāvakāryakāraṇapramāṇādyupapannabhāvavaidhuryād gaganakamalavadvā yathākramaṃ malānāṃ kṣayotpādābhāvād akṣayānutpādajñānātmikā sarvadharmāviparītādhigatilakṣaṇā yathāvad dhamakāyādyātmikā mahābodhirabhidhīyata iti /
children.translated_text: —since those whose own-nature is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> have no cessation or arising, just like space; since they lack the coherence of having a single nature with cause, effect, means of knowledge, and the like; or like a lotus in the sky—due to the absence of destruction and arising of the defilements respectively, the great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) is said to be characterized by knowledge of non-destruction and non-arising, having the nature of the non-inverted realization of all <s>dharmas</s>, the reality (<s>dharma</s>)-body and the rest.

children.text: yasmādevaṃ ato ye bhāvavināśābhisandhinā kṣīṇe kṣīṇamiti jñānaṃ kṣayajñānam, bhāvānutpādābhisandhinā ca anutpanne 'nutpannamiti jñānamanutpādajñānaṃ varṇayanti / bodhiñca kṣayānutpādajñānaṃ varṇayanti / teṣāṃ kṣayānutpādavaikalyād etajjñānaṃ na ghaṭata ityantaraślokenāha -
children.translated_text: Since this is so, those who—with the intention of the destruction of [real] entities—describe destruction-knowledge as 'knowing that which has been destroyed is destroyed,' and—with the intention of the non-arising of [real] entities—describe non-arising-knowledge as 'knowing that which has not arisen has not arisen,' and who describe <s>bodhi</s> as being destruction-and-non-arising-knowledge: for them, due to the deficiency of [actual] destruction and non-arising, such knowledge does not obtain. He says with an intervening verse—
When the fundamental nature has not ceased, through the path called seeing,

children.text: vikalpajātaṃ ki kṣīṇaṃ kiṃ vānutpattimāgatam // Abhis_5.19 //
children.translated_text: what among conceptual products has been destroyed, and what has come to non-arising? (Abhis 5.19)

children.text: iti / utpannānutpannayorthathākramaṃ kṣayotpattivighātalakṣaṇanirodhena aniruddhāyāṃ paramārthatastathatārūpāyāṃ prakṛtau satyāṃ katarad vikalpādirūpamutpannaṃ kṣīṇaṃ, kataraccānutpannam anutpattidharmakaṃ jātaṃ darśanamārgabalena vitathabhāvābhiniveśināṃ bhavatām? yāvatā naiva kiñcit / tasmādasmākaṃ matamevāṅgīkartavyamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: When the fundamental nature (<s>prakṛti</s>)—which is in reality the form of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness)—has not ceased, being characterized by the absence of obstruction to destruction and arising of things arisen and not arisen respectively, then what form of conceptualization and the rest that has arisen has been destroyed, and what has come to non-arising—having the nature of non-arising—through the power of the path of seeing, according to you who fixate on the reality of false entities? Inasmuch as nothing whatsoever [has been so destroyed or not arisen], therefore our position alone should be accepted—this is the intent.

children.text: anyathā tāttvikadharmasattvopagame bhagavataḥ sarvathā vikalpakleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ mahadvismayasthānīyaṃ syādityantaraślokenāha -
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if real existence of <s>dharmas</s> and beings were accepted, then the complete abandonment by the Blessed One of all conceptualization, afflictive, and cognitive obscurations would be a great cause for astonishment. He says with an intervening verse—

children.text: sattvā ca nāma dharmāṇāṃ jñeye cāvaraṇakṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: That beings exist by name, and that the destruction of the obscurations to the knowable of <s>dharmas</s>—

children.text: kathyate yatparaiḥ śāsturatra vismīyate mayā // Abhis_5.20 //
children.translated_text: that which others assert of the Teacher (<s>Śāstṛ</s>)—at this I marvel. (Abhis 5.20)

children.text: iti / tatra hyadayavyayaśūnyatvānnāstyātmeti vibhāvayannātmābhiniveśaṃ parityajya tadviviktaskandhādikaṃ pratītyasamutpannam udayavyayadharmakaṃ samupalabhya nīlataddhiyoḥ sahopalabhbhaniyamāccittamātramevedaṃ na bāhyārtho 'stīti manasikurvan aparityaktagrāhakākāracittābhiniveśo bāhyārthābhiniveśaṃ tiraskṛtya grāhyābhāve grāhakābhāva iti nidhyāyaṃstāmapi grāhakākāralakṣaṇāṃ vijñaptimātratāmavadhūya advayajñānameva kevalaṃ bhāvato bhāvarūpamiti niścitya tadapi pratītyasamutpannatvānmāyāniḥsvabhāvaṃ tattvato 'pagataikāntabhāvābhāvādiparāmarśarūpamiti bhāvayan bhāvanābalaniṣpattau keṣāñcinmaṇirūpyādijñānavad utsāritasakalabhrāntinimittāyā māyopamātmapratibhāsadhiyo nirvikalpāyāḥ kathañcit pratyātmavedyāyāḥ samutpāde jñeyāvaraṇaṃ samyag yogī prajahyāt / anyathā paraiḥ sarvadā ākāśasya dravyābhāvamātrarūpadhāraṇavad anādheyānapaneyasvarūpadhāraṇād dharmāṇāṃ kṣaṇikānāṃ jñānamātrarūpāṇāṃ jñeyalakṣaṇānāñca yadi paramārthato vidyamānatā syāt tadā pratipakṣabhāvanayā ākāśasyeva teṣāṃ na kiñcit kriyate / ato bhāvābhiniveśaviparyāsāvinivṛtyā yad bhagavataḥ sarvathāḥ jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ dharmāṇāñca yatsattopagamyate paraiḥ tatparasparaviruddhārthābhyupagame vismayasthānīyaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Thus: For in that case, one who contemplates 'there is no self' through the emptiness of arising and perishing, abandoning fixation on the self and then apprehending the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) and the rest as isolated from that [self] and dependently arisen, having the nature of arising and perishing; thinking 'this is mind-only, there is no external object' due to the invariable co-apprehension of blue and the cognition of blue; one who, while not having abandoned fixation on the mind as having the aspect of a grasper, discards fixation on external objects; contemplating that 'in the absence of the grasped there is no grasper,' discarding even that mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>) characterized by the aspect of a grasper; determining that only non-dual knowledge alone has real existence as reality; and cultivating that even this [knowledge], being dependently arisen, is like an illusion, without own-nature, and in reality free from the clinging to absolute existence and non-existence—when through the completion of cultivation, like the knowledge of jewels and silver for some, at the arising of a non-conceptual [wisdom] that is in some way individually self-aware, illusion-like, a self-appearing cognition whose causes of all error have been removed, the practitioner might properly abandon the cognitive obscurations. Otherwise, as maintained by others, if <s>dharmas</s>—which are momentary, whose nature is mere knowledge, and which have the characteristic of being knowable—had real existence in the ultimate sense, then just as nothing can be done to space which merely holds the form of the absence of substance, so nothing could be done to those [<s>dharmas</s>] through the cultivation of an antidote, since they would hold an intrinsic nature to which nothing can be added or removed. Therefore, without the reversal of the perverse fixation on real existence, the assertion by others that the Blessed One has completely abandoned cognitive obscurations and that <s>dharmas</s> have [real] existence—this acceptance of mutually contradictory meanings would be cause for astonishment.

Having thus refuted the position of real existence and having established the position of essencelessness, in order to state the proper position to be accepted by those seeking liberation, he says with an intervening verse—
Therefore, nothing whatsoever is to be removed, and nothing whatsoever is to be added;

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ bhūtadarśī vimucyate // Abhis_5.21 //
children.translated_text: reality is to be seen as reality—one who sees reality is liberated. (Abhis 5.21)

children.text: iti / yasmādevaṃ bhāvābhiniveśena mukteranupapattirato apavādasamāroparūpamapanayanaprakṣepaṃ kasyaciddharmasyākṛtvā idameva pratītyasamutpannaṃ saṃvṛtyā tathyarūpaṃ rūpādiniḥsvabhāvādirūpato nirūpaṇīyam, evañca māyāgajena aparamāyāgajaparājayavad viparyāsanivṛtyā tatvadarśī vimucyata iti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Since liberation is impossible through fixation on real existence, therefore, without performing any removal or addition—which have the form of deprecation and superimposition—regarding any <s>dharma</s>, this very dependently arisen [reality] is to be examined as having the form of truth conventionally, and as having the nature of the essencelessness of form and the rest. And thus, just as a magical elephant defeats another magical elephant, through the reversal of perversion, one who sees reality is liberated.
Having thus stated what is incidental, he states the main topic—the path of seeing—

children.text: ekaikasyaiva dānādai teṣāṃ yaḥ saṅgraho mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mutual inclusion of each and every one of those [<s>pāramitās</s>], in giving and the rest,
that, being momentary, subsumed under <s>kṣānti</s> (patience/acceptance)—this is the path of seeing here. (Abhis 5.22)

children.text: iti / dānādiṣaṭpāramitānāṃ pratyekamekaikabhāve dānādau yaḥ parasparaṃ sarvapāramitāsaṅgrahaḥ, so 'traikakṣaṇiko mūrdhābhisamaye duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntisaṃgṛhītaḥ trimaṇḍalaviśuddhiprabhāvitaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadākāranirjāto darśanamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: When each one of the six <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with giving has the nature of a single [<s>pāramitā</s>] such as giving, the mutual inclusion of all <s>pāramitās</s> in that—this is the momentary path of seeing in the peak <s>abhisamaya</s> (clear realization), subsumed under <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering), empowered by the threefold purity, produced in thirty-six aspects.

children.text: asmiṃśca (darśanamārge) samutpanne kāmarūpārūpyadhātubhedena pratyekaṃ caturvikalpanavaprakāratayā aṣṭottaraśatagrāhyagrāhakavikalpaprahāṇena tatsaṃgṛhītavikalpajanakavāsanākleśāṣṭottaraśataprahāṇaṃ pratītyasamutpādadharmatayopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: And when this path of seeing has arisen, through the division of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm, by each [having] nine varieties of the four types of conceptualization, through the abandonment of one hundred and eight conceptualizations of the graspable and the grasper, the abandonment of one hundred and eight defilements—latencies generating those conceptualizations subsumed under them—is accomplished.

children.text: tatra vaśitvārthaṃ tāmeva punaḥ punarbhāvayatīti antaraślokenāha -
children.translated_text: To that end, [the yogin] cultivates that [<s>samādhi</s>] again and again for the sake of mastery—[the author] states with an intervening verse—
"Having entered that <s>samādhi</s>, then the <s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s> (Lion's Play),"
"He observes dependent origination in forward and reverse order."

children.text: iti / sa darśanamārgaprāpto yogī kleśajñeyāvaraṇabhayābhāvāt siṃhavijṛmbhitaṃ (nāma) samādhiṃ samāpadya uttarakālamavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityādyanulomaṃ jarāmaraṇanirodho jātinirodhād ityādipratilomaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ nirūpayati /
children.translated_text: That yogin who has attained the path of seeing, because of the absence of fear from the obscurations of defilements and the knowable, enters the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s> (Lion's Play) and thereafter [contemplates]: 'Conditioned by ignorance are formations'—in forward order, and 'the cessation of old age and death is [due to] the cessation of birth'—
6 - The Path of Cultivation (<s>Bhāvanāmārga</s>) (The Peak Practice)

children.text: darśanamārgamevamabhidhāya vipakṣaprahāṇādikam ādhārapratipattipūrvakaṃ subodhamiti ādhāraṃ bhāvanāmārgamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus described the path of seeing, since the abandonment of opposing factors and the rest is easily understood when preceded by the basis of practice, [the author] states the basis—the path of cultivation—
"Having transcended what is attained in the desire realm, the non-concentrated consciousness,"
"The attainments with cessation—going forward and coming back, nine, in two ways;"
"By skipping one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, or eight,"
"The leaping attainment; non-cessation; and the incomparable."

children.text: iti / bodhisattvāḥ prathamadhyānamārabhya yāvannirodhaṃ gatvā tato nirodhamārabhya yāvat prathamadhyānamāgamya evamanulomapratiloma (krama)-dvayena caturdhyāna caturārūpyanirodhalakṣaṇā nava samāpattīrgatvā āgamya punaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadya tato vyutthāya nirodham, evaṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanānnirodhaṃ samāpadya, tato vyutthāya anantarasamāpattimālambya kāmāvacaraṃ vijñānaṃ maryādārūpeṇāvasthāpya upāyakauśalyabalena vyutthāya tadeva vijñānamasamāhitamāmukhīkṛtya, tato nirodhaṃ tato 'samāhitaṃ tato nirodhamekaṃ parityajya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ tato 'samāhim tato dvayaṃ parityajya ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ tato 'samāhitam, evaṃ yāvadaṣṭau parityajya prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ tato 'samāhitam, ityekādiparityāgenānirodhasamāpattiṃ yāvad visadṛśadvāreṇa gacchatītyatulyagām avaskandasamāpattiṃ vaśitvalakṣaṇām āmukhīkṛtya bhāvanāmārgo bhavati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, beginning from the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to cessation, going forward, and from cessation back to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, coming back—in this twofold order of forward and reverse, the four <s>dhyānas</s>, four formless [attainments], and cessation—

children.text:
bhāvanāmārgamevamabhidhāya tatra praheyaḥ caturvidho vipakṣo vaktavyaḥ /
prathamaṃ tāvad grāhyavikalpamāha -
children.translated_text:
Having thus described the path of cultivation, the fourfold opposing factor to be abandoned therein should be stated.
First, the conceptualization of the graspable is stated—
"In abbreviation, in elaboration, [and in relation to] the <s>Buddhas</s>; in reliance and non-comprehension;"
"In the three times; in the absence of qualities; in the three kinds of the path to the excellent;"
"This is one [type of] conceptualization of the graspable, whose domain is the aspect of practice."

children.text: iti saṃkṣiptarūcisattvānugraheṇa dharmasaṃkṣepe, vistararucisattvānukampayā dharmavistare, yathāvihitārthānanuṣṭhānena buddhasānāthyāparigrahe, samutpannaniruddhatvena prayogamārgaguṇābhāve, samyagutpattihetuvaidhuryād darśanamārgaguṇābhāve, anāgatāsattvena bhāvanāmārgaguṇābhāve, viparyāsaśāntatvādinā nirvāṇaprayogamārge, śūnyatābhinirhāratvena darśanamārge, naiḥsvābhāvyabhāvakatvena bhāvanāmārge ca prathamo grāhyavikalpaḥ asyāmavasthāyāṃ praheyatvena bhāvanāmārgaprayogāvasthāyāṃ navavidho viṣayī /
children.translated_text: In the abbreviation of the <s>Dharma</s> through compassion for beings who prefer brevity; in the elaboration of the <s>Dharma</s> through compassion for beings who prefer detail; in the non-comprehension of reliance on the <s>Buddha</s> through not practicing the prescribed meaning; the practice-path being arisen-and-ceased—
Having thus indicated the first, [the author] states the second conceptualization of the graspable—
"The second is considered to have as its domain the activity of mind and mental factors."
"The non-arising of the mind; mental engagement on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening);"
"Mental engagement on the lesser vehicle; non-mental-engagement on perfect awakening;"
"In cultivation and non-cultivation, and their very opposite;"
"And the erroneous—[these] conceptualizations on the path of cultivation should be known."

children.text: iti / kalyāṇamitrādivaikalyād bodhicittānutpāde, viśiṣṭabuddhālambanapuṇyābhāvād bodhimaṇḍāmanaskāre, śrāvakagotratvāt tadyānamanaskaraṇe, pratyekabuddhagotratvāt tadyānāmukhīkaraṇe, prajñāpāramitāpratipattivaidhuryāt samyaksambodhyamanaskaraṇe, sopalambhatvena bhāvanāyāṃ nirupalambhavattvena abhāvanāyām, anupalambhānanupalambhatvāt nabhāvanānābhāvane, viparītābhiniveśād ayathārthatve ca dvitīyo grāhyavikalpaḥ tasyāmavasthāyāṃ praheyatvena bhāvanāmārge cittacaittapravṛtyavasthāyāṃ navavidho viṣayī /
children.translated_text: Through the lack of spiritual friends and the rest, the non-arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>; through the lack of merit from [contemplating] a distinguished <s>Buddha</s>-object, mental engagement on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>; through being of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage, mental engagement on that vehicle; through being of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> lineage, turning toward that vehicle—
Having thus indicated the second, [the author] states the first conceptualization of the grasper—
"The first grasper should be known as having the domain of the designation of beings."
"It consists of the designation of <s>dharmas</s>, non-emptiness, attachment, and analysis."

children.text: kṛte ca vastuno yānatritaye ca sa kīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is proclaimed in relation to what has been done, to an object, and to the three vehicles;"

children.text: dakṣiṇāyā aśuddhau vā caryāyāśca vikopane // Abhis_5.31 //
children.translated_text: "And in the impurity of the gift, and in the corruption of practice."

children.text: iti / dravyasadanupapattyā sattvaprajñaptau, pratibhāsamātratvāt (sarva)-dharmaprajñaptau, sarvatragatvāt sarvākārajñatādidharmāśūnyatve, sarvathābhiniveśāprahāṇād dharmasaktau, niḥsvabhāvāvabodhena dharmapravicaye, samuddeśākaraṇena vastūddeśakaraṇe, rūpādyupalambhatvād yānatrayaniryāṇe, samyagapratipannatvena dakṣiṇāśuddhau, dānādyupalambhapratiṣattyā caryāvikopane ca pūrvavad grāhakavikalpo bhāvanāmārgaprayogāvasthāyāṃ navavidho viṣayī /
children.translated_text: Through the impossibility of a substantially existent [person], [there is conceptualization regarding] the designation of beings; through [everything] being mere appearance, [regarding] the designation of all <s>dharmas</s>; through [<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>] pervading everything, [regarding] the non-emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; through the non-abandonment of attachment in all respects, [regarding] attachment to <s>dharmas</s>—
Having thus indicated the first, [the author] states the second conceptualization of the grasper—
"The other [grasper], having as its domain the designation of beings and its causes, is ninefold;"
"Connected with the path of cultivation, it is the opposing factor, through its destruction."

children.text: iti / vipakṣo dvitīyo grāhakavikalpaḥ sattvaprajñaptitadvyavasthāpanapratibhāsamātrahetuviṣayo bhāvanāmārgeṇa sampraheyatvāt tatsambaddho navaprakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The second opposing factor—the conceptualization of the grasper—has as its domain the designation of beings and the mere-appearance-nature causes that establish it; being to be abandoned by the path of cultivation, it is connected with it and is of nine varieties.
If asked: how is it of nine varieties? [The author] states with two intervening verses—
"In the threefold obscuration of each of the three types of omniscience,"
"In the conjunction and disjunction with the peace of the path, <s>tathatā</s>, and the rest;"
"In the inequality regarding suffering and the rest; in the nature of the defilements;"

children.text: dvayābhāve ca saṃmohe vikalpaḥ paścimo mataḥ // Abhis_5.34 //
children.translated_text: "And in the absence of the pair, and in confusion—this is considered the last conceptualization."

children.text: iti / sarvākārāparijñānena sarvākārajñatāvaraṇasaṃmohe, sarvamārgāparijñānena mārgajñatāvaraṇasaṃmohe, sarvavastvaparijñānena sarvajñatāvaraṇasaṃmohe, prajñāpāramitā 'parijñānena sarvaśāntamārgasaṃmohe, tathatājñeyarūpādyaparijñānena tathatādisaṃyogaviyogasaṃmohe, mārādisvarūpāparijñānena asamatvasaṃmohe, yathārūtārthagrāhitvena duḥkhādisatyasaṃmohe, rāgādisvabhāvāparijñānena kleśaprakṛtisaṃmohe, grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇāparijñānena advayasaṃmohe ca pūrvavat paścimo grāhakavikalpo bhāvanāmārgacittacaittapravṛttyavasthāyāṃ navaprakāro viṣayī mataḥ //
children.translated_text: Confusion in the obscuration of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> through non-comprehension of all aspects; confusion in the obscuration of <s>mārgajñatā</s> through non-comprehension of all paths; confusion in the obscuration of <s>sarvajñatā</s> through non-comprehension of all objects; confusion in the obscuration through non-comprehension of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—

children.text: teṣāṃ bhāvanāmārgavipakṣāṇāṃ prahāṇe caturvidhapratipakṣo 'pi tadbhedena bhinno 'vagantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the abandonment of those opposing factors of the path of cultivation, the fourfold antidote should also be understood as differentiated by the division of those [factors].

children.text: pūrvavad aṣṭottaraśatavikalpaprahāṇasamakālameva tatsaṃgṛhītāṣṭottaraśatakleśānāṃ prahāṇena sarvaguṇasampado bhāvanāmārgasthaṃ bodhisattvamāśrayanta iti dvābhyām antaraślokābhyāmāha -
children.translated_text: As before, simultaneously with the abandonment of the one hundred and eight conceptualizations, through the abandonment of the one hundred and eight defilements subsumed under them, all the perfections of qualities attend the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the path of cultivation—[the author] states with two intervening verses—
"When these [conceptualizations], which are calamities, are exhausted, it is as if one breathes freely after a long time;"
"The perfections of qualities that accomplish the happiness of the world in all its aspects,"
"All [converge] with complete approach, [upon] that great being who is rich in the desired fruit,"
"As rivers [flow into] the great ocean."

children.text: iti / bhāvanāmārgābhyāsād āsāṃ caturvikalpajātīnāmupadravatvena itīnāṃ kṣaye sati saṃrodhavaikalyena saṃharṣocchvāsaprāptā iva sarvāstriyānasaṃgṛhītā guṇasampadaḥ kṛpāpāratantryāt sarvaprakārajagatsaukhyotpādanadakṣā sarvathābhimukhyāgamanaprakāreṇa prakarṣaparyantādhigamaphalaiḥ prātaśobhaṃ bhāvanāmārgasthaṃ bodhisattvamāśrayante mahāsamudramiva nadya iti /
children.translated_text: Through the practice of the path of cultivation, when the four classes of conceptualization, which are calamities, are exhausted—as if gaining the breath of joy after imprisonment—all the perfections of qualities included in the three vehicles, through the dependence on compassion—
7 - The <s>Ānantarya-samādhi</s> (Immediate Concentration) (The Peak Practice)
After the path of cultivation, [the author] states the uninterrupted path—
"Establishing the beings of the tri-thousand [world system] in the attainment of the realization of disciples and solitary realizers,"

children.text: bodhisattvasya ca nyāme pratiṣṭhāpya śubhopamāḥ // Abhis_5.37 //
children.translated_text: "And in the certainty of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and making comparisons with the merit [thereof];"
"Through the abundance of merit, the immediate [concentration] for attaining Buddhahood—"

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiḥ sa sarvākārajñatā ca tat // Abhis_5.38 //
children.translated_text: "That <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s> is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects)."

children.text: iti / śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ nyāme trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātavīyasattvān pratiṣṭhāpya kaścid yatpuṇyaṃ prasravati, tadupamīkṛtya tadviśiṣṭapuṇyabahutvena yā sarvākārajñatā tad buddhatvamiti buddhatvaprāpteravyavahito yaḥ samādhiḥ so 'trānantaryasamādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having established the beings of the tri-thousand great-thousand world system in the certainty of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> respectively, whatever merit flows from that—making a comparison with that, through the abundance of merit that surpasses it, that which is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>—

children.text: tadālambanādayaḥ kīdṛśā iti ced? antaraślokena ālambanādīnāha -
children.translated_text: If asked: what are its object-support and the rest? [The author] states the object-support and the rest with an intervening verse—
"Its object-support is the non-existence [of all <s>dharmas</s>]; and mindfulness is considered its dominant [condition];"
"Its aspect is quiescence—here, for those who speak and dispute."

children.text: iti / asya cānantaryasamādheḥ sarvadharmābhāvopalabdhiḥ ālambanapratyayaḥ, smaraṇaṃ cādhiparipratyayaḥ, prakṛtiśāntatā cākāraḥ / atra ca sthāne duravagāhatvād aviditopāyakauśalānāṃ pravādināṃ (nānā)-codyamukhaparamparāprasarpiṇī (vipratipattiḥ) iti upāyakauśalena sā nirākartavyeti / anenāsya gabhīratā abhihitetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And of this <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s>, the apprehension of the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> is the object-support condition; mindfulness is the dominant condition; and quiescence by nature is its aspect. And here, because of its unfathomability, for those who do not know skillful means—
8 - The Wrong Understanding (<s>Vipratipattiḥ</s>) (The Peak Practice)

children.text: viparyastamatīnāṃ kīdṛśīḥ vipratipattīḥ nirākṛtya sa samādhirutpādayitavya iti cet? samādheranantaraṃ vipratipattīrāha -
children.translated_text: If asked: by refuting what kinds of wrong understandings of those with perverted minds should that <s>samādhi</s> be generated? After the <s>samādhi</s>, [the author] states the wrong understandings—
"In the object-support and its arising; in the ascertainment of its own-nature;"
"In the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; in the ultimate along with the conventional;"

children.text: prayoge triṣu ratneṣu sopāye samaye muneḥ /
children.translated_text: "In practice; in the three jewels; in skillful means; in the teaching of the Sage;"
"In perversion; in the correct path; and in the antidote and the opposing factor;"
"In the characteristic; and in cultivation—the wrong understandings are considered"

children.text: sarvākārajñatādhārā ṣoḍhā daśa ca vādinām // Abhis_5.42 //
children.translated_text: "To be sixteen-and-ten, based on <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, for those who speak."

children.text: iti saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtadhātvorabhāvatvena ālambanopapattau, sarvathā nīrūpatvād ālambanasvabhāvāvadhāraṇe, bhāvābhāvānupalambhena sarvākārajñatājñāne, tathatāsvabhāvatvena saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyadvaye, dānādyanupalambhena prayoge, boddhavyābhāvād buddharatne, nāmadheyamātratvād dharmaratne, rūpādyālambanapratiṣedhāt saṃgharatne, dānādyanupalambhena upāyakauśale, bhāvābhāvobhayarūpādhigamapratiṣedhāt tathāgatābhisamaye, prapañcavyavasthāpitānityāditvena nityādiviparyāse, vibhāvitamārgaphalāsākṣātkaraṇena mārge, hānopādānābhāvena vipakṣe pratipakṣe ca, dharmyabhāvād dharmalakṣaṇe, svasāmānyalakṣaṇānupapattyā bhāvanāyāñca parasparaviruddhā bhāṣārthānuṣṭhānena ayujyamānatayā saṃśayarūpāḥ ṣoḍaśa vipratipattīryathānirdiṣṭaviṣayatvena sarvākārajñatādhiṣṭhānāḥ sarveṣāmeva aviditabodhisattvopāyakauśalajanapravādināṃ yathāsambhavamubhayasatyāśritopāyakauśalena nirākṛtya samyak sarvathā niścayamutpādya kalyāṇakāmairbodhisattvairānantaryasamādhiradhigamyata iti /
children.translated_text: Through the non-existence of both the conditioned and unconditioned elements, regarding the arising of the object-support; through being utterly formless, regarding the ascertainment of the own-nature of the object-support; through the non-apprehension of existence and non-existence, regarding the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; through being the nature of <s>tathatā</s>, regarding the conventional and the ultimate—
Thus ends the commentary on the fifth chapter in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instruction on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Sixth Chapter: The Sequential Realization (<s>Ānupūrvikā</s>)

children.text: prāptamūrdhā 'bhisamayo vyastasamastatvena adhigatānarthān anupurvīkṛtya sthirīkaraṇāya vibhāvayatītyanupūrvābhisamayamāha -
children.translated_text: The one who has attained the peak realization, in order to stabilize by cultivating in proper sequence the meanings realized separately and collectively—[the author] states the sequential realization—

children.text: dānena prajñayā yāvad buddhādau smṛtibhiśca sā /
children.translated_text: "Through giving and through <s>prajñā</s> up to the <s>Buddha</s> and the rest, and through the applications of mindfulness,"
"Through the own-nature of the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s>—this is considered the sequential practice."

children.text: iti / trimaṇḍalaviśuddhiprabhāvitadānādiṣaṭpāramitāsarvākāraparipūraṇena prajñāpāramitāntargatapāramitācatuṣṭayatvāt samyag daśabhūminiṣpādakena smṛtyupasthānādinā saptabodhyaṅgākāreṇa āryāṣṭāṅgamārgatayā ca paramārthataḥ asmaraṇalakṣaṇena trividhabuddhānusmaraṇena yathākramaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyadarśanabhāvanāmārgadyotakena tathaiva kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtadharmānusmaraṇena pūrvavad āryāvaivartikabodhisattvasaṃghasmaraṇena tathaiva śīlatyāgadevatānusmaraṇena rūpādisarvadharmābhāve svabhāvāvabuddhena ca yo 'dhigamaḥ sānupūrvakriyeṣyata iheti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Through the complete fulfillment in all aspects of the six <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with giving, empowered by the purity of the three spheres; through the fourfold <s>pāramitā</s> included within <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; through the aspect of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) beginning with the applications of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) that properly accomplish the ten stages; through the noble eightfold path; through the threefold recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmaraṇa</s>), whose characteristic is ultimately non-recollection, which illuminates respectively the aids to penetration, the path of seeing, and the path of cultivation; likewise through the recollection of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>; through the recollection of the assembly of noble non-retrogressing <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as before; likewise through the recollection of morality, renunciation, and the gods; and through one who has awakened to the own-nature in the absence of all <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the rest—this attainment will be explained here in sequential order.
Thus ends the commentary on the sixth topic in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instructions on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Seventh Topic: The Chapter on Single-Instant Realization (<s>Ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>)

children.text: vibhāvitānupūrvābhisamayasya svabhyastīkaraṇāya teṣāmeva kṣaṇenaikenādhigama ityekakṣaṇābhisambodhaḥ / so 'pi lakṣaṇena caturvidha iti /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of making thoroughly familiar what has been elucidated as sequential realization, the attainment of those very [realizations] in a single instant is the single-instant realization. This too is fourfold by characteristic.
1 - The Characteristic of Non-ripening (<s>Avipākalakṣaṇa</s>)
The first single-instant realization has the characteristic of the single instant of all undefiled <s>dharmas</s> in the state of non-ripening. Thus [the author] says—
"Since all undefiled [<s>dharmas</s>] are encompassed by each and every one,
this single-instant awakening of the Sage should be known through giving and the rest." (Abhis 7.1)
In the form of the nature of <s>dharmadhātu</s>—

children.text: eko bhāvaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ sarve bhāvā ekabhāvasvabhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: "One entity has the nature of all entities; all entities have the nature of one entity;

children.text: eko bhāvastattvato yena dṛṣṭaḥ sarve bhāvāstattvatastena dṛṣṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: one who has seen one entity in its reality has thereby seen all entities in their reality."

children.text: itinyāyānna kevalaṃ bahubhirekasya saṃgrahaḥ, api tvekakṣaṇadānādijñānena ālambyamānena apagatapratiniyatavastugrahaṇaviparyayarūpeṇa dānādyaśītyanuvyañjanalakṣaṇānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃgraheṇa muneḥ bodhisattvasyāvabodho hi ekakṣaṇābhisambodha iti jñātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this principle, not only is one encompassed by many, but through the knowledge of giving and the rest in a single instant—being apprehended, having the form of the reversal of the grasping of fixed particular objects—through the encompassment of <s>dharmas</s> characterized by giving and the rest and the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), the awakening of the Sage, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, is indeed the single-instant realization. This should be known.

children.text: kimevaṃ punarekānāsravajñānālambane sarvānāsravasaṃgraha iti cet? laukikadṛṣṭāntenāha -
children.translated_text: If one asks whether there is indeed the encompassment of all undefiled [<s>dharmas</s>] in the object of a single undefiled knowledge, [the author] responds with a worldly analogy—
"Just as even a single plank of a water-wheel, set in motion by a person,
moves everything at once—so too knowledge in a single instant." (Abhis 7.2)

children.text: iti / yathaikāpi padikā puruṣeritā sakṛdekavāraṃ sarvamaraghaṭṭaṃ sacchilpipūrvaparikarmasāmarthyāt calayati tathā pūrvapraṇidhānāvedhadharmadhātusāmarthyād ekasminneva kṣaṇe ekamanāsravamālambyamānaṃ sarvaṃ sajātīyamabhimukhīkārayatīti /
children.translated_text: Thus: Just as even a single plank, set in motion by a person, moves the entire water-wheel at once, at a single time, through the power of the prior preparation by a skilled craftsman—so too, through the power of prior aspirations, penetration, and <s>dharmadhātu</s>, in a single instant, a single undefiled [knowledge] being apprehended causes all that is of the same class to face [realization].
2 - The Characteristic of Ripening (<s>Vipākalakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text: evaṃ prathamaṃ nirdiśya vipākadharmatāvasthānāsravasarvadharmaikakṣaṇalakṣaṇo bhavatyekakṣaṇābhisambodho dvitīyaḥ / ityāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus explained the first, the second single-instant realization has the characteristic of the single instant of all undefiled <s>dharmas</s> in the state of the nature of ripening (<s>vipākadharmatā</s>). Thus [the author] says—
"When the state of the nature of ripening, entirely constituted of the wholesome,
has become <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—then knowledge in a single instant." (Abhis 7.3)

children.text: yadā bodhisattvasya pratipakṣabhāvanayā sarvavipakṣāpagamanena sakalavyavadānapakṣavipākadharmatāvasthā sarvakalaṅkāpagamena śaradindujyotsnāvat śuklasvabhāvā jātā tadā ekasminnevakṣaṇe vipākāvasthāprāptānām anāsravadharmāṇāṃ bodhāt jñānaṃ prajñāpāramitā ekakṣaṇābhisambodha iti /
children.translated_text: When, through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s cultivation of antidotes, with the removal of all opposing factors, the state of the nature of ripening of the entire purification-side, through the removal of all stains, has become of pure nature like the radiance of the autumn moon—then, in a single instant, through the awakening to the undefiled <s>dharmas</s> that have attained the state of ripening, the knowledge that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the single-instant realization.
3 - The Characteristic of Non-characterization (<s>Alakṣaṇalakṣaṇa</s>)
Having thus explained the second, the third single-instant realization has the characteristic of the single instant of all <s>dharmas</s> as without characteristics. Thus [the author] says—
"Abiding in <s>dharmas</s> that are like a dream, through the practice of giving and the rest,
one realizes the characteristiclessness of <s>dharmas</s> in a single instant." (Abhis 7.4)

children.text: pūrvaṃ svapnopamasarvadharmābhyāsena sambhāradvayamanubhūya adhigamāvasthāyāṃ svapnasvabhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu upādānaskandhādiṣu sthitvā dānādiṣaṭpāramitāpratipattyā dānādirūpanirūpaṇākāreṇa alakṣaṇāḥ sarvadharmā iti saṃkleśavyavadānarūpāṇāṃ dharmāṇām ekenaiva kṣaṇenālakṣaṇatvaṃ jānātītyevamekakṣaṇābhisambodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Previously, through the practice of all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like, having experienced the twofold accumulation, in the state of attainment, abiding in all <s>dharmas</s>—the aggregates of clinging and the rest—which are of dream-nature, through the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with giving, by the mode of examining and analyzing giving and the rest, [one realizes that] all <s>dharmas</s> are without characteristics. Thus one knows the characteristiclessness of <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to defilement and purification in a single instant—this is the single-instant realization.
4 - The Characteristic of Non-duality (<s>Advayalakṣaṇa</s>)

Having thus explained the third, the fourth single-instant realization has the characteristic of the single instant of all <s>dharmas</s> as having the characteristic of non-duality. Thus [the author] says—
"One does not perceive the dream and the dreamer through the connection of duality;
one sees the non-dual reality of <s>dharmas</s> in a single instant." (Abhis 7.5)

children.text: nirantaradīrghakāladvayapratibhāsaprahāṇābhyāsasātmībhāvād unmūlitadvayapratibhāsavāsano yadā bodhisattvo grāhyagrāhakayogena svapnaṃ grāhyaṃ svapnadaśiṃnaṃ grāhakaṃ nekṣate, tadā sarve 'pvevaṃdharmāṇo dharmā iti dharmāṇāmadvayaṃ tattvam ekenaiva kṣaṇenādhigacchatītyekakṣaṇābhisambodha iti /
children.translated_text: Through the long and continuous practice of eliminating the appearance of duality having become second nature, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having uprooted the latent impressions of the appearance of duality, does not perceive the dream as the grasped and the dreamer as the grasper through the connection of duality—then, [realizing that] all <s>dharmas</s> are of this very nature, one attains the non-dual reality of <s>dharmas</s> in a single instant. This is the single-instant realization.
Thus ends the commentary on the seventh topic in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instructions on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Eighth Topic: The Chapter on the <s>Dharmakāya</s>
1 - The <s>Svabhāvakāya</s> (Essential Body)

children.text: vibhāvitaikakṣaṇābhisambodhasya dvitīye kṣaṇe dharmakāyābhisambodhaḥ / sa ca svābhāvikakāyādibhedena caturvidhaḥ / (tatra) prathamaḥ svābhāvikakāya ityāha -
children.translated_text: In the second instant after the elucidated single-instant realization, there is the realization of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. This too is fourfold, divided into the <s>Svābhāvikakāya</s> (Essential Body) and the rest. [Of these,] the first is the <s>Svābhāvikakāya</s>. Thus [the author] says—

children.text: sarvākārāṃ viśuddhiṃ ye dharmāḥ prāptā nirāsravāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those undefiled <s>dharmas</s> that have attained complete purity in all aspects—
the <s>Svābhāvikakāya</s> (Essential Body) of the Sage is characterized by their nature." (Abhis 8.1)

children.text: smṛtyupasthānādayo jñānātmakā lokottarā dharmadhāturūpatvād anāsravāmalānāmāgantukatvena sarvaprakārāṃ viśuddhiṃ prakṛtiviviktalakṣaṇāṃ prāptāsteṣāṃ yā prakṛtiḥ svabhāvo 'nutpādarūpaḥ, ayaṃ munerbuddhasya bhagavato lokottareṇa mārgeṇa prāpyate, na kriyata ityakṛtrimārthena māyopamavijñānasarvadharmapratipattyādhigataḥ svābhāvikaḥ kāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The supramundane [<s>dharmas</s>] beginning with the applications of mindfulness, being of the nature of knowledge and having the form of <s>dharmadhātu</s>, being undefiled and pure, with adventitious [defilements] having been removed, have attained complete purity in all aspects—purity characterized by natural separation. Their nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), the own-being in the form of non-arising—this is attained by the Sage, the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, through the supramundane path; it is not created. In this sense of the uncreated, the <s>Svābhāvikakāya</s> is realized through the practice of all <s>dharmas</s> as illusion-like consciousness.

children.text: pariśiṣṭakāyatrayaṃ tathyasaṃvṛtyā pratibhāsamānaṃ paramārthato dharmatārūpaṃ yathādhimokṣaprabhāvitaṃ buddhabodhisattvaśrāvakādigocaratvena vyavasthāpitamiti kathanāya -
children.translated_text: The remaining three bodies, appearing through true conventional [truth], being in nature ultimate <s>dharmatā</s>, are established through having been empowered according to [beings'] aspirations, as the domain of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and the rest. To explain this—
"Since it is accepted that separation is not different from the separated,"
by this principle, even though non-different from that [<s>Svābhāvikakāya</s>], it is separately established.
2 - The <s>Jñānadharmakāya</s> (Knowledge <s>Dharma</s>-Body)

children.text: itthaṃ prathamaṃ kāyaṃ nirdiśya dvitīyo niṣprapañcajñānātmako dharmakāyaḥ anāsravaḥ smṛtyupasthānādyātmaka iti tamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus explained the first body, the second <s>Dharmakāya</s>, being of the nature of non-elaborated knowledge, undefiled, and consisting of the applications of mindfulness and the rest—[the author] states it—
"The factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) in sequence,
the ninefold attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>), the totalities (<s>kṛtsna</s>) of ten kinds; (Abhis 8.2)
the bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>) of eight types in their divisions,
<s>araṇā</s> (non-hostility <s>samādhi</s>), aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); (Abhis 8.3)
the four purities in all aspects, the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>),
the ten powers (<s>bala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the non-guarding (<s>arakṣaṇa</s>); (Abhis 8.4)
the threefold application of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the threefold nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asaṃmoṣadharmatā</s>),

children.text: vāsanāyāḥ samuddhāto mahato karuṇā jane // Abhis_8.5 //
children.translated_text: the uprooting of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), and great compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) for beings; (Abhis 8.5)
the eighteen <s>dharmas</s> that are exclusively the Sage's own,
and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects)—these are called the <s>Dharmakāya</s>." (Abhis 8.6)

children.text: iti / smṛtyupasthānādyārabhya āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaparyantā bodhipakṣāḥ / pūrvavadapramāṇāni maitryādicaturbrahmavihārāḥ / adhyātmaṃ rūpyarūpī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatīti dvauḥ, śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopampadya viharatītyekaḥ, ākāśavijñānākiñcanyanaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanānīti catvāraḥ, saṃjñāveditanirodha ityekaḥ ityaṣṭau vimokṣāḥ / rūpadhātucaturdhyānāni caturārūpyasamāpattayo nirodhasamāpattiriti nava samāpattayaḥ / pṛthivyaptejovāyunīlapītalohitāvadātavijñānākāśamiti kṛtsnaṃ daśavidham / adhyātmarūpārūpasaṃjñinau pratyekaṃ parīttādhimātrākārābhyāṃ bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatastānyabhibhūya jānīta iti catuṣṭayam, adhyātmārūpasaṃjñī eva nīlapītalohitāvadātānabhibhūya paśyatīti catuṣṭayamityaṣṭavidhamabhibhvāyatanam / parasantānagatakleśaraṇaprabandhonmūlanāt samādhirityaraṇā / samyagapagatasarvanimittasaṅgavyāghātaṃ saṃśayāpanayanakāripraṇidhānasamṛddhyā āsaṃsāramasamāhitāvasthāyāṃ pravartata iti praṇidhijñānam, ṣaḍabhijñāścatasraśca pratisavidaḥ pūrvoktā āśrayālambanacittajñānapariśuddhaya iti catasraḥ śuddhayaḥ / āyuścittapariṣkārakarmopapattyadhimuktipraṇidhānarddhijñānadharmavaśitā iti daśa vaśitāḥ / pūrvoktāni daśa balāni, catvāri vaiśāradyāni ca / pariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥsamudācārastathāgataḥ, nāstyasya viparītasamudācāratā, yāṃ paraparijñānabhayāt pracchādayitavyāṃ manyeta ityarakṣaṇaṃ trividham / dharmadeśanāyāṃ śrotukāmāśrotukāmobhayakāmeṣu yathākramamanunayapratighobhayavivikta evopakṣekaḥ smṛtimān viharatīti smṛtyupasthānaṃ tridhā / sattvārthakriyākālānatikramalakṣaṇetyasaṃmoṣadharmatā / kleśajñeyāvaraṇānuśayarūpabījaprahāṇād vāsanāyāḥ samuddhātaḥ sakalajanahitāśayatā, mahatī karuṇā jane 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā sarvākārajñatā / 'ca' iti śabdena saṃgṛhītāḥ mārgajñatādayo 'pi prāguktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: The factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) are from the applications of mindfulness up to the noble eightfold path. The immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> of loving-kindness and the rest, as before. The liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) are eight: two—'having form internally, one sees forms externally' and 'formless internally, one sees forms externally'; one—'having directly realized the liberation of the beautiful, one abides having attained it with the body'; four—the spheres of infinite space, infinite consciousness, nothingness, and neither-perception-nor-non-perception; and one—the cessation of perception and feeling. The nine attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) are the four <s>dhyānas</s> of the form realm, the four formless attainments, and the cessation attainment. The tenfold totality (<s>kṛtsna</s>) is earth, water, fire, wind, blue, yellow, red, white, consciousness, and space. The eightfold base of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>) is: a set of four—one with form-perception and one with formless-perception internally, each seeing external forms in their limited and excellent aspects, mastering and knowing them; and a set of four—one with formless-perception internally alone, seeing blue, yellow, red, and white, mastering them. <s>Araṇā</s> (non-hostility <s>samādhi</s>) is the concentration that uproots the continuity of defilements in others' mind-streams that provoke hostility. Aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>) operates in the non-concentrated state throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>, through the fulfillment of aspirations that remove all doubt, completely free from all obstruction by signs—. The six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) are as previously stated. The four purities are of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>), object (<s>ālambana</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). The ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>) are mastery over lifespan, mind, requisites, <s>karma</s>, birth, aspiration, vow, miraculous powers, knowledge, and <s>dharma</s>. The ten powers (<s>bala</s>) and four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) are as previously stated. The threefold non-guarding (<s>arakṣaṇa</s>) is: the <s>Tathāgata</s> has purified conduct of body, speech, and mind; there is no mistaken conduct that he might think needs to be concealed for fear of others' knowledge. The threefold application of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) is: in teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, toward those who wish to listen, those who do not wish to listen, and both, respectively, free from approval, hostility, or both, one abides attentive, with mindfulness, as an onlooker. Non-forgetfulness (<s>asaṃmoṣadharmatā</s>) is characterized by not missing the time for accomplishing the welfare of beings. The uprooting of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) is through the abandonment of seeds in the form of the latent tendencies of the obscurations of defilements and knowables. The intention for the welfare of all people is great compassion toward beings. The eighteen exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), <s>mārgajñatā</s> and the rest as previously stated are also included.

children.text: sarve cāśrayaparāvṛttyā parāvṛttā bodhipakṣādayo niṣprapañcajñānātmakā dharmakāyo 'bhidhīyata iti kecit /
children.translated_text: Some say: All [these]—the factors of awakening and the rest, transformed through the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>)—being of the nature of non-elaborated knowledge, are called the <s>Dharmakāya</s>.
Others, however—

children.text: sarvākārāṃ viśuddhiṃ ye dharmāḥ prāptā nirāsravāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those undefiled <s>dharmas</s> that have attained complete purity in all aspects—
the <s>Svābhāvikakāya</s> of the Sage is characterized by their nature."

children.text: iti yathārutattvena lokottarānevānāsravān dharmānabhyupagamya teṣāṃ yāṃ prakṛtiranutpādatā tallakṣaṇaḥ svābhāvikaḥ kāyaḥ, sa eva ca dharmatākāyo dharmakāya iti bhāvapratyayalopād vyapadiśyata iti vyākhyāya, ke punaste 'nāsravā dharmā yeṣāṃ prakṛtilakṣaṇo dharmakāya ityāśaṅkya 'bodhipakṣāpramāṇānī' tyādikārikāmavatārayanti / teṣāṃ yogisaṃvṛtyā viśiṣṭārthapratibhāsajananadvāreṇāśrayaparāvṛttyā parāvṛttā dharmadeśanādyarthakriyākāriṇo 'vaśyamadvayāścittacaitāḥ kathamabhyupagantavyāḥ? saṅgṛhītā ityapare /
children.translated_text: —taking literally only the supramundane undefiled <s>dharmas</s>, explain that the <s>Svābhāvikakāya</s> is characterized by their nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), which is non-arising, and that this very [body] is called the <s>Dharmatākāya</s> or <s>Dharmakāya</s> through the elision of the possessive affix. Then, suspecting 'But what are those undefiled <s>dharmas</s> whose nature-characteristic is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>?'—they introduce the verse beginning 'The factors of awakening, the immeasurables.' Of those [<s>dharmas</s>], transformed through the transformation of the basis by means of generating the appearance of distinguished meaning through the <s>yogin</s>'s conventional [perception]—the mind and mental factors that perform the efficacious activity of teaching <s>dharma</s> and the rest must necessarily be non-dual. How are they to be accepted? Others say they are encompassed [in the <s>Dharmakāya</s>].
Some, in explaining the fourfold body, [cite]—
"The <s>Svābhāvika</s>, together with the <s>Sāmbhogika</s>, and likewise another, the <s>Nairmāṇika</s>,
and the <s>Dharmakāya</s> with its activity—the fourfold [body] is proclaimed."

children.text: itikārikāyāṃ svābhāvikaśabdānantaraṃ dharmakāyaśabdasyāpāṭhāt kāyatrayameveti / anye tūpadarśitaprayojanasāmarthyāt kārikābandhānurodhena jñānasyaiva kāritreṇa sambandhārthaṃ caivamuktam, ato 'viruddhaṃ sarvaṃ pradeśāntarābhihitaṃ kāyacatuṣṭayaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: In this verse, since the word '<s>Dharmakāya</s>' does not appear immediately after the word '<s>Svābhāvika</s>,' [they hold that] there are only three bodies. Others, however, [say that] through the force of the purpose indicated, in accordance with the verse composition, it is stated thus for the purpose of connecting activity with knowledge alone. Therefore, all is consistent, and the fourfold body as stated in other passages obtains.
To show the distinction of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>araṇā samādhi</s> from the <s>araṇā samādhi</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, [the author] says in one intervening verse—
"From the seeing of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>'s <s>araṇā</s>, there is the avoidance of human defilements;
for the cutting off of the stream of their defilements in villages and the rest—the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>araṇā</s>." (Abhis 8.7)

children.text: iti / mā 'smaddarśanāt kasyacit kleśotpattiḥ syāditi manuṣyakleśotpattiparihāritā śrāvakādyaraṇāsamādhiḥ / tathāgatānāṃ tu sakalajanakleśaprabandhonmūlanaṃ syāditi grāmādiṣu araṇāsamādhiviśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus: 'May no arising of defilements occur in anyone from seeing me'—the <s>araṇā samādhi</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others avoids the arising of human defilements. But for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, 'May the uprooting of the continuity of defilements of all people occur'—this is the distinction of the <s>araṇā samādhi</s> in villages and the rest.
To show the distinction of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s aspiration-knowledge from that of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, [the author] says in one intervening verse—
"Effortless, unattached, unobstructed, always abiding,
dispelling all questions—the <s>Buddha</s>'s aspiration-knowledge is accepted." (Abhis 8.8)

children.text: iti / nirnimittatvena svarasapravṛttam, vastvanabhiniveśād rūpādisaṅgavigatam, savāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt sarvajñeyāvyāghātam, āsaṃsāramavasthānāt sadā sthitam, samyak pratisaṃvillābhāt praśnavisarjanakāri tāthāgataṃ praṇidhijñānamitīṣṭam / śrāvakādīnāṃ viparītatvena naivam /
children.translated_text: Thus: Operating spontaneously through being free of signs; free from attachment to form and the rest through non-grasping of objects; unobstructed with respect to all knowables through the abandonment of the obscurations of defilements and knowables together with their latent impressions; always abiding through remaining throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>; performing the answering of questions through the attainment of correct analytical knowledge—such is the aspiration-knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as accepted. For <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, being the opposite, it is not so.

children.text: syādevaṃ nityaṃ mahākaruṇāmayadharmakāyāvasthāne kathaṃ (sakalaprāṇabhṛtāṃ) sadā nāthekriyeti? antaraślokena samādhānamāha -
children.translated_text: If it be so—that the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the nature of great compassion abides permanently—how is it that the welfare of all sentient beings is not always accomplished? [The author] resolves this in one intervening verse—

children.text: paripākaṃ gate hetau yasya yasya yadā yadā /
children.translated_text: "When the cause has ripened for whomsoever, at whatever time,

children.text: hitaṃ bhavati kartavyaṃ prathate tasya tasya saḥ // Abhis_8.9 //
children.translated_text: whatever benefit is to be accomplished—for that [being], that [<s>Dharmakāya</s>] manifests." (Abhis 8.9)

children.text: iti / kalyāṇamitrādisamavadhānād buddhādyālambane paripoṣaṃ gate hetau pūrvāvaropitakuśalamūlabīje sati, yasya sattvasya yasmin kāle dharmadeśanādikaṃ kriyamāṇamāyatipathyaṃ bhavati, tadā tasyārthakaraṇāya pūrvapraṇidhānasamṛddhyā tatpratibhāsānurūpeṇārthakriyākārī bhagavāniti (mahākaruṇāsvabhāvadharmakāyāvasthānena) sarvadā cintāmaṇirivopasthito 'pi svakarmāparādhajanitahetuvaidhuryānna phaladāyakaḥ pratibhāsata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the cause — the seed of wholesome roots previously planted — has been nourished through association with <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friends) and so forth, and has matured with respect to objects such as the <s>Buddha</s> and others, then for whatever being at whatever time the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> and so forth being performed becomes beneficial for the future, at that time, for the sake of benefiting that being, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, through the fulfillment of his prior <s>praṇidhāna</s> (aspiration), performs the activity corresponding to whatever appears to that being — this is the intended meaning. By abiding in the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body) whose nature is great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), he is always present like a wish-fulfilling gem, yet due to the deficiency of causes produced by one's own karmic faults, he does not appear as a bestower of results.
When the objection arises 'how is this so?', he states an illustration with the following intermediary verse:

children.text: varṣatyapi hi parjanye naiva bījaṃ prarohati /
children.translated_text: For even when the rain-cloud pours down, a seed does not sprout;
Even when <s>Buddha</s>s arise, one who is <s>abhavya</s> (incapable of liberation) does not obtain good fortune. (Abhis 8.10)

children.text: iti / yathā devarāje varṣatyapi sati pūtībhāvādinā abījībhūtaṃ bījaṃ tilādi na prādurbhavati, tadvad buddhānāṃ sakalamanorathaparipūraṇadakṣāṇāṃ samutpāde 'pi abhavyo na bhadraṃ saddharmaśravaṇādikaṃ prāpnotīti /
children.translated_text: Thus, just as even when the lord of gods sends rain, a seed such as sesame that has become incapable of germination due to putrefaction and the like does not come forth, similarly, even when <s>Buddha</s>s who are capable of fulfilling all wishes arise, one who is <s>abhavya</s> (incapable of liberation) does not obtain the good fortune of hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> and so forth.

children.text: kathaṃ jñānātmako dharmakāyaḥ pratiniyatayogisantānādhāravartī pratikṣaṇamutpadyamāno vyāpo nitya iti kathyata iti ced? antaraślokenāha -
children.translated_text: If one asks: how can the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body), which is of the nature of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), which abides in the continua of specific <s>yogin</s>s, and which arises at every moment, be called pervasive and permanent? He states with the following intermediary verse:
Thus, due to the extensiveness of his activity, the <s>Buddha</s> is declared to be pervasive;

children.text: akṣayatvācca tasyaiva nitya ityapi kathyate // Abhis_8.11 //
children.translated_text: And because of the very inexhaustibility of that, he is also called permanent. (Abhis 8.11)

children.text: iti / yathoktanyāyenaivaṃ sarvatra pratibhāsadvāreṇārthakriyākaraṇavaipulyāt prabandhatayā āsaṃsāramavasthānena ca bhagavataḥ kṣayābhāvād yathākramaṃ buddho vyāpī nitya ityabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner stated, because of the extensiveness of performing beneficial activity everywhere through the medium of appearances, and because of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s absence of exhaustion through abiding as a continuum until the end of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> is called pervasive and permanent, respectively.
3 - <s>Sambhogakāya</s> (Enjoyment Body)

children.text: kāyadvayamevaṃ nirdiśya lakṣaṇānuvyañjanavirājitaḥ sāmbhogikaḥ rūpakāyasvabhāvastṛtīyaḥ / tamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus explained the two bodies, the third is the <s>Sāmbhogika</s> (enjoyment) <s>Rūpakāya</s> (form body), resplendent with <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks) and <s>anuvyañjana</s>s (minor marks). He states this:
This body of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage), consisting of the thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks) and eighty <s>vyañjana</s>s (minor marks),
Is considered the <s>Sāmbhogika</s> (enjoyment) body, because of the enjoyment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). (Abhis 8.12)

children.text: iti / dvātriṃśallakṣaṇāśītyanuvyañjanātmako 'yaṃ daśabhūmipraviṣṭamahābodhisattvaiḥ paramānavadyamahāyānadharmasaṃbhogaprītisukhopabhogāt buddhasya bhagavataḥ sāmbhogikakāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, this body consisting of the thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks) and eighty <s>anuvyañjana</s>s (minor marks) is the <s>Sāmbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body) of the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, because great <s>Bodhisattva</s>s who have entered the ten <s>bhūmi</s>s (stages) enjoy the bliss and happiness of partaking of the supremely blameless <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>.
If one asks: what are those thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks)? He states with five intermediary verses:
His hands bear the mark of a wheel; his soles are like a tortoise in their steadiness; his fingers and toes of hands and feet are webbed;

children.text: karau sapādau taruṇau mṛdū ca samutsadaiḥ saptabhirāśrayo 'sya // Abhis_8.13 //
children.translated_text: His hands and feet are soft and youthful, and his body has seven prominent features. (Abhis 8.13)
He has long fingers; his body is tall and straight with elongated heels; his feet have raised arches and his body hair grows upward;
He has shanks like an <s>eṇeya</s> (antelope); his thighs and arms are well-rounded; his private parts are enclosed in a sheath. (Abhis 8.14)
He is golden in color with fine skin, and each hair curls to the right;

children.text: ūrṇāṅkitāsyo haripūrvakāyaḥ skandhau vṛtāvasya citāntarāṃsaḥ // Abhis_8.15 //
children.translated_text: His face is adorned with the <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-curl); his upper body is like a lion's; his shoulders are rounded and his torso is broad between the shoulders. (Abhis 8.15)
The inferior among tastes is absent, and the supreme taste manifests for him; his body is symmetrical like a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree;
He has the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) on his head; his tongue is broad and beautiful; his voice is like <s>Brahmā</s>'s; his jaw is like a lion's; his teeth are bright white. (Abhis 8.16)
His teeth are even in size and without gaps, and the sets of teeth number four tens — not more, not less;

children.text: nīlekṣaṇo govṛṣapakṣmanetro dvātriṃśadetāni hi lakṣaṇāni // Abhis_8.17//
children.translated_text: His eyes are deep blue; his eyelashes are like those of a bull — these are the thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks). (Abhis 8.17)
Thus: (1) Through following after teachers by going to meet them and the like, there is the mark of wheel-signs on hands and feet.

children.text:
(2) dṛḍhasaṃvarasamādānatvāt kūrmavat supratiṣṭhitapādatā /
(3) catuḥsaṃgrahavastusevanād rājahaṃsavat jālāvanaddhāṅgulipāṇipādatā /
(4) praṇītakhādyabhojyādidānād mṛdutaruṇahastapādatā /
(5) praṇītataralehyādidānena samucchritahastapādaskandhagrīvāpradeśatvāt saptocchrayatā /
(6) vadhyamokṣaṇatvād dīrghāṅgulitā /
(7) jīvitānugrahaṇād āyatapārṣṇitā /
(8) prāṇātipātaviratyā bṛhadṛjugātratā /
(9) kuśaladharmasamādānād ucchaṅkhapādatā /
(1)) gṛhītakuśalasamādānavardhanāt ūrdhvagaromatā /
(11) satkṛtya vidyāśilpādidānād eṇeyajaṅghatā /
(12) saṃvidyamānārthayācanakajanāpratyākhyānāt paṭūrūbāhutā /
(13) sarvajanabrahmacaryasamādāpanaguhyamantrārakṣaṇāt kośagatabastiguhyatā /
(14) praṇītopāstaraṇadānāt suvarṇavarṇatā /
(15) prāsādādivaradānāt ślakṣṇacchavitā /
(16) saṅgaṇikādiparivarjanāt pradakṣiṇāvartaikaikaromatā /
(17) sarvagurujanayathāsthānaniveśanād ūrṇāṅkitamukhatā /
(18) sarvathā mukharavacanānavasādanāt siṃhapūrvārddhakāyatā /
(19) priyavāditvasubhāṣitānulomatvāt susaṃvṛtaskandhatā /
(20) bhaiṣajyādidānāt citāntarāṃsatā /
(21) glānajanopasthānād rasarasāgratā /
(22) vanārāmādikaraṇasamādāpanāt nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalatā /
(23) vihārādyabhyadhikapradānāduṣṇīṣaśiraskatā /
(24) ślakṣṇādivacanāt prabhūtajihvatā /
(25) sarvalokadhātusattvasaddharmavijñapanād brahmasvaratā /
(26) sambhinnapralāpaviratyā siṃhahanutā /
(27) sarvajanasammānādinā śukladantatā /
(28) viśuddhājīvatvāt samadantatā /
(29) satyavacanasamudācārād aviraladantatā /
(30) piśunavacanānabhyāsāt samacatvāriṃśaddantatā /
(31) sarvasattvaikaputradarśanād abhinīlanetratā /
(32) pratighātādivivekadarśanād gopakṣmanetratā /
children.translated_text:
(2) Through firmly undertaking <s>saṃvara</s> (moral restraint), there is the mark of feet well-established like a tortoise.
(3) Through practicing the four <s>saṃgrahavastu</s>s (means of gathering disciples), there is the mark of webbed fingers and toes on hands and feet like a royal goose.
(4) Through giving refined food, drink, and the like, there is the mark of soft and youthful hands and feet.
(5) Through giving refined sweets, confections, and the like, the areas of hands, feet, shoulders, and neck being elevated, there is the mark of seven prominences.
(6) Through liberating those condemned to death, there is the mark of long fingers.
(7) Through granting the gift of life, there is the mark of elongated heels.
(8) Through abstaining from taking life, there is the mark of a large and upright body.
(9) Through undertaking wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, there is the mark of feet with raised arches.
(10) Through maintaining and increasing the undertaking of wholesome practices, there is the mark of upward-growing body hair.
(11) Through respectfully giving instruction in knowledge, crafts, and the like, there is the mark of shanks like an <s>eṇeya</s> (antelope).
(12) Through not refusing those who come seeking what one possesses, there is the mark of well-rounded thighs and arms.
(13) Through establishing all people in <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and protecting secret <s>mantra</s>s, there is the mark of private parts enclosed in a sheath.
(14) Through giving refined bedding and seats, there is the mark of golden color.
(15) Through giving excellent mansions and the like, there is the mark of smooth skin.
(16) Through avoiding gatherings and the like, there is the mark of each hair curling to the right.
(17) Through establishing all venerable persons in their proper places, there is the mark of the <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-curl) adorning the face.
(18) Through never disparaging the speech of anyone at all, there is the mark of an upper body like a lion.
(19) Through speaking pleasantly and conforming to good speech, there is the mark of well-covered shoulders.
(20) Through giving medicine and the like, there is the mark of a broad torso between the shoulders.
(21) Through attending to the sick, there is the mark of supremacy among tastes.
(22) Through establishing others in the creation of parks and groves, there is the mark of a body symmetrical like a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan tree).
(23) Through giving excellent <s>vihāra</s>s (monasteries) and the like, there is the mark of the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) on the head.
(24) Through smooth and gentle speech, there is the mark of a broad tongue.
(25) Through proclaiming the true <s>Dharma</s> to beings in all world-realms, there is the mark of the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>.
(26) Through abstaining from divisive speech, there is the mark of a jaw like a lion.
(27) Through honoring all people, there is the mark of white teeth.
(28) Through pure livelihood, there is the mark of even teeth.
(29) Through the practice of truthful speech, there is the mark of teeth without gaps.
(30) Through not habituating to slanderous speech, there is the mark of a full set of forty teeth.
(31) Through regarding all beings as one's only child, there is the mark of deep blue eyes.
(32) Through contemplating the separation from hostile reactions and the like, there is the mark of eyelashes like those of a bull.
He states with an intermediary verse that through the accomplishment of causes, the marks are accomplished:
Whatever cause here is the accomplisher of whatever mark,
The fulfillment of each such cause is the characteristic of its attainment. (Abhis 8.18)

children.text: iti / yeṣāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ ye prasādhakāḥ, tān prapūrya tāni dvātriṃśallakṣaṇāni prādurbhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus, by fulfilling those causes that are the accomplishers of those marks, those thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks) come into manifestation.
If one asks: what are the causes of those? He states with two intermediary verses:
Following after teachers and so forth; firmness with regard to <s>saṃvara</s> (moral restraint);

children.text: saṅgrahāsevanaṃ dānaṃ praṇītasya ca vastunaḥ // Abhis_8.19 //
children.translated_text: Practicing the <s>saṃgraha</s>s (means of gathering); and giving of refined things; (Abhis 8.19)
Liberating those condemned to death; and the increase of what is wholesome;
These and so forth, according to the <s>sūtra</s>s, are the causes that accomplish the marks. (Abhis 8.20)

children.text: iti / ime dve kārike uparyeva lakṣaṇavyākhyānāvasare sphuṭite, ato na punaḥ vistīryeta iti /
children.translated_text: Thus, these two verses have already been made clear above in the context of explaining the marks, therefore they need not be elaborated upon again.
Having thus explained the <s>lakṣaṇa</s>s (major marks), he states the eighty <s>anuvyañjana</s>s (minor marks) with twelve intermediary verses:

children.text: tāmrāḥ snigdhāśca tuṅgāśca nakhā aṃgulayo muneḥ /
children.translated_text: The nails of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) are copper-colored, glossy, and raised;
His fingers are rounded, tapering gradually, with veins that are hidden and free from knots. (Abhis 8.21)
His ankles are hidden; his feet are even; his gait is like that of a lion, an elephant, a bull, and a lord of geese;
His stride is dignified, his walking is graceful, and his body is straight and rounded. (Abhis 8.22)
